chapters.title: Chapter 5730: A Glorious Dream! II
paragraphs: The Primordial Paradox raised his hands, and where he stood the fight bent, two things true at once. Noah pushed his old Infinity into the man’s dream of catching the impossible whole, and the contradiction around him got deeper!
Dark soldiers who struck at him found they had both struck and not struck, couldn’t settle which, and stood there with their weapons out while the fight went past them.
Descartes and Erwin held the side as he helped them the only other way he had.
He reached across the folds, into the storage of his own Realm, and drew out the thing he’d carried since Vasileia burned.

The skeleton of a Provenance Lifeform. Aurelius’s gift, the dim golden bones from the sacred spring, the ones Descartes had asked him for before they parted. A corpse of a Provenance Lifeform, no reason given.

Noah didn’t know what Descartes wanted it for. He didn’t need to. Through the dream, spending his own Provenance this time instead of his Infinity, he set the golden skeleton down beside the man in the middle of the fight, quiet, unremarked, a thing that was suddenly there where nothing had been.
|Provenance spent to manifest a requested object into the dreamed narrative.|
|-5 PROVENANCE ESSENCE.|
Descartes’ hand closed on the bones like he’d been waiting for them, and something on his side changed that Noah didn’t fully follow.

Descartes had asked for a dead Provenance Lifeform and given no reason, and a man who dreamed of turning the world back into a thing of the mind didn’t ask for corpses idly. Whatever the bones were to him, they were part of an argument he was building, and Noah had just handed him the piece!
Noah was learning bit by bit.

What mattered the most was...placement. The Immense Ones ruled by pressing down, laying their frames over the folds and making everything climb inside. Noah was doing the opposite thing from the same height.

He wasn’t making anyone bigger than their dream. He was letting each of them be exactly as big as their dream already said they were, and clearing the small things in the way. Quiet work. It left no marks!
And it grew his own Provenance while he did it, because for THE Human Dreamer, helping a dream come true was the same act as dreaming.
|Provenance rises as you shepherd the dreams of others toward their fullness.|
|+6 PROVENANCE ESSENCE.|
|THE OVERSEEING ONE frowns.|
|His heroes are not dying on schedule.|
The fight turned, slow, the way Noah had pushed it. The Peacemaker’s shots cut deeper than they should. The Primordial Paradox held a stretch of ground that should have folded.
Eckert’s quiet unity had gone into a third of the dark army with not one purple eye to show for it. And whatever Descartes had done with the bones was holding the side that should have broken first.

None of it looked like help from outside. That was the point! Each hero was just doing what his dream said he could do, a little more than he should have managed, and no eye looking down would find a hand behind any of it. They were rising. That was all. Heroes rose!
But the Dark Lord didn’t fall.

He stood at the center and let the fight come to him, and where his power touched, the heroes’ new strength just stopped being strength. The Peacemaker’s deeper shots hit his shadow and came apart into nothing.

The Primordial Paradox’s held ground met the shadow and stopped being held. Even Eckert’s crept unity, reaching at last for the middle, thinned as it got near him, because you can’t turn a mind on a thing whose ground has been pulled out from under it.
The heroes rose, and the Dark Lord ate what they rose with, and the fight ground toward a wall.
|THE OVERSEEING ONE senses another gaze upon his narrative.|
HUUM!
Noah went still inside the dream.
|THE OVERSEEING ONE assumes a peer has come to watch.|
|He is embarrassed.|
That was the thing Noah had counted on and hadn’t been sure of!

The Overseeing One couldn’t see him for what he was. He saw a watcher, and took it for one of his own kind, another Immense One drifting past to look in on the story he’d staged. And the one he’d backed to win was struggling in front of company.
|THE OVERSEEING ONE will not be seen to author a narrative that falters.|
|He lends the Dark Lord his backing.|

Power came down out of the sky into the middle of the dark army, and the Dark Lord swelled with it. His shadow spread wider, faster, hungrier, eating the ground the heroes had won back in big swallows.
The Peacemaker’s road closed. The Primordial Paradox’s ground folded. Eckert’s unity got shoved back to the edges and pinned there!
He’d done it to save face in front of a peer who wasn’t there. And it was working.

Noah watched his quiet work come undone and didn’t panic. He’d known it could happen. He fed the three old threads a little harder, patient, keeping the heroes on their feet instead of pushing them ahead. He’d never been trying to win the Overseeing One’s story. He’d come to see it, to keep the people in it alive, and to learn who the Dark Lord was.
And the Dark Lord, swollen with a borrowed eye’s power, did a thing the Overseeing One hadn’t written for him.
He turned his back on the heroes.
He looked up. At the sky, at the thing pressing down on all of them, and when he spoke his voice came up out of the whole dark army at once!
"I didn’t ask for your power," he said. "I didn’t ask for the part, or the enemies, or the ending you drew for all of us."
WAA!
Eckert’s unity crept to the edge of his shadow and stopped, and he let it. Didn’t strike it down. Didn’t even look at it like a threat!
"These aren’t my enemies," he said, still looking up. "You made them my enemies. You made me their Dark Lord. You sit up there and move us around and call it a story."
The shadow drew in close around him, and for the first time it didn’t look like a weapon. It looked like a man who’d decided not to move!
"I mind your hand in my life more than I mind losing to these four. A lot more. Take your power back. I never wanted it."
|THE OVERSEEING ONE is silent.|
|THE OVERSEEING ONE decides this narrative is no longer worth the watching of peers.|
|He withdraws his backing.|
|"A defiant tool is a broken tool. Enjoy your death, all of you."|
The power went out of the Dark Lord all at once, and the gaze lifted off the Cabin, and THE Overseeing One pulled his attention back like a hand off a board!
The story didn’t end as it just lost the man who was writing it.
Noah’s eye held over the Cabin and didn’t blink.
Not my enemies, the Dark Lord had said!
Noah had heard him!

chapters.title: Chapter 5731: A Glorious Dream! III
paragraphs: The story didn’t end when THE OVERSEEING ONE left, it was only made...free.

Noah watched from above, unblinking, as the Dark Lord straightened in the middle of his shadow and felt the sky go empty over him. No more gaze pressing down. No more hand moving the pieces. And instead of relief, the thing let out something that in a smaller creature would have been a laugh!

He’d been holding back. That was the part none of the heroes had understood. The whole time the Overseeing One watched, the Dark Lord had fought the way the story asked him to fight, a wall, a thing that stood and took and gave nothing. He hadn’t been trying to win. He’d been trying to be left alone, and standing still was the closest a chess piece got to that.
Now no one was watching. Well, or so he thought, so he stopped standing still.

The shadow came off him all at once as it dropped over the whole floor of the Cabin like a lid closing on a jar, and everywhere it touched, Exietence stopped meaning anything. This was his real power, the thing the Overseeing One had leashed to a role, and it was worse than nullifying strength!
It nullified everything.

The Peacemaker loosed a shot filled with Causes and the arrow simply forgot it was an arrow halfway to him. The Primordial Paradox held two states at once and the shadow reached them and neither state was true anymore, neither false, just gone.
Descartes’ philosophy and wonder, whatever he’d built with the golden bones, met the falling dark and lost the argument it had been making, its logic pulled out from under it mid-sentence!
HUUM!

Noah felt the fight tip. The heroes had been rising while the eye held them to a story. Now the story was off, and there was nothing above them anymore, and there was nothing holding the Dark Lord to a shape!

He could not be beaten. That was simply true. A thing that unmade meaning could not be out-argued, out-shot, or out-thought, because argument and arrow and thought all stopped being what they were the moment they came near him. The heroes were going to lose, and this time there was no author to complain to about it!
Except for one thing the Dark Lord had missed.
Eckert.

Back when the eye still watched, Eckert’s unity had crept quiet through the dark ranks, mind to mind, and reached at last for the center. The Dark Lord had felt it come and nullified it, the way he nullified everything, and it should have thinned and died at the edge of his shadow like all the rest.
It hadn’t.

Noah had held it there. A single thread of his old Infinity, fed patient into Eckert’s easy dream, keeping the unity bound to the Dark Lord’s edge even as the shadow tried to unmake it. It had been a small thing, unnoticed, a splinter under a fingernail while the giant fought with both hands. Now the giant had turned all his weight on the heroes, and the splinter was still there, and Noah pressed on it.

’This man does not wish to be a chess piece,’Noah sent, down the old thread, into the mind wearing Abbadon’s stolen body. ’Erase everything about his will, entirely, and let him rest. Then you can use him. He will be your sharpest weapon yet.’
For a moment nothing answered.
Then Eckert’s unity, held to the Dark Lord’s edge by a hand it hadn’t known was there, stopped creeping and started to bite.
BOOM!

The shadow flinched. For the first time since the Overseeing One left, the falling dark that unmade everything it touched met a thing it could not unmake, because the unity wasn’t power and it wasn’t meaning. It was a decision, one mind spreading into many, and Noah’s Infinity had welded it to the one place the Dark Lord’s authority couldn’t clear it off.
A voice came back up the old thread, dry and amused.
’I thought it might be you, when things started to go crazy down here,’ Eckert said, in the quiet where only Noah’s Infinity could hear. ’The little pushes. Too neat to be luck.’

Something in the tone almost smiled. ’I’d like to catch up. Talk. It’s been a while, and I have questions. But not now. Let me focus on eating this monstrous Dimensionality of his and doing what you asked. This is going to take everything I have.’
The unity dug in!
Noah watched from above, and he thought about dreams.

He was giving the Dark Lord his. The Dark Lord had dreamed of not being a piece in another man’s game, of a domain that was his, of never again having a hand reach down and write his ending. And Noah was about to make it true. No more author. No more role. No more being moved!
He was going to erase the will that had wanted all of that, and let the being rest, and use the shell.

A dream could come true, Noah thought, and not come true the way the dreamer had hoped.The Dark Lord would get exactly what he asked for. He would never be a chess piece again. He would simply stop being anyone who could be played, which was, in the end, the only way a being like this ever got free.

He wondered if that counted. Whether a dream that arrived sideways like this was still a dream, or whether it turned, somewhere in the crossing, into a nightmare. He didn’t have an answer. He wasn’t sure the difference mattered to the one who got to rest!
Prompts bloomed quiet across the eye.
|You have guided the dreams of five existences toward their fullness within a Narrative of Existence.|
|THE Human Dreamer grows for shepherding what others could not reach alone.|
|+14 PROVENANCE ESSENCE.|
|A dream has been fulfilled by your hand, though not as the dreamer imagined it. The Human Dream deepens on the fulfillment and on the cost.|
|A new understanding settles: THE FULFILLED DREAM AND ITS SHADOW. You perceive, now, the gap between a dream as wished and a dream as granted.|
Noah let the prompts fade.
On the floor of the Cabin, the heroes felt the fight change under them and did not understand why.

The Peacemaker lowered his bow. His shots had been dying against the shadow, and then, all at once, the shadow stopped coming for him. He looked at the Dark Lord, who had turned his whole weight away from the heroes and toward some struggle at his own center, and then the Peacemaker did a thing he had not done in the whole battle.
He looked up.

He looked at the empty sky over the Cabin, at the place where the pressing gaze had been, and something in him went still and wary. He had felt the eye leave. He had felt the fight turn the moment it left, and turn again just now, and both turns had come from nowhere he could point to. For half a breath he almost believed there was still something up there. Another watcher. A hand he couldn’t see!
Maybe even someone he knew very well!
He looked back down.
Beside him, Descartes had done the same. A glance up, a flat unreadable moment, a look back down at the golden bones in his hand. He said nothing.
The Primordial Paradox and Erwin held their ground and watched the center, where the real fight had gone.
The Dark Lord was losing, and he did not know to whom.

His shadow, which unmade everything, could not unmake the thing spreading through him. He tore at it and it held. He nullified it and it was still there, because you cannot nullify a choice the way you nullify a force!

Eckert’s unity climbed through the monstrous Dimensionality one thread at a time, backed by Noah’s terrifying power, and every thread it took, it turned, and every turn was one more piece of the giant’s own power now answering to the mind in Abbadon’s body.
The Dark Lord fought hard, then harder, then not at all.
And somewhere in the fight, Noah thought, the will got what it wanted. No more hand in the sky. No more being moved. Just the long quiet of a thing finally, completely, left alone!
The struggling stopped.

The shadow, which had fallen over the whole Cabin like a lid, went still, and then it did not lift, but it changed hands. It stopped being the Dark Lord’s and started being Eckert’s, all that nullifying weight now bound under one idle, patient mind.
BOOM!
The Dark Lord sank to one knee.

He knelt, and behind him, across the whole floor of the Cabin, his dark army knelt with him, rank after rank of shadow folding down toward the being who now held their master’s power, the mind wearing Abbadon’s stolen body at the center of it all.

Eckert stood among them, idle as ever, having lifted no hand for any of it, a tired thing that had wanted only to sit still and grow stronger without effort. And here, without effort, he had grown by an entire army and the monstrous power of the being that led it.
His dream, too, coming true!
Above the Cabin, Noah’s blue-gold eye held over the kneeling ranks, patient, unnoticed, and did not blink.
One dream ended so another could rest. He wasn’t sure it was mercy. He wasn’t sure it wasn’t.
He let the dream carry him back up, out of this particular Narrative and story, into a unique space in this Infinite Dream he had initiated at the cost of 75 Provenance Essence.
He did not want to show himself before Eckert and all others as he didn’t want his brightness and his Dream to overshadow theirs!
Just like him, they were their own individual existence in their own grand journeys.
He did, however, want to talk to an old friend as among all those down there, the monster spreading unity was his closest.
So he tugged on his weavings to bring him to that unique space of his Infinite Dream where he could decide where to take his gaze next!

One dream ended so another could rest.
He wasn’t sure it was mercy.
He wasn’t sure it wasn’t.
He let the dream carry him back up, out of this particular Narrative and story, into a unique space in this Infinite Dream he had initiated at the cost of 75 Provenance Essence.
He did not want to show himself before Eckert and all others as he didn’t want his brightness and his Dream to overshadow theirs!
Just like him, they were their own individual existence in their own grand journeys.
He did, however, want to talk to an old friend as among all those down there, the monster spreading unity was his closest.
So he tugged on his weavings to bring him to that unique space of his Infinite Dream where he could decide where to take his gaze next!

chapters.title: Chapter 5732: That Uncrossable Line!
paragraphs: <A Record Lost In Shattered Scales>
An unknown number of years ago, they brought Vakochev to a grandmother half-dead.
The grandmother had no name that mattered to the grand powers and no Provenance worth their notice, only a small warm house at the quiet edge of a dying Observable Existence and a very long memory.
She had known the maker of the Scales since before he was grand, back when he was only a stubborn boy in a tribe near a mountain- when she called him Tokoloshe.

And so when they laid the ruined thing that had been Vakochev across her table and left, leaking Causes and Dimensionality from a hundred wounds that should each have killed him, she was not surprised.
She put water on to boil. She had mended him before. She would likely mend him again, if he was foolish enough to keep living the way he lived.

He had gone against The Vheldrani.A Provenance Lineage older than most laws, a bloodline so deep and so terrible it had pushed two of its own children up past the threshold and out into the Dimensional Skies.
Two Immense Ones grown from a single tree, and the tree still standing, still proud, still certain that a thing which had birthed two of the Immense was a thing that answered to no one.
Vakochev had walked up to that tree and put his fist through it anyway.
For his trouble he had most of his existence hanging out of him, and he lay on her table while she worked and did not complain.
He had learned long ago that she had no patience for the complaints of people who had chosen their own wounds.
"Why," she said, when the bleeding had slowed.

She seemed...tired, like someone who has asked a beloved fool the same question across an Age. "Two of that Lineage sit in a place we cannot see. You knew it before you went. You knew what backed them. And you went anyway. So...why?"
He was quiet for a while. She thought he had passed out.
Then he replied.

"There is a practice in their lesser holdings. In the small Observable Existences they own but do not bother to rule, where the lives are short and the Causes are thin. When one of the Vheldrani children nears the threshold, when it is close to becoming what its parents already are, it needs to be fed. Not food but...Foundation. So they go down into one of those small holdings, and they take the newborns. The very newest. The ones a day into breathing, before a life has had time to become a life, because a Cause that has not yet been spent is the purest thing there is to eat."
The grandmother’s hands did not stop moving over his wounds, but they slowed.

"They harvest them," Vakochev said. "They empty a whole Observable Existence of its first breaths and they render them down into a broth of unspent beginnings, and they feed it to a child of their bloodline so that child can climb a little faster. The parents who wake to find every cradle in their world gone cold on the same morning are told nothing, because you do not explain rules to peasants. I saw the cradles. I counted them until I could not count anymore, and then I went and found the tree that ate them."
"And that is your business how?" she said, though her voice had changed. "You did not know those infants. You never could have. They are gone now, every last one, regardless of anything you did."
"They are,"he agreed.

"Then you nearly died for nothing. For strangers. For ash. Against a Lineage that could unmake you between two breaths and felt nothing while doing it, because they are so far above you that your dying is nothing to them."She wrung the cloth out ths was bloody red in color.

"The Vheldrani do not believe your right and wrong apply to them. By every measure that exists, they are correct. A being that high is not judged by the rules of the low. Nothing judges them. There is no one left up there to do it."
"I know,"Vakochev said.
"Then why?"
And he turned his head on her table, and he looked at the old woman who had mended him more times than either of them could count.

"Because a rule that only binds the weak is not a rule,"he said. "It is a leash. They tell the low that right and wrong are real, and they build their whole order on the low believing it, and then they step over the line themselves whenever it suits them. They want the leash on everyone below and no collar on themselves. And the moment I decide their height excuses them, I have agreed with them. I have said the line is real for me and not for them. I have put on the collar and handed them the leash myself."
He breathed heavily!
He was quiet a moment, and when he went on.

"They think it ends when the cradles go cold. They took the first breaths, they fed the broth to their child, and they walked away certain the thing was closed. The small ones are ash, and ash forgets, so the account is settled."
His ruined hand closed slowly on the edge of her table.

"It does not end. Those parents will say the names of their children when this holding has rotted down to dust. They will say them when the star that lit their world has gone dark and cold. And when the last light anywhere in existence gutters out, when there is no one left in all of creation to hear it, some small ruined thing will still be floating alone in the black, saying a name into the dark that took everything, and the Vheldrani will have forgotten an Age ago that a name was ever theirs to take."

"That is what they actually did, Grandmother. Not a killing. A killing ends. They opened a wound with no bottom, one that keeps being inflicted long after everyone who inflicted it has gone home to eat. And they will never feel the weight of it, because the whole of their order is built so that the ones on top never have to."
He breathed gloriously!

"They are not above right and wrong. Nobody is. They are just tall enough that no one has told them no. So I told them no. That is all I did. I told two of the Immense no, out loud, with my fist, and they will remember for the rest of their long lives that a thing beneath them said it."
WAA!
The grandmother said nothing for a long moment.
Then she went and took the water off the boil, because it was ready, and she made him tea he was in no condition to drink!
"You will die of this someday," she said.
"I know," said THE Maker of the Scales.

"Good," she said as she smiled with quintessential pride. "If ever it happens, just know that I...am endlessly proud of you. And as always...Persevere. In the face of the impossible, Persevere. In the face of the unthinkable, Persevere!"

chapters.title: Chapter 5733: An Idle Existence!
paragraphs: The space where the dream lived was a strange one, and Noah was still learning what it could do.

It was not the sandy-gold storm his body had floated in, and it was not the Cabin he had watched from above. It sat between them. A room made of nowhere, held open by his own Provenance, where he could pull his attention out of one story and hold it still before deciding where to send it next.
Versatile, was the word he kept landing on. It did more than he had asked it to!
Seventy-five Provenance to open the Infinite Dream, and it had been a heavy price. He did not regret it, but he felt the size of what he had spent!

He did not know much about the Provenances the other First Lifeforms carried. There had never been anyone to ask. He had the one he shared with Thalia, the two of them holding a single grand thing between them, and there was the strange separate one her father wore, and beyond that, the record was thin as he didn’t do much research for others.
But he suspected, looking at what his own could do, that his was one of the grandest ones! Of course, this could be his own hubris.
He was only human, so he could be prideful! Superbius and Humilitas ran through him all at once!

But his Provenance did all this. It let him hide his own existence from the highest watchers in existence, borrow the rulings the Immense Ones had strung across everything, and dream himself into their exact seat, a gaze over a story, present and unseen.

That was not a small thing. Standing here in the room made of nowhere, looking at the plain human body he had shaped for himself in the space between spaces, he understood that it was closer to terrifying than he usually let himself think.
Then, a few feet from him, the air folded and a second body stepped out of it.
Eckert.

He came through looking like a handsome king who had misplaced his kingdom and did not much mind. Dark hair, a face built for easy confidence, and eyes that would not settle on a color. Blue, and then not blue, then something warmer, then something colder, changing from one blink to the next, as if the man behind them was one thing in this instant and a different thing in the next and had made peace with being both.
He saw Noah’s blue-gold body across the empty room, and he did not bow, and he did not posture. He crossed the space and wrapped Noah in a hug.
Noah blinked.
Then he brought up his arms and returned it!
Eckert pulled back and held him by the shoulders, looking him over, smiling!

"Why so surprised,"he said."It has been weeks for me. A little more, maybe. And you are the strangest thing I have been near for the longest stretch of my whole existence, all the way back to when the two of us barely had a spark to our names."
"From Primordials in The Primordial Cosmos...we have come far. The us of this moment can look at our past selves running through Cosmos as mere ants we can crush with a shred of thought..."
His changing eyes were fond.

"Growing apart from you was a curve I had to learn. There were plenty of times I wanted to call out for help. I would get to the edge of it, right to the edge, and then I would stop myself and think, there was a time before Osmont existed at all. When people hit a wall, or fell into trouble, back before there was a you to call, did they all just sit there waiting for someone who had not been born yet?"
He shrugged. "No. They got through it. So I persevered. And here we are."
Noah looked at him, and he couldn’t help the smile.
Two thrones bloomed out of the dream behind them, blue and gold, and the two of them sat.
"You got past all of it, though," Noah said. "And you climbed at a strange pace. You almost kept up with me."

"Hah. Almost?"Eckert leaned back into the throne. "You don’t have to soften it, big guy. I made my peace with that a long, long time ago. Existence is full of wonders and full of monsters, and I stopped measuring myself against you before I even understood what you were. Anyone who measures himself against you tends to dig an early grave out of his own thoughts and climb in."

He waved a hand. "No. I climbed as fast as I climbed, on my own, and it is more than fine that I am nowhere near you. Existence is vast. Maybe there is a timeline somewhere where one of us sits out ahead of you. Who knows."

His eyes changed color again as if amused. "Maybe in every timeline your Infinity just wins. Doesn’t matter. What matters to me is living true to what I am. I found that lining myself up with existence, with the actual shape of me, threw my unity wide open. And the shape of me has always been, and is idle. I am...an Idle Existence."
He said it grandly, and then he said it like it meant something!
"I am. I AM."
HUUM!
The dream buzzed around them, waves of it stirring at the words, and prompts opened quiet across Noah’s sight.
|You are gazing upon an existence that carries a unique Trueness, one you helped forge.|
|Your own PROVENANCE and VERITAS rise by 1.|
Noah shook his head slowly, and he almost laughed.
"Just how idle have you been?"
"I went back to my roots." Eckert spread his hands like a man showing off a garden he had let grow wild on purpose.

"Every Observable Existence I spread my unity into, every Dimension, I lay down my Idle System over it. And then the Causes that hold that place together, the ones that make it what it is, they have to feed me. Idle Loot, dripping back up the line into me. Into my existence. My Trueness. My weight."

His grin widened. "So I worked it out. If I seed myself across enough of existence, across enough different points in time, I can be a thing that sits in the dark weavings of it all and does absolutely nothing. Nothing at all. And every nanosecond that passes, without me lifting a single finger, I get grander. And grander. And grander still!"
WAA!
He spread his arms in the throne, delighted with himself.
"Now what," he said, "is that if not a dream come true."
BOOM!
His trueness rang out and the dream shivered with it, the whole space between spaces buzzing like a struck bell, and Noah found himself pulled all the way into the conversation, leaning in!
So he stretched the moment out. Long, and then longer, out toward the edge of infinity, and held it there!
He was doing something he almost never let himself do.
He was simply talking to a friend!

chapters.title: Chapter 5734: Boundless Dreams!
paragraphs: While one of him sat on a throne in a dream and talked to an old friend, another of him was at work!
This body sat on golden sand, on a shore inside THE Infiniverse. An endless sea ran out from it in slow blue-gold swells, and behind him lay island farmland so quiet and so full!
He thought about his people while he worked.
His children. His mother. The Queens. The ones who had walked beside him across his journey. The Emperor Penguin, Erikson, Titano, Ul’moreth, Kazuhiko, all the rest.
They were technically safe in THE Infiniverse all this time.
But safe was not the same as growing. Shelter kept a thing alive. It did not make a thing strong.
In the cass things went wrong, their Dimensionality could not be so weak that all then could be broken with a single foot coming down!

Of course, he would not just give them power. He thought of the jade lifeform in a story Atlas told, who had never once failed and shattered the first time he met a wall, and Noah had no intention of building a house full of jade lifeforms.
He would give them a place to earn it.
He called the full weight of his Provenance up out of himself and let it pour onto the sand.

Infinite Sanguine Mana came with it, crimson and gold, and the eight elements turned in the air over his hands, hydrogen through neodymium in their strict order. Nine droplets of Distilled Cause Essence condensed beside them. And into all of it he threaded the two things that made this his and no one else’s: THE Precept of the Waking Dream, and the fresh gold script of the Foundational Narrative Inscription running down his forearm, feeding the whole working a foundation that would not crack under its own size.
He began to build.
HUUM!
It was not a shelter, and it was not a weapon. It was a place to live a life in!
Time inside would not answer to time outside. A day out here on the shore would be a hundred years in there. That was the baseline.
And what they earned in there would be real when they woke!

A dream is usually a thing you wake up from and leave behind. Not this one! Built on his Provenance, mortared with Distilled Cause Essence, fed by his Infinite Sanguine Mana, the dream would hold onto whatever a sleeper forged inside it, every insight, every rank of Trueness, every scrap of Dimensionality won through struggle, and when the dreamer opened their eyes, the dream would hand it to their waking body and make it true.
HUUM!
|THE SOVEREIGN PROVENANCE DREAM ENGINE has been engineered.|
|A place to live, struggle, and advance. Power forged within crystallizes without on waking. Time within is decoupled from the continuum.|
The working finished, and it rose off the sand.
A chrysalis of blue-gold light, enormous, faceted, turning slow above the shore, its surface running with the same script that ran down his arm. It hummed!
Time.
Again and again, time was a factor as another body had already been sent out to head towards an Atlas Elsedimension where he would further throw himself into the weavings of time!
Noah looked at his design for a moment. Then he closed his eyes and called his people.
They came onto the golden sand one after another, and the shore filled.

His mother came, and Henry, and Seo-yeon. Adelaide. Barbatos. Eon, Naldine and the other Queens. Kazuhiko and Titano and Ul’moreth and the Great Beyonder, and behind them a long tide of others, every face he had gathered across a long climb!
Even the ones who were more record than flesh now, the weavings Oppenheimer, Commander Feng, a dozen more, took shape on the sand and stood among the living!
Noah sat before all of them as no pressure rolled off him. No aura pushed anyone back. He was only a man! Only a Human Dreamer!
He told them calmly about the Immensity all around them.

The Dimensionality where a monster could be standing right before you...and you wouldn’t even be able to perceive it. He told of Primeval Ones, Descendants, Provenance Lifeforms, THE Immense Ones and everything he was shielding them from!
"I have kept you safe," he said."I would keep you safe forever if safe were enough. It may not be enough."
Then he showed them the chrysalis.

"I have Dreams, but so do you all. Dream an endless and glorious Dream in here. Your own lives, your own troubles, your own enemies, your own long roads. A hundred years in there for a day out here, more if your existence can bear more. Whatever you win in the dream, you keep when you wake."

"There is a library inside, everything I have ever learned or gathered, arts, techniques, and THE Infinite Scales. Study them if you like. Follow them if they fit. Or throw them out and build something that is only yours. I don’t much care which. I care that you come back able to stand next to me instead of behind me."
For a moment nobody moved.
Then Kazuhiko, THE Emperor Penguin, and Erikson stepped forward as they did not ask a single question!
RAA!
They walked to the chrysalis and entered in a flash of brilliance!
Henry, Seo-yeon, and others followed!
After that, the others slowly went as their eyes shone brilliantly!

A hairy Ul’moreth, yet another one of Noah’s Teachers, looked at Noah in a face hidden by boundlless obsidian gold hair as he also disappeared.THE Big Stepper made a move as he might make something out of THE First Tongue more than Noah did!
Noah’s mother was the last to go as she came up to him and floated beside him.
"I am already living my grandest Dream, but I will see what more is out there. After all, I am the origin of...your Infinite Dream. If I get serious, could I make something grand happen?"
His mother smiled as if she were joking as she let the threads of dreams wrap around her too!
Noah couldn’t help but smile.
The chrysalis hummed, and millions of fine threads spun up around the dreamers, weaving the shape of the lives they were about to live.
Out in the waking part of THE Infiniverse, their bodies were laid into warm pools of Infinite Sanguine Mana, and their cells began to drink.
Noah stood over them for a little while.
THE Infiniverse manifested at his side, and Ruination beside her as they were quiet.
Noah looked at the chrysalis a while longer, at the turning threads, at his people!
Then he stepped back and left it to the two of them.
"Tell me..."he said, "when the first one opens their eyes."

This body sat on golden sand, on a shore inside THE Infiniverse.
An endless sea ran out from it in slow blue-gold swells, and behind him lay island farmland so quiet and so full!
He thought about his people while he worked.
His children.
His mother.
The Queens.
The ones who had walked beside him across his journey.
The Emperor Penguin, Erikson, Titano, Ul’moreth, Kazuhiko, all the rest.
They were technically safe in THE Infiniverse all this time.
But safe was not the same as growing.
Shelter kept a thing alive.
It did not make a thing strong.
In the cass things went wrong, their Dimensionality could not be so weak that all then could be broken with a single foot coming down!
Of course, he would not just give them power.
He thought of the jade lifeform in a story Atlas told, who had never once failed and shattered the first time he met a wall, and Noah had no intention of building a house full of jade lifeforms.
He would give them a place to earn it.
He called the full weight of his Provenance up out of himself and let it pour onto the sand.
Infinite Sanguine Mana came with it, crimson and gold, and the eight elements turned in the air over his hands, hydrogen through neodymium in their strict order.
Nine droplets of Distilled Cause Essence condensed beside them.

And into all of it he threaded the two things that made this his and no one else’s: THE Precept of the Waking Dream, and the fresh gold script of the Foundational Narrative Inscription running down his forearm, feeding the whole working a foundation that would not crack under its own size.
He began to build.
HUUM!
It was not a shelter, and it was not a weapon.
It was a place to live a life in!
Time inside would not answer to time outside.
A day out here on the shore would be a hundred years in there.
That was the baseline.
And what they earned in there would be real when they woke!
A dream is usually a thing you wake up from and leave behind.
Not this one!

Built on his Provenance, mortared with Distilled Cause Essence, fed by his Infinite Sanguine Mana, the dream would hold onto whatever a sleeper forged inside it, every insight, every rank of Trueness, every scrap of Dimensionality won through struggle, and when the dreamer opened their eyes, the dream would hand it to their waking body and make it true.
HUUM!

|A place to live, struggle, and advance.
Power forged within crystallizes without on waking.
Time within is decoupled from the continuum.|

Time.

chapters.title: Chapter 5735: A Terrifying Narrative I
paragraphs: As his people began to dream endless dreams of their own, noah returned to explore the immensity of his own terrifying dream!
Eckert was still talking when Noah set his gaze after...THE Creature.

He could sit on a blue-gold throne across from an old friend and listen to him explain how he had turned laziness into a system, and at the same time, with the same attention, reach out and follow a different thread somewhere else.
So he reached. He found THE Creature’s weavings inside THE Dimensional Provenance Train and threads of dreams pulled him along!
He meant only to look in on a friend he had not seen in a while.
Truly, this was all he meant to do!
Waves of blue-gold light pulsed and pulsed all around for a short while as his consciousness moved alongside his grand Provenance.
The dream carried him into a Cabin, and he opened his eye in a sky full of eyes.
The weavings of existence that communicated exactly what was around him told him a great deal of many things in the first nanosecond as...
He went still.
He had come in over the Tragic Heroes with one gaze above him, and that had been enough to make him careful. This...was not one!
’Fucking hell...’
His Provenance pulsed as he became extremely careful!
The prompts came before he could count them.
|You have entered a Narrative of Existence observed by several of Those Who Remain.|
|Observing: THE OVERSEEING ONE. THE UNPAID COLLECTOR. THE GLOATING JAILER. THE CACKLING BUTCHER. THE STARVING CONNOISSEUR. THE SLEEPLESS FIEND.|
|One further gaze is present and is not observing the Narrative.|
WAA!
THE OVERSEEING ONE, sour with a humiliation he had not finished digesting, the same gaze that had staged the Tragic Heroes and walked away from it!
THE UNPAID COLLECTOR, who had burned half a lineage over a stolen lifeform and promised to come back for the rest!
Noah had stood under both of those. He recognized their brilliance!
And THE SLEEPLESS FIEND.
Oh, this fucker.

He let his gaze go to that name now and barely dared to hold it there. What hung in that part of the sky was not a shape so much as a brightness that never rested, woven, restless, the light of something that had not closed its eyes in countless ages and did not intend to.

He looked at it for the space of a breath and looked away, because even masked, even beneath notice, looking at the Fiend felt like standing too close to a thing that would eventually notice it was being looked at.
Information began to flow to him as his dream pulled and pulled!
|NARRATIVE OF EXISTENCE: The Weaving of IT.|
|Two lifeforms within this Cluster carry Shards of Existence. Within the Shards are weavings of IT.|
|Collapse the bearers. Expose the Shards. What slipped the hands of the Immense may be glimpsed by whoever holds them.|
|The prey holding The Shards: THE CREATURE. THE WRITER OF MYTHOS.|
|The hunters: THE INFINITY EATER. THE CHAMPION. THE USURPER. And THE ZENITH OF SUBJUGATION.|
The Sealed One, or really one of his Vessels, was also here! It was packed!

Noah did not move his eye as he did not let the mask so much as flicker. He hung at the far edge of the gallery, a small weak watcher come to spectate, and the gathered high seats did exactly what he had bet his existence they would do.
They took him for a newcomer. Something lesser drifting in to see a story it could never have staged. Only THE OVERSEEING ONE glanced over as he still seemed embarrassed and did not look for long!
He let himself breathe, if a dream can breathe. Then he looked down.
Below the gallery spread a cluster of Dimensions coupled together into one great wound in the side of the Train!

Rivers ran through it, and the rivers were the dead. Cities stood in it, and the cities had been raised by the unburied out of whatever they had left behind. Gates opened in it, and every gate opened only downward.

The sky over one Dimension was the underside of another Dimension’s floor. Every region was a different death, and they went on, region beyond region beyond region, further than even his gaze could chase!
A cluster of underworlds!
And in one of them, upon the bank of a river that ran grey and slow, a Descendant ferryman stood in a flat boat with a pole in his hands.
He was taking coins. Coins that pulsed faintly with Existential Narrative!

A thing that looked less a Descendant than a collapsed, half-illusory lifeform came up out of the water, pressed something into his palm, and stepped down into the boat, and the ferryman pushed off and poled across the grey.

By the wear on the pole and the coins heaped at his feet, he had been doing this for a very long while, and all around the boat, beneath the slow grey surface, obscene collapsed Descendants swirled and drifted like ghosts.
Noah looked at that for longer than he had meant to.
Then the hidden-gaze spoke, tbe gaze that was not listed among other Immense Ones, and the words carried her fury across the whole of the sky!
|THE MATRIARCH OF INK objects. My Descendant is not a game piece.|
The other gazes did not stir. THE OVERSEEING ONE answered her the way a lord answers another...or maybe even a servant who has spoken out of turn at his own table.

|Every single lifeform apart from us is a piece that we may play with however we wish. Have you grown so attached to something so feeble, and so lesser? You would not do something so detrimental to your own existence... would you?|
The ink went darker. It did not reply!
And far below in the Cluster, upon a stretch of dead ground beneath a sky that was some other Dimension’s floor, a woman with silver-white hair calmly opened a book.
The Glorious Writer of Mythos!

chapters.title: Chapter 5736: A Terrifying Narrative II
paragraphs: The first hunter reached THE Writer of Mythos before Noah had even finished looking around!

THE INFINITY EATER came across the underworld with an infinite sea of Dimensionality heaving at his back, and that sea was all of what he was, density without end, weight without a bottom, a tide that had been grinding against existence since before most of the Train had even been laid down!
Noah knew this one. This was the farmer whose fields had been drunk to their roots by him!
But he...he was not here for Noah. He had come for the woman with the book, and he came for her like a flood comes for a house!
Yet she did not lift her eyes from the page.
Noah looked down upon her with Sonder, and he saw at once what the gallery hungry for prey had not troubled itself to see!
She was a Descendant. Bred, spoken, a sentence with a bloodline, the way all of them were. That much they all knew. What some had not looked at was the rest of her!
She brimmed with her own Provenance! Not borrowed and not inherited, but hers, generated from within, precisely as Noah’s was his own!

And around her turned seas of Existential Narrative, slow and wide and immense, the single most guarded thing an Immense One possessed, and she wore it openly in the middle of a hunt like a grand coat she had simply decided never to remove! Someone up in that sky had handed her their very Narrative to wear, and Noah did not need to guess which gaze it was.
He looked past all of it, down to her dream, and it was the strangest dream he had yet read!
She...wanted a story she could not control!

That was it. Not power. Not survival. Not even the Shard they said she held within her. She had written every ending she had ever seen coming, an eternity of endings, and she had grown so weary of knowing them all that she had walked into a Cabin where Immense Ones fully intended to kill her, and she had done it on purpose, because here, at long last, she might actually lose!
So she wrote.
Her pen moved once across the page, the words rising off it heavy with weight, and a figure stepped up out of the book and onto the dead ground!
THE ONE WHO RETURNS!

A person! A shape every story had always carried somewhere within it, the one who was lost and came back again, given now a body and a stride and a purpose, and it walked straight into the Infinity Eater’s endless tide and met it head-on with seas of illusory Dimensionality and Provenance.
HUUUM!
The sea crashed down, and it did not go through!
She began writing tropes and archetypes on her books as shockingly...they manifested in existence.

She wrote again, unhurried and serene.THE FALLEN CHAMPIONrose off the page, broken once and standing regardless, and struck at the Eater’s side! She wrote a third time, and Noah watched the Eater’s whole infinite weight lurch to a halt in confusion, because THE TRAITOR AT THE GATE had appeared behind him!
Behind him! The Eater swung his enormous head to stare at a thing that had no business standing there, and he did not understand, could not understand, how it had come to be!
But Noah understood exactly how it had!

He knew this. He had done this himself as he was writing tropes into scenes as absolute law and letting probability itself bend to keep the story true. She... was doing the very same thing! She was doing it with the pen held out in the open, where the whole gallery of monsters could watch, and the archetypes she wrote did not merely tilt a fight as they stood up and fought it themselves!
The gallery stirred at last. THE CACKLING BUTCHER was delighted, and said as much! THE STARVING CONNOISSEUR was bored, and said that too! THE SLEEPLESS FIEND said nothing at all!
And in the very middle of it, in the middle of holding back an infinite sea with three stories and a pen, Calliope stopped.
She looked up.
Not at the gallery but well...past it! To the far edge of the sky, where a weak watcher hung and had hung since the moment he opened his eye, small and masked and beneath the notice of anyone!
She blinked once with surprise.
Then she looked back down to her book, and she wrote a single line.
And grandly, in the next moment, Noah felt his weavings buzz as words arrived on a unique frequency of his existence!
They arrived directly within his Provenance, the way only one writer could ever place them into another...

|Oh my. Are you another existence with the capability to steer and write the narratives of existence? And for you to be so bold as to write yourself as though you were an Immense One, and even stand among them! Wow! Hello. I am Calliope. Who are you?|
At her shocking words, Noah was silent.

He gauged this unique lifeform from the far edge of the gallery, this being who could bend the narratives of existence and was somehow not one of the Immense Ones watching her, and he was entirely, dangerously curious! So he gazed upon her fully, and the weavings of existence answered his gaze with her measure!
|CALLIOPE, THE WRITER OF MYTHOS - DESCENDANT OF THE MATRIARCH OF INK|
|VERITAS: 330|
|PROVENANCE: 299|
|POTENTIA: 207|
|PONDUS: 204|
Noah’s eye went wide!

Her POTENTIA and PONDUS sat in the low two hundreds, respectable! But her VERITAS blazed at three hundred and thirty, and her PROVENANCE at two hundred and ninety-nine, towering over the rest of her like a cathedral built over a cottage! Such Trueness! Such Provenance! She held an existence more true and more self-generated than almost anything he had ever measured, and she wore it under a mask of serene boredom while an infinite sea tried to drown her!
And even as he drank in the numbers...
|Are you trying to quantify my power? That is an invasion of privacy. And you didn’t even answer me.|
The words arrived in his Provenance, delighted and pointed, and then they sharpened.
|Should I start screaming very loudly to the Immense Ones watching, that the other gaze they are ignoring is not who they think it is? Shall I drag you into this mess, fellow Writer?|

|Should I start screaming very loudly to the Immense Ones watching, that the other gaze they are ignoring is not who they think it is?
Shall I drag you into this mess, fellow Writer?|

chapters.title: Chapter 5737: A Terrifying Narrative III
paragraphs: A threat! It was casual, playful, and absolutely lethal, dropped between them like a coin onto a table!
Noah’s eye squinted.

He did not panic, but he moved carefully now, with the caution of a man who had walked into a room full of monsters and just discovered the one being in it who could point at him. He wove the frequency of his own Provenance together with the Mantle of THE Meta-Fictional Protagonist, threading a narrow private narrative between his existence and hers, a channel only two authors could share, and he spoke into it.
"I am Osmont," he said."I am curious about you, and your narrative. That is all."
His gaze swept the gallery of gathered gazes, the sea below, the hunters converging. "Though you seem to be in a predicament where even as a manipulator of narratives, you... might just lose."
Calliope’s reply came bright and fast, colored with something like joy!
|Hah! Now that would be something new. Something worth writing.|
Her pen never stopped moving as she answered, even as THE ONE WHO RETURNS reeled from a blow of the infinite sea.
|But if you can hide beneath the gazes of Immense Ones and sit among them wearing a little mask, then tell me, what exactly can I not do? Losing sounds thrilling. I might allow it.|
Then, without a breath between:

|But hey, forget all that. I don’t tend to find many interesting things about existence, but I love when I find some truly odd and interesting things! Like...did you know a pig’s orgasm can last more than thirty minutes? Sometimes more than an hour, even. Isn’t that wild?|
What the fuck?
Noah’s existence buzzed as he ran the words back through his own weavings to make certain he had heard it correclty!

THE Writer of Mythos was surrounded on every side by hunters sent to collapse her existence and tear a Shard out of her corpse, an infinite sea crashing against her stories, four of the mightiest predators in this Train converging on her position, and here she was, cheerfully informing him about the reproductive endurance of pigs!
Noah shook his head slowly and did not answer.

Instead he looked away from her, out across the wound in the side of the Train, because he had never forgotten why his gaze had been pulled into this cursed room in the first place. He had come for a friend. And so, while THE Writer of Mythos clashed with THE Infinity Eater, Noah sent his gaze across the Cluster!
Region beyond region of the dead unrolled beneath his eye, until he found the one he sought.
It was a place where the unburied built cities.

They raised them out of what they had left behind, these dead, walls of stacked and silent things, streets that led only to more streets, towers with no one at the windows and no one who would ever come.

Grey light lay over all of it. Nothing here decayed, because decay was a thing for the living, and so the dead cities simply stood, immense and patient and wrong, a civilization holding its breath forever.
And through them marched THE Creature!
His army of Descendants came behind him.
A massive statue was now visible and walked behind its King, faceless and worn, a mountain of carried figures upon its back turning slowly as it moved.
Noah’s gaze found that approaching enemy of THE Creature, and his gaze became cold.
THE ZENITH OF SUBJUGATION!

THE Sealed One, wearing a Vessel, come personally across the Cluster to meet THE Creature, walking through the dead cities with his hands loose at his sides and an expression of mild, patient interest upon his borrowed face. He did not rush!

He did not gather power or raise a weapon or announce himself. He simply walked, unhurried and condescending, a collector who had come to collect, examining the architecture of the dead as he passed as though he might purchase a piece of it on his way to the transaction he actually wanted!

Two prey, carrying two Shards. Two hunts unfolding across two ends of the same Cluster. And the Sealed One, the most terrible of all the hunters, had not gone for the writer who could shield herself with an army of stories.
He had come for THE Creature.
The Sealed One walked closer, and closer, through the streets of the unburied.
And the statue stopped walking.

It halted mid-stride, the mountain on its back going still, and slowly, deliberately, it turned to face the approaching Vessel. For the first time in a long while it did not look toward the far dark or fade back into stone. It stood, and it faced the collector, and something in its worn grey stance became a challenge!
THE Creature’s flat voice rolled out across the dead cities.
"You are my power," he said. "Existence is my power."
The words fell like slabs of iron laid down one atop another!
"Assimilate into existence," THE Creature said, "and let us not play anymore."
The statue answered him without a sound!
It melded. It fused! The worn grey colossus flowed forward into its King and sank into him, stone becoming weight becoming bearing, and THE Creature’s titanic body drank it all down and CHANGED!

His frame took on some of the statue’s qualities, the ancient grey texture running through his obsidian, the mountain of carried figures settling somewhere into the depths of him, and his hand rose and closed, and a terrible bow was grasped in his grip!
HOONG!

Obsidian white flames of Dimensionality erupted around THE Creature, raging up his titanic frame in sheets of white presense, and the dead cities trembled at the heat of them, and Noah looked down upon his friend with a shining gaze, because THE Creature had stopped bearing and had begun to STAND!
And Noah could not be entirely sure, but when he looked at this monstrous lifeform who had his own foundation and legends surrounding him...he felt like he was still hiding a lot more inside of him!

chapters.title: Chapter 5738: A Terrifying Narrative IV
paragraphs: While Noah was looking at the changes of THE Creature...
|You’re going to ignore me again?|
Calliope’s voice slid back into his Provenance, and Noah’s gaze split its attention without effort, half of it on the friend below and half on the writer across the Cluster!
"You say odd things," Noah said, "that do not fit the context of the terrifying things happening right now."
|I say what I say when I want to say it, regardless of the situation.|The words came easily, her pen still dancing across the page as she held back the infinite sea with the other hand.

|I am a Writer of existence. A Writer of Mythos. I know a great many niche facts about existence and I always, always want to learn more. The lifeforms called pigs and their strange little behaviors were new to me, and new things are the only things I love anymore.|
Then, coyly, she proceed to say...

|But hey. Do you want to know something else? If you actually listen, if you engage with me instead of staring at whatever is burning over there, I will tell you about these Shards the Immense Ones say I carry.|
Her illusory archetypes surged against the Eater’s tide as she wrote, buying herself the space to keep talking.
|It isn’t even a Shard, not really. It is one of the grand Hieroglyph Runestones. I came across it a very long time ago.|
A Hieroglyph Runestone?
Now Noah was even more curious, and he listened in fully, both halves of his attention sharpening!
The Eater’s sea raged around her, and Calliope held it off with one hand and wrote with the other, and the two authors spoke across a channel no gaze in that sky could see.

It was a duel, though no blow was struck between them. She was bored and delighted at once, a being who had finally found a story with a hand in it she could not locate, and she circled Noah with her questions like a scholar circles a specimen she has waited an age to find.
He answered carefully, honestly where he could, because Sonder had shown him her dream and it was not a cruel one.
She wanted a story she could not control. There was no malice under that. There was only a terrible, ancient boredom, and a hunger to learn.
Her hunger was a unique one as it seemed to bud off of her like sparks of utter majesty. And every stroke she made, every movement of her pen looked like a masterpiece of...origin.
"Writing is a Provenance, then," Noah said. It was not a question so much as a thing he was confirming aloud.
|It is. One of the rarer ones.|

Her stories crashed against the sea and held. |Some of us are born with the pen already in the hand. Some of us steal one. And you... I think you stole yours. No offense, but you don’t seem like a natural talent. You have that flavor.|

She said it without accusation, almost approvingly. |My caretaker who is fuming up there is THE MATRIARCH OF INK. She birthed me with the pen in my grip. She did not agree to this...this game, and yet here we are. She is up there right now, furious, and there is nothing she can do about it, which is a story I would rather not be inside of. But how interesting is that? All that power as an Immense One, and one is still constrained. It makes you wonder about power...|
"What about the Shards this whole show is put around? The Runestones..."
|The Shard is real. But Shard is their word, a small ugly word.|
Her voice warmed, the way it only did when she reached the thing she actually loved.
|As I mentioned before, they are called Hieroglyph Runestone. Do you want to know what those are, Osmont? Truly? Because almost no one decent left in existence does.|
Noah’s gaze fixed on her fully!

|They are stones, old ones, older than some of the Immense Ones sitting above me right now, and upon them is carved the history of Existence itself. THE history. What happened before the Sundering. What the ones who left wrote down before they went. What IT was, before it slipped every hand that reached for it.|

Her pen slowed, and her words came slower with it, reverent now. |They were scattered across all of existence, hidden in the deepest and deadest places. But if you find them, Osmont...Ho Ho Ho... If you find enough of them, and you can read what is carved there, they point. Each stone points to the next, and the next, and the next. And the road they make...|
She let it hang for one perfect beat.

|The road they make leads to IT, well, or something even grander. Because even I want it to be a surprise. I want to be swept off my feet for grand Mythos of existence...otherwise if I find them inadequate, I will write my own.|
BOOM!
The whole shape of the room rearranged itself in Noah’s mind at once!

He looked up, past the writer, up at the gallery of gathered gazes watching a game they had staged, and he began, coldly, to understand what he was actually looking at. And Calliope, still writing, still holding back an infinite sea with one lazy hand, said the thing that turned the entire Narrative on its head.
|They did not stage, this entire Train to find IT, or even these Runestones, you know.|
Her pen moved.

|They staged it to find out who can HOLD it. Someone who can find a Hieroglyph Runestone, and read it, and carry it in their existence without it tearing them apart, that someone has the potential to hold IT itself. And here is the funny part, the part they would gouge my eyes out for saying aloud.|

Her voice dropped into something wickedly delighted. |Even Immense Ones are not guaranteed to be able to hold, or grasp, or utilize the weavings of IT. Not one of them up there knows for certain that they could touch it and survive. So they are doing what they always do when they are afraid and pretending not to be.|
|They are basically fucking around right now.|

chapters.title: Chapter 5739: Hieroglyph Runestones I
paragraphs: <Epigraph- An Unknown Age, Discovery of Hieroglyph Runestones>
Two beings stood in a dead place at the bottom of a dead Dimension, and the two Hieroglyph Runestones waited in the dark ahead of them.

The first was a cube. A vast one, obsidian shading to grey, each face wider than an Observable Existence, and across every face ran carvings in a tongue so old that the marks did not sit still under the eye; rearranging themselves whenever a mind tried to hold them.

The second was a sphere, greater than the cube, perfectly round and perfectly cold, and its surface too was written over end to end, spiraling script that wound around it without beginning and without end.
Serala stood beside Vakochev and looked at the two shapes for a long time.

She was beautiful. Dark hair, a sharp and patient face, eyes that missed nothing. She had walked beside the maker of the Scales through more dead places than either of them could count, and she had never yet asked him a foolish question.
"What are they?" she said at last.
Vakochev smiled.

He raised one hand, and from the whole of his body endless seas of THE Primordial Source surged out, dense and dark and old, pouring across the dead ground and rising up the two shapes to wrap them, and where the Source touched, the ancient carvings woke and began to glow, cube and sphere lighting the dead Dimension with the cold light of the first things.
"They are Hieroglyph Runestones," he said.
He walked a slow circle around the cube as he spoke, the Source trailing off him.

"Existence has a memory. Everything that has ever happened is written somewhere, in the weavings, in the Records, in the agreement of things about what they are. But the Records can be edited. The weavings can be torn and re-sewn. What is written in the ordinary bones of existence can be rewritten by anyone strong enough to hold the pen, and there are beings strong enough to hold the pen, and they are not kind, and they do not love the truth. So the memory of existence is not safe. It has never been safe."
He set his palm flat against a glowing face of the cube, and the crawling script slowed under his hand as if it recognized him.

"These are the exceptions. These are the memories of existence made into a thing that cannot be edited. They were carved before the frameworks were laid, in a tongue that predates agreement itself, out of a substance that does not answer to any authority born after it. You cannot rewrite what is on a Hieroglyph Runestone. You cannot lie to one. You cannot make one forget. An Immense One could pour the whole of its existence against this cube and it would not change a single mark, because the cube is older than the Immense One, and older than the thing that makes an Immense One what it is. They are...the one honest thing left in a dishonest existence."
BOOM!
Serala came to stand beside the cube, and she reached out and stopped, her fingers a breath from the glowing stone.
"You can read them? It all seems like gibberish to me." she said.
"I have read this one." He touched the cube. "The sphere I have not been able to read at all. Trueness is the key...among other things."
"And what does it say?"Serala asked.
Vakochev was quiet for a moment, and the glow of the two Runestones lit his face.
When he spoke his voice had changed, gone lower and more careful.
"It tells the beginning," he said. "The real one. Not the story the Immense Ones tell about themselves. The first."
He looked up at the cube.

"There was a Dimension. The Runestone names it, though I will not say the name aloud in a dead place, because names have a way of reaching the things they belong to. Lets call it... THE Sundered Dimension, because that is what it became. In the earliest age of existence, before there was a first among lifeforms, before anyone had ever exceeded anything, a being went into that Dimension alone."
The Source coiled tighter around the cube, and the glow deepened.

"It was trying to become something existence had no shape for. There was no ladder then. No Scales, no Weave, no path up, because no one had ever gone up. The being had to make the climbing and do the climbing at the same time. And in THE Sundered Dimension, where reality was already thin, it found that it could take the weight of existence itself and bring it down onto its own foundation as a catalyst for growth. It was THE First Adversity... and it was carried out by existence itself. It has always Existence..."
"It became the first Immense One?" Serala said quietly.

"Eventually yes, it became the first Immense One."Vakochev nodded. "It did not become an Immense One by growing strong. Strength was only the road. What actually happened, at the threshold, is that the being touched IT."
The name fell into the dead Dimension, and even the crawling script on the cube seemed to still for a moment.

"IT was there, in THE Sundered Dimension, because that is where the walls were thinnest, and IT is the thing on the other side of every wall. Some actually posed that Atlas forged IT. They do not know the true history. Atlas was not even alive and IT what’s already there."

"But I digress. Back to that lifeform. The being touched IT, and for one instant it held the pen that writes existence, and in that instant it wrote itself into a shape existence had never permitted before. It became the first Immense One. And more than that, it became the only being, before or since, that could truly wield IT. The one and only. Every hand that has reached for IT in all the ages after touched the same thing the first one touched, and not one of them could make it answer."
Serala’s hand finally came to rest against the cube, and the glow ran up her fingers, and she did not flinch.
"The first one could use it," she said slowly. "And no one after. Why?"
"That is the question the cube asks and does not answer."Vakochev’s voice went low.

"Here is what it does say. The first being touched IT, became an Immense One, held the authorship of existence in its own hand, and looked out at the whole vastness of what it had become and what it could now do. It stood at the precipice of the one thing every lifeform that has ever lived secretly wants. Absolute authorship. The pen that writes the weavings Existence. It is untold wonder with no ceiling above it, simply endless possibilities."
He was quiet for a moment!
"And it glanced at that endless possibility once. Only once. And then it reached into its own existence and gouged out its own Trueness and its own origin, and it ended itself."
BOOM!

"It dissipated its own being at the very moment it had won everything there was to win. Whatever it saw when it held the pen, whatever knowledge or power came with the touching, it looked at that and chose to stop existing rather than keep it."
Oh!
