They were carved before the frameworks were laid, in a tongue that predates agreement itself, out of a substance that does not answer to any authority born after it.
You cannot rewrite what is on a Hieroglyph Runestone.
You cannot lie to one.
You cannot make one forget.

An Immense One could pour the whole of its existence against this cube and it would not change a single mark, because the cube is older than the Immense One, and older than the thing that makes an Immense One what it is.
They are...the one honest thing left in a dishonest existence."
BOOM!
Serala came to stand beside the cube, and she reached out and stopped, her fingers a breath from the glowing stone.
"You can read them?
It all seems like gibberish to me." she said.
"I have read this one." He touched the cube.
"The sphere I have not been able to read at all.
Trueness is the key...among other things."
"And what does it say?"Serala asked.
Vakochev was quiet for a moment, and the glow of the two Runestones lit his face.
When he spoke his voice had changed, gone lower and more careful.
"It tells the beginning," he said.
"The real one.
Not the story the Immense Ones tell about themselves.
The first."
He looked up at the cube.
"There was a Dimension.
The Runestone names it, though I will not say the name aloud in a dead place, because names have a way of reaching the things they belong to.
Lets call it...
THE Sundered Dimension, because that is what it became.
In the earliest age of existence, before there was a first among lifeforms, before anyone had ever exceeded anything, a being went into that Dimension alone."
The Source coiled tighter around the cube, and the glow deepened.
"It was trying to become something existence had no shape for.
There was no ladder then.
No Scales, no Weave, no path up, because no one had ever gone up.
The being had to make the climbing and do the climbing at the same time.
And in THE Sundered Dimension, where reality was already thin, it found that it could take the weight of existence itself and bring it down onto its own foundation as a catalyst for growth.
It was THE First Adversity... and it was carried out by existence itself.
It has always Existence..."
"It became the first Immense One?" Serala said quietly.
"Eventually yes, it became the first Immense One."Vakochev nodded.
"It did not become an Immense One by growing strong.
Strength was only the road.
What actually happened, at the threshold, is that the being touched IT."
The name fell into the dead Dimension, and even the crawling script on the cube seemed to still for a moment.
"IT was there, in THE Sundered Dimension, because that is where the walls were thinnest, and IT is the thing on the other side of every wall.
Some actually posed that Atlas forged IT.
They do not know the true history.
Atlas was not even alive and IT what’s already there."
"But I digress.
Back to that lifeform.
The being touched IT, and for one instant it held the pen that writes existence, and in that instant it wrote itself into a shape existence had never permitted before.
It became the first Immense One.
And more than that, it became the only being, before or since, that could truly wield IT.
The one and only.
Every hand that has reached for IT in all the ages after touched the same thing the first one touched, and not one of them could make it answer."
Serala’s hand finally came to rest against the cube, and the glow ran up her fingers, and she did not flinch.
"The first one could use it," she said slowly.
"And no one after.
Why?"
"That is the question the cube asks and does not answer."Vakochev’s voice went low.
"Here is what it does say.
The first being touched IT, became an Immense One, held the authorship of existence in its own hand, and looked out at the whole vastness of what it had become and what it could now do.
It stood at the precipice of the one thing every lifeform that has ever lived secretly wants.
Absolute authorship.
The pen that writes the weavings Existence.
It is untold wonder with no ceiling above it, simply endless possibilities."
He was quiet for a moment!
"And it glanced at that endless possibility once.
Only once.
And then it reached into its own existence and gouged out its own Trueness and its own origin, and it ended itself."
BOOM!
"It dissipated its own being at the very moment it had won everything there was to win.
Whatever it saw when it held the pen, whatever knowledge or power came with the touching, it looked at that and chose to stop existing rather than keep it."
Oh!

chapters.title: Chapter 5740: Hieroglyph Runestones II
paragraphs: Serala had said nothing as the dead Dimension was very still!
But she had thought at that time about what could have possibly made an existence who was so profound and who held such power end everything they held?

"Since then," Vakochev went on, "very few have touched IT, and none have ever made it work. The barrier is not power. It is not strength. Multiple Immense Ones have stood and stared straight at IT and could not activate a single one of its functions, not one, though each of them could unmake a Dimension with a thought. And IT slipped right past them. But...a peasant with no authority at all, a thing of no standing whatsoever, could in principle put a hand on IT and change the entire landscape of existence. The lock has nothing to do with how mighty you are. The first one had almost no strength when it began, and it is still the only one who ever held the pen."
He turned from the cube and looked at her.

"So the question is why. What did that first being see, at the precipice of every glory a lifeform could want, that made it end itself rather than hold on? What was done, all the way back then, to make IT the way IT now is, a thing that answers to no strength and no weakness, that turned the only being who ever wielded it into a suicide, and has refused every hand since? Is IT the answer to something, or the warning against it?"

His voice dropped."I do not know. The cube brings me to the edge of the knowing and stops. But THE Hieroglyph Runestones are the only things left in existence that might tell the true story of what happened back then. Not this one alone. There are others, scattered, each a page. If I could gather enough of them, I think they would tell me why the first of the Immense unmade itself the very day it became one."
He glanced at the silent sphere.

"But I have found only two in a whole lifetime of looking. And multiple of them, I am certain, are already in the hands of Immense Ones, who guard them not to read them, but to make sure no one else ever does."
The two of them stood in the light of the two stones, the cube read and the sphere still silent, the seas of THE Primordial Source turning slow around them both.

"You are going to look for the rest of them? You may spend spend what is left of your life chasing stones, so that one day you can read why a being unmade itself at the moment of its glory. Is it all...worth it?"
Was it worth it?
Vakochev had been silent for a little while.

"More than worth it. But...I am going to build a ladder first," Vakochev said. "So that when I am gone, the ones below do not have to break themselves finding the road the way I did. I do not want to be the last honest thing in a dishonest existence. I want to make honesty cheap enough that everyone can afford it."
He looked at her. "And yes. After that, I am going to keep chasing the stones, until I know what that first one saw. Because I think it is the most important thing that has ever been forgotten."
Serala was quiet for a long moment.

"They will try and stop you. They will definitely stop us as..." she said. "You may never live to read the last stone. You may be...just like that first Immense One. If you eventually grasp everything that they grasped, what if you do the same thing and choose to..."
She could not finish her words!
WAA!
"Maybe."
"Then why read the stone at all?" she asked, her eyes almost tearing up.
"Why this need to know? I just...I just want to spend all of existence holding on to you. I don’t want to know!"
Vakochev looked at the cube for a long time, and then he looked at the sphere he had never been able to read, the greater of the two, older still, holding a truth he would go to his grave without.
He could not gaze at the woman beside him...as if he knew his conviction would be shaken if he did!

"Because a thing that is true is worth knowing whether or not you can use it,"he said. "The Immense Ones believe knowledge is a tool, and a tool is only worth the work it does, and a truth you cannot spend is a truth not worth having. That is why they rewrite the Records. That is why they bury the stones. To them, a fact that cannot be turned into power is garbage, and the past is only a resource to be mined or hidden."
He set his hand against the cube one last time, and the crawling script warmed under his palm.

"But the past is not a resource. It is not a tool. It is the true thing, the thing that happened, whether or not anyone ever benefits from knowing it. And an existence that only values the truths it can spend is an existence that will, in the end, forget it was ever true at all."

"I read the stone because it is true. I may die before I use it. And it was still worth every year it cost me, because for one night, in a dead place, at the bottom of a broken realm, one being ended himself in the face of Everything...but even his record was said aloud. Aloud and recorded on the Hieroglyph Runestones."
He turned from the stone.
"In an existence built on a lie, one true thing said aloud is not nothing. It may be the only thing that isn’t."
The two Runestones glowed a while longer in the dead Dimension, the read and the unread, and then the maker of the Scales let the Source fall away from them, and the ancient light went out!
<Current Age>
The Immense Ones were fucking around!
That was the truth stripped of all its grandeur, and Noah turned the thought over from the far edge of the gallery.

Here were beings of terrifying, existence-ending power, gazes that had burned lineages and frozen springs and staged whole tragedies for their own amusement, and they had gathered over this cluster of Dimensions for one reason, which was that not one of them, for all their might, could be certain they were able to hold IT!
They already had power beyond counting. They were hunting for a KEY, a lifeform shaped correctly enough to grasp the one thing their power could not!
And they did not know which shape that was as the clue came with those...holding Hieroglyph Runestones.
But these were terrifying beings, reduced to gamblers who could not read their own dice!
Noah was still turning that over when Calliope’s voice slid back into his Provenance, and she was, as ever, talking a great deal.

|Hmm, it is so hard, you know, to come across another existence who can freely steer narratives when they have not even reached the level of an Immense One. So hard! I feel like I could talk to you for an Age and only get started. And yet look at this predicament around me. It simply does not allow it!|
Her pen never stopped as she spoke, archetypes surging and breaking against the infinite sea below.

|Whatever narrative the Immense Ones have designed here, I do not like its flow. It is not coherent. It does not carry the feeling of a grand myth, of a true epic, and I would know, since building those is the whole of what I am! It reads like something written by old men, by bored things who have forgotten how a story is supposed to move. I want...to change it up.|

chapters.title: Chapter 5741: Change The Narrative! I
paragraphs: She wrote, and THE ONE WHO RETURNS heaved the sea back as if he were smashing all of Existence back itself!

|Look at the pieces they have gathered. Two Vessels of THE Sealed One are present in this Cluster. One holds the weavings of the Sealed One himself, clean, the real thing. But the other? The other is a murky mixture, and it fascinates me, because it seems that even THE Sealed One was targeted, once, and had a portion of his own existence assimilated by someone else. A collector, collected! And then there is the other prey, the one who is not me, who carries another Hieroglyph Runestone just as I do, which means there is someone else in this Cluster capable of holding a Runestone inside their existence without it tearing them apart. Someone who might be able to handle IT. I am terribly curious about that one, too.|
She was talking a whole lot, and Noah let her, because every word she spilled was more information for him!

He turned his gaze toward one direction of the Cluster, toward the lifeform who held the Mantle of THE USURPER, and his eye sharpened with recognition as he could see a glimmer of the Dream and identity of the lifeform within.

Adrastia. He remembered this existence he had crossed paths with before, and it was exactly as strange as Calliope had said. It carried the power of THE Sealed One, and yet it was not the Sealed One, a mixture of itself and the thing that had tried to claim it. Had it been meant to become a Vessel, and instead found the capability to RESIST, to swallow half of what came to swallow it? A being that had been targeted for assimilation and had assimilated its assimilator halfway back?
Was that the murky one Calliope spoke of? A Vessel that had, in some measure, refused?
Noah turned his gaze the other way, across the whole span of the Cluster, to the region of dead cities where his friend stood.
THE Creature.

As grand as this being had always been, Noah understood now that THE Creature too held the capability to hold IT. He carried a Shard, a Hieroglyph Runestone woven inside him. And he was in a unique state, after fusing with the statue, a state Noah had never seen an existence occupy. He gazed upon his friend fully, and the weavings answered!
|THE CREATURE|
|VERITAS: 244|
|POTENTIA: Undefined.|
|PROVENANCE: Undefined.|
|PONDUS: 251|
|Note: the analyzed lifeform is in a state of existential transformation.|
|It is both generating and not generating its own weavings, paradoxically and at once.|
|Its Provenance is being established at this present moment. Its Provenance was already established in the future. A paradoxical continuum of time has begun to wrap around this existence...|
Noah squinted!

Undefined. Not a number too high to read, not a veil of question marks, but Undefined, a thing the weavings of existence could not resolve because THE Creature was, at this instant, standing in two times at once!

His Provenance was being born and had already been born. He was building his foundation and had finished building it in a future that had not yet arrived. The fusion with the statue had wrapped a loop of time around his titanic frame, and inside that loop the ordinary rules of before-and-after did not hold!
What a state! What a monstrous, paradoxical state!
Noah’s eyes shone.
Below, the battle was changing fast!

THE CHAMPION had entered it. Alcaeus came charging across the Dimensions toward Calliope, a second hunter joining the first, and the infinite sea and the charging Champion converged on the writer at once as she wrote and wrote, new archetypes unfolding off her pages to meet them!
And Noah watched her hand move across a fresh empty page, and he watched the words rise off it heavy with weight!
|The Archetype of THE Rebel shall unfold before me.|

|The Rebel is a unique Mythos. Driven to frustration by the systems and rulings that bind it, the lifeform rebels, for it wishes for change above all things. It will not serve the shape it was given.|
|This Mythos shall unfold within the existence known as... THE CHAMPION.|
BOOM!
Noah felt her Provenance twist uniquely as in the next moment...
THE CHAMPION stopped mid-charge!

Noah saw the great hunter freeze in the dead air over the dreary environment of an underworld, his entire existence beginning to buzz with a terrifying density of Dimensionality, and then his own body began to move without him willing it! An inscription blazed to life upon his right foot he had kept hidden this whole time, ancient and burning, and Alcaeus floated down from the skies against the whole of his intent, and he turned as he targeted...THE INFINITY EATER!
The Champion’s body transformed!

His titanic frame folded and stretched and hardened, obsidian and gold, untill the whole of him had become a massive golden sword, kilometers upon kilometers of blazing blade, and his right foot with its shining inscription became the very tip of that sword, glowing white-hot with enough Dimensionality to cleave through multiple Dimensions at a stroke!
THE CHAMPION had become a weapon, and the weapon was turning on his own ally.
He was rebeling!

The golden sword that had been a hunter fell upon the Infinity Eater’s sea, and the Dimension split beneath the blow, and Noah looked upon it all with shining eyes as Calliope’s voice, warm and bright and entirely delighted, poured back into his Provenance!
|Isn’t it neat? To be able to steer a narrative like this?|

Her pen was already moving to the next page. |I found out, you see, that one of the capabilities of IT is to rewrite how existence is unfolding. Or how it has unfolded. Or how it will unfold, which is my favorite. And when I learned that, I told myself, well, why do I not simply begin developing a little capability like that of my own? I am the Writer of Mythos! So let me write how I want events to unfold, right here, right in front of everyone, and let existence catch up!|
BOOM!
Her words burned with a confidence that made even the dead cities seem to lean in to listen, and Noah could not help but take a second, longer look at her.

What she had just described, what she was doing with a pen and a page in the middle of a killing ground, was extremely, uncomfortably similar to the thing he could accomplish with his own Provenance when he unleashed the full weight of the Mantle of THE Meta-Fictional Protagonist!
Writing tropes into existence as law. Bending how a story unfolded.

He had thought the art was his! He had thought no one else in all of existence had walked this particular road! And here was a Descendant of ink and mythos, bored and delighted and surrounded on all sides, who had already been quietly perfecting the art itself!

paragraphs: Existence breathes, and epochs pass, leaving Civilizations that become monuments, then crumble to memory, and are long forgotten when that breath comes again. In all these epochs, just what reigns supreme?
As Noah thought about the wonder that was Calliope, in the distance...the golden blade fell, and it fell as a rebellion given edge and gravity!

Alcaeus the Champion, rewritten by a pen he had never consented to, plunged downward through the dead air of the Cluster as a sword Gigaparsecs long, his inscribed foot the white-hot tip, and he crashed with the whole of his stolen weight into THE INFINITY EATER’s abyssal infinite sea of Dimensionality!
There was no burst of heat. No detonation of fire!

The blade did something colder and far more surgical, because Calliope had not written destruction, she had written betrayal, and betrayal cuts where a thing is weakest! The golden sword sheared clean through the Eater’s primary harvesting conduits, the great feeding channels through which the Infinity Eater drank the Infinity of countless lifeforms across a thousand Observable Existences and more thousands of Dimensions, all those distant existences who pulled their own Infinity from him and paid for it with a portion of themselves!
The conduits parted.
The infinite sea, cut off at its source, LURCHED, and the Eater staggered as an ocean that had always been fed suddenly found itself bleeding from a wound it did not undersand.
But above, over her open codex, Calliope’s hand trembled as she breathed out.

To force an architect’s own champion to rebel against his deepest nature was not a thing done for free! The causal tension of it, a being made to betray the very shape it had been forged into, pushed back against her pen, and the tax came due in her own flesh.

Her silver-white hair whipped through the air as though a storm blew through the dead Dimensions, and from beneath her fingernails, dark and glistening, droplets of black ink began to seep! Her internal reserves burned rapidly, poured out drop by drop to hold the Rebel in place against Alcaeus’s screaming, authentic will.

|An archetype written into a living vessel must be continually fed. Where the vessel’s true historical intent pushes back against the imposed Mythos, the causal tension snaps backward into the author...|
Her Trueness itself was fraying at the edges, and she wrote on regardless, serene and bleeding at once.
Noah looked at this as this seemed like a limitation he may not be...too entirely bound by if he had acted.
But as things unfolded, far below, in the lower rift of the Cluster, THE Zenith of Subjugation reached THE Creature.

The clean Vessel of THE Sealed One did not rush even now. It extended its hands, and from them uncoiled seven pale chains of absolute suppression, each one a sentence of dormancy, each one designed to seize an existence and freeze it and press it down into a permanent, silent sleep! The chains lashed out toward THE Creature to still his weavings forever.
THE Creature ROARED at this time, sending his army far behind him as if he knew they could do nothing.

His titanic frame, caught in that paradoxical continuum where his Provenance existed both now and in a future not yet arrived, blazed with obsidian-white flames, and the flames scorched the pale chains where they touched!

But the Vessel’s weight was the weight of a being who specialized in taking, one piece at a time, everything a thing had, and slowly, grindingly, the suppression forced THE Creature’s titanic knees downward toward the dead ground!
Down!
And still further down!
And as his knees bent under the sentence of a monster, THE Creature reached back, and his great hand closed around the pure white bow the statue had carried for so long, and he pulled!
The dead Dimensions answered his draw!

As THE Creature hauled the bowstring back, thousands upon thousands of illusory Dimensions gathered before him, folding and compressing, layering one atop another into a single shape, and the shape was an ARROW.
An arrow made of a thousand collapsed Dimensions, nocked to a bow of the first make, drawn by a King almost forced to his knees and refusing to stay there.
His eyes burned with obsidian-white flame, and in that moment THE Creature did not look like a King, and he did not look like a Ruler!

He looked like an ancient fiend, a primordial thing of fire and bearing, and from the depths of him an unknown Provenance began to spill, dark and vast and unnamed, an authority the weavings of existence could not yet put a number to.
He loosed!

The thousand-Dimension arrow tore across the rift toward THE Sealed One, and behind it THE Creature was already drawing another, and another, arrow after arrow of collapsed existences forming and flying, his obsidian flames raging higher with each pull, a fiend of the deep loosing Dimensions at a collector who had thought this would be simple!
And yet even in the face of this...THE Sealed One smiled as he raised his hand as if to welcome everything. As if his purpose here...was much more sinister.
Above it all, in the gallery, THE OVERSEEING ONE leaned forward over the brass balcony!

His crimson gaze pulsed with a mounting, ugly irritation, because his scripted Narrative was coming apart before the eyes of his peers! The Champion had broken formation and turned on his own side! The Eater was being pushed back and bled.
The Creature, who was meant to be pressed quietly into dormancy, was on his knees loosing arrows of worlds and spilling a Provenance no one had accounted for.
Twice now a theater he was watching and rooting for a certain side had refused to obey him. Twice, in front of the others!
He would not suffer it a third time!
|THE OVERSEEING ONE will not be embarrassed again.|
|He reasserts his authorship over a faltering Narrative.|

Streams of the Overseeing One’s own Narrative poured down from the balcony, and they wrapped around both THE Sealed One’s Vessel and THE CHAMPION, threading into them, reinforcing, bracing the failing script with the full weight of an Immense One’s will.
The pale chains on THE Creature drank the reinforcement and pulled tighter! Alcaeus’s rebellion strained against a second, stronger hand now laid over Calliope’s!
And the whole of the Dimensional Cabin, the whole vast Cluster of Dimensions beneath it, began to BUZZ with the terrifying collection of authority gathering in that one place!
|WARNING.|
|Authority within this Narrative of Existence is compounding beyond stable thresholds.|
|Multiple sovereign authors and one Immense One now write over the same continuum at once...|
The dead cities trembled. The rivers of the dead ran backward. The buzz climbed and climbed, existence itself groaning under the weight of too many hands writing over the same page at once!

chapters.title: Chapter 5743: Change The Narrative! III
paragraphs: And in the middle of it, bleeding ink from beneath her nails, her hair a silver storm, Calliope looked up.
She looked past the gallery, past the balcony, to the far hidden edge of the sky where a mobius-pupiled eye had hung masked and silent since the beginning.
She opened their private conduit, and this time her voice carried none of its earlier playful detachment. It was serious, and it was fast, and it was still, somehow, delighted!
|My ink is running a bit dry, Osmont.|
Her pen shook over the page.

|Before my Matriarch has to interfere and ruin the fun, and she will, if this keeps going the way it is going... why don’t the two of us do something grand? Let us change the narrative. Or are you going to sit up there and simply watch, when the two of us together could ruin their entire theater?|
Noah’s masked eye held over the burning Cluster.
And then he moved!
He did not answer with words. He reached out with the whole quiet weight of his Provenance and his Infinite Dream, found the writer’s consciousness in the middle of her bleeding, and PULLED!
Calliope’s perception of the collapsing Cluster froze.

The screaming sea, the falling arrows, the pale chains, the buzzing sky, all of it stopped between one instant and the next, held in a stretched and silent moment, as Noah drew her consciousness up and out and into the inner sanctuary of his Infinite Dream.
An instant, stretched out towards infinity.
Time. Once more, time!
They stood together in a domain of blue-gold clouds.

Endless soft light rolled around them in slow drifts, quiet and boundless and entirely his, a place between spaces where no gaze of any Immense One could reach and no ink ran dry. The war outside did not exist here. Only the two authors, and the stillness he had wrapped around them both.
Calliope looked around at the blue-gold clouds, and her bleeding stopped, and her storm-tossed hair settled, and a slow smile spread across her face.
She waved her hand at Noah, and then, grandly, delighted, she gave a little bow!

"Oh, this is lovely,"she said, aloud now, her voice her own again in the quiet. "You pulled me right out of the story and into your own private one. Very unique. This is...narrative infused with Infinity itself?"
She looked around, and then she straightened, and the delight sharpened into something more serious, because she had been offered a stage and she intended to use it.
"Alright, so let me tell you the truth of what I do," she said, "since we are about to do it together, and you should know the wall before you run at it with me!"
She lifted a hand, and ink gathered at her fingertip.

"I cannot write a falsehood into existence. That is the first law of my craft and it has never once bent for me! An archetype cannot be conjured from a vacuum, out of nothing, out of a lie. It must have an anchor. An authentic historical thing that has already cut its mark into the bedrock of reality, a truth that actually happened, that existence still remembers. I write the Mythos, yes, but the Mythos must have somewhere true to stand, or it does not stand at all!"
Her eyes glittered."I have found ways around the edges of that law, here and there. But they are costly. Very costly."
She smiled again, and this time there was something almost reverent in it.
"But here. Since we are being grand. Let me show you the truest thing I own."
She tapped her own wrist, once, and grandly, from the clouds of Noah’s own sanctuary, something began to emerge.
It rose slowly out of the blue-gold light as something vast and dark and ancient, and it was a....HIEROGLYPH RUNESTONE.

A massive obsidian cube, its faces wider than an Observable Existence, black shading toward grey, and across every face crawled the oldest carvings Noah had ever seen, marks that would not sit still, rearranging themselves whenever the eye tried to hold them, the true history of Existence written in a tongue older than agreement itself!
The moment Noah laid his eyes upon it...
HUUM!
His existence BUZZED!
Something deep in him, deeper than thought, deeper than Provenance, answered the stone.

Noah walked forward as if in a trance, his masked awareness narrowing to the cube and the cube alone, his hand rising of its own accord, reaching, reaching, until his fingers pressed against a glowing obsidian face!
And the Runestone LIT!

Obsidian light blazed up out of it, and obsidian lightning flowed up the whole of Noah’s body in a single crackling surge, racing through his existence, and from Noah’s eyes there erupted beams of pure obisidian light!
Calliope blinked!
Her delight moved into shock, and then into a frown, because this was not what she had expected.
"Osmont? What do you see? Hey, what do you see...?!"
But Noah did not hear her.
For him, everything froze!

The blue-gold clouds, the writer, the cube, the obsidian lightning, all of it locked into a single suspended instant, because Noah’s mind had already been seized and carried away, wrenched somewhere unfathomably far...
Noah’s consciousness woke, and he was looking down upon the beginning of...Existence.
Well, not really, but it felt like it!

He hung, bodiless, over a forest, and it was a forest such as had never grown anywhere he had walked in all his long climb! Ancient beyond ancient, Primordial in the truest sense, a forest from the earliest era of existence when existence had barely learned to be, and it stretched below him further than sight, further than thought, an endless green that was somehow older than green itself.
And the trees were budding with fruit.
But the fruit were not fruit!

Noah stared, his existence gone still with wonder, because upon the boughs of every ancient tree hung Dimensions and Observable Existences, ripening! Each one a swirling jewel of wonder, each one heavy with the lifeforce of of Causes, and each one held within a shape he knew, a faceted crystalline structure of deep blue-white, something almost exactly like a Genesis Tesseract.
Whole domains hung from the branches like how apples hang from an orchard, and the trees that bore them burned with the raw and endless life of the Causes budding inside them!
This was a garden where realities grew like fruit.
And through that garden, a lifeform walked.

Noah’s gaze fell to it, and it surprised him, because for all the impossible grandeur of the forest, the being walking through it was small, and rough, and simple! A caveman-like thing, hunched and unhurried, thick-limbed and unadorned, picking its way between the trees of worlds with the calm of a creature that had been walking here since before walking had a name.
Then a voice boomed out, and it boomed for Noah alone.
It was the voice of the Hieroglyph Runestone, and it did not speak into his ears but into the very core of him, and its words unfolded as prompts across the whole of his frozen sight!
|In the earliest era of existence, no lifeform truly understood Infinity.|

|Not one. They lived within it, they reached for it, they built the first crude frameworks upon its assumption, and yet not a single existence among them could hold it, or see it, or say what it truly was.|
|One of the first ever to begin to understand it... was known as Lucy.|

chapters.title: Chapter 5744: Change The Narrative! IV
paragraphs: Lucy.

Noah watched the small rough being pick her way onward, and understood that he was looking at her, this hunched unhurried thing walking through a forest of growing Dimensions, and the voice of the stone rolled on!

|The earliest existences looked into the heart of a Dimension, into its very center, and their reckoning told them a strange thing: that the center held zero volume, and infinite density. A point of nothing, containing everything.|
|And the wisest among them did not take this to mean that an actual, physical infinity existed there. No. They took it to mean something humbler and far more honest.|
|It meant their understanding had reached its edge. It meant that what lay beyond the center was a thing their minds could not yet envision, could not yet shape, could not yet hold.|
|So they gave that edge a name. They called it... Infinity.|
The forest breathed around the walking figure, worlds ripening on every bough!
|No lifeform has ever truly known Infinity. No lifeform has ever grasped it, or seen it, or proven it even exists.|

|Every musing on Infinity that has ever been spoken, in every age, by every mighty thing, became only this: their own definition of what Infinity could be, as far as they themselves were able to understand it and grasp it.|
|Infinity was never a thing. It was a word. A word each existence filled with the shape of its own not-knowing.|

Noah’s frozen existence turned that over! He had branded his identity onto infinity before! He had wielded it as though it were a thing, a substance, an authority with edges he could hold! And the stone was telling him, gently and enormously, that no one had ever held it at all, that they had only ever held their own understanding of a thing they could not understand!
Below, Lucy stopped walking.

She came to the bank of a river, and the river ran bright and quick, and it was filled with fish! Small, silver, countless, they schooled in the shallows, and the moment Lucy knelt down beside the water, every fish in that river turned its face up toward her and gathered, crowding to the bank, waiting, as though they had done this a thousand times and loved every one.
Lucy smiled at them.

She reached up to the nearest tree and plucked a single Dimension from a low branch, a swirling jewel of a world heavy with a million Causes, and she held it in her thick rough hands, and white light began to wrap around it, spilling from her fingers, wrapping the plucked world in a growing radiance!
And then...
Thousands of genuine Dimensions bloomed from her hands!

Noah watched, and his existence could scarcely hold what it saw, because from that single plucked world, cradled in the hands of a simple caveman thing, Dimensions poured forth without end! Not illusions, not images, but real and genuine Dimensions, thousands of them, then tens of thousands, blooming out of her palms in an endless radiant stream, each one whole, each one ture, each one heavy with its own Causes and its own laws.
She smiled wider, and she directed the endless stream down toward the water.
And the fish ATE them!

The silver fish rose up and took the blooming Dimensions into their mouths as if they were nothing more than crumbs of bread scattered on a pond, swallowing whole Domains, feeding happily, jostling for more.

And Lucy laughed a soundless laugh and kept producing them, minute after minute, Dimension after Dimension after Dimension, what looked to Noah like millions of genuine domains spilling endlessly from the hands of a small rough being for no greater reason than to feed the fish in a river!
An infinite production! Effortless! Joyful! Casual as scattering feed!

Noah’s mind reeled at the sheer, quiet impossibility of it, this being who did not strain, did not calculate, did not grasp at anythng, simply opened her hands and let the infinite pour out as though it were the most natural thing in all of existence.
At last the fish were full, and they scattered back into the bright water, sated and happy, and Lucy let the stream die in her palms and wiped her rough hands on her knees and rose!
She smiled once more at the river, and then she turned, and she walked on through the forest of growing domains, unhurried as ever, as though she had done nothing at all!
And the Runestone spoke its last.
|Infinity will never be a thing you see. It will never be a thing you grasp, or hold, or conquer. It is, and it always was, only a word, a definition given to a thing one does not understand.|
|But here is the key the stone offers you, the only key it has.|

|Attain a good definition. Your own. Unique to you. A clear and sufficient understanding of the very thing you cannot understand. Do not borrow another’s edge, or understanding of Infinity, for another’s edge of impossibility is only the shape of another’s not-knowing.|
|Reach a clear and sufficient definition of your own, and you will be able to read the true idea of Infinity written within this Runestone.|
|And when you read it, a path will light up before you.|
|Where that path leads... is unknown even to the stone.|
HUUM!
The forest began to fade!

The domains on the boughs grew murky, the endless green dimming, the bright river washing out to grey, the whole Primordial garden dissolving at its edges as the vision released its hold upon him and Noah’s consciousness began, slowly, to rise back toward the blue-gold clouds and the frozen war and the writer he had left behind!
And as everything faded, as the forest thinned to almost nothing...
In the very corner of his fading sight, Noah could have sworn he saw it!

The record of the visage of Lucy, the small rough caveman being who scattered infinite Dimensions to feed the fish, stopped walking. She turned her head. And across the whole impossible distance of an age that had ended before Noah was ever born, that ancient thing looked up, directly at him, directly at the watcher the vision was never supposed to notice...
And she smiled at him!
Fiendishly!

sentences.text: Lucy.

Noah watched the small rough being pick her way onward, and understood that he was looking at her, this hunched unhurried thing walking through a forest of growing Dimensions, and the voice of the stone rolled on!
|The earliest existences looked into the heart of a Dimension, into its very center, and their reckoning told them a strange thing: that the center held zero volume, and infinite density.
A point of nothing, containing everything.|
|And the wisest among them did not take this to mean that an actual, physical infinity existed there.
No.
They took it to mean something humbler and far more honest.|
|It meant their understanding had reached its edge.
It meant that what lay beyond the center was a thing their minds could not yet envision, could not yet shape, could not yet hold.|
|So they gave that edge a name.
They called it...
Infinity.|
The forest breathed around the walking figure, worlds ripening on every bough!
|No lifeform has ever truly known Infinity.
No lifeform has ever grasped it, or seen it, or proven it even exists.|

|Every musing on Infinity that has ever been spoken, in every age, by every mighty thing, became only this: their own definition of what Infinity could be, as far as they themselves were able to understand it and grasp it.|
|Infinity was never a thing.
It was a word.
A word each existence filled with the shape of its own not-knowing.|
Noah’s frozen existence turned that over!
He had branded his identity onto infinity before!
He had wielded it as though it were a thing, a substance, an authority with edges he could hold!
And the stone was telling him, gently and enormously, that no one had ever held it at all, that they had only ever held their own understanding of a thing they could not understand!
Below, Lucy stopped walking.
She came to the bank of a river, and the river ran bright and quick, and it was filled with fish!

Small, silver, countless, they schooled in the shallows, and the moment Lucy knelt down beside the water, every fish in that river turned its face up toward her and gathered, crowding to the bank, waiting, as though they had done this a thousand times and loved every one.
Lucy smiled at them.

She reached up to the nearest tree and plucked a single Dimension from a low branch, a swirling jewel of a world heavy with a million Causes, and she held it in her thick rough hands, and white light began to wrap around it, spilling from her fingers, wrapping the plucked world in a growing radiance!
And then...
Thousands of genuine Dimensions bloomed from her hands!
Noah watched, and his existence could scarcely hold what it saw, because from that single plucked world, cradled in the hands of a simple caveman thing, Dimensions poured forth without end!

Not illusions, not images, but real and genuine Dimensions, thousands of them, then tens of thousands, blooming out of her palms in an endless radiant stream, each one whole, each one ture, each one heavy with its own Causes and its own laws.
She smiled wider, and she directed the endless stream down toward the water.
And the fish ATE them!

The silver fish rose up and took the blooming Dimensions into their mouths as if they were nothing more than crumbs of bread scattered on a pond, swallowing whole Domains, feeding happily, jostling for more.

And Lucy laughed a soundless laugh and kept producing them, minute after minute, Dimension after Dimension after Dimension, what looked to Noah like millions of genuine domains spilling endlessly from the hands of a small rough being for no greater reason than to feed the fish in a river!
An infinite production!
Effortless!
Joyful!
Casual as scattering feed!

Noah’s mind reeled at the sheer, quiet impossibility of it, this being who did not strain, did not calculate, did not grasp at anythng, simply opened her hands and let the infinite pour out as though it were the most natural thing in all of existence.
At last the fish were full, and they scattered back into the bright water, sated and happy, and Lucy let the stream die in her palms and wiped her rough hands on her knees and rose!
She smiled once more at the river, and then she turned, and she walked on through the forest of growing domains, unhurried as ever, as though she had done nothing at all!
And the Runestone spoke its last.
|Infinity will never be a thing you see.
It will never be a thing you grasp, or hold, or conquer.
It is, and it always was, only a word, a definition given to a thing one does not understand.|
|But here is the key the stone offers you, the only key it has.|
|Attain a good definition.
Your own.
Unique to you.
A clear and sufficient understanding of the very thing you cannot understand.
Do not borrow another’s edge, or understanding of Infinity, for another’s edge of impossibility is only the shape of another’s not-knowing.|
|Reach a clear and sufficient definition of your own, and you will be able to read the true idea of Infinity written within this Runestone.|
|And when you read it, a path will light up before you.|
|Where that path leads... is unknown even to the stone.|
HUUM!

The domains on the boughs grew murky, the endless green dimming, the bright river washing out to grey, the whole Primordial garden dissolving at its edges as the vision released its hold upon him and Noah’s consciousness began, slowly, to rise back toward the blue-gold clouds and the frozen war and the writer he had left behind!

And she smiled at him!
Fiendishly!

chapters.title: Chapter 5745: Change The Narrative! V
paragraphs: Noah’s awareness snapped back into the blue-gold clouds, and no time had passed at all.

The instant he had left was still the instant he returned to, frozen and stretched and waiting, and Calliope stood before him exactly as she had, the massive obsidian Runestone at her back, her eyes fixed on him and shining bright with a curiosity that had sharpened into something almost hungry!
She had seen the stone reach for him. She had seen the obsidian lightning climb his existence and the beams pour from his eyes. And she wanted, desperately, to know what he had been shown.
But Noah could not answer her, not yet, because his entire existence was BUZZING!

Something had changed in him! Something enormous and quiet had shifted in the deepest place of him, in the way he understood the very thing he had built his early climb upon, and he could feel it moving through him like a tide finding a new shore!
Infinity!

For his whole existence he had treated Infinity as a substance! A thing with weight and corners, an authority he had branded his identity onto, a power he wielded as though he had truly grasped it in his hands.
But the forest had shown him the truth!

No lifeform had ever grasped Infinity. No one had ever held it. It was only ever a word, a definition, a shape each existence poured into its own not-knowing! Lucy had not grasped Infinity when she scattered a million Dimensions to the fish. She had simply reached a definition so clear, so wholly and quietly HERS, that the infinite had poured from her hands like water because she had stopped trying to hold it and simply understood what it was to her!
And Noah understood, in that stretched and frozen instant, what he had to do.
He did not need to grasp Infinity. He never could have.Nobody could.
What he needed was a definition of his own, unique and clear and sufficient, his own understanding of the very thing that could not be understood!
His understanding of the edge. Of Impossibility.
His Infinite Sanguine Mana began to cycle!

Crimson-gold vitality surged and ran through the whole of his existense, through every one of his two hundred decillion quarks and as it moved, Noah gave it a task it had never been given! He poured his new understanding into it, his own fresh and hard-won definition of impossibility, and he let the Sanguine Mana carry that definition through his existence like ink spreading through water.
|You have witnessed a truth kept by a Hieroglyph Runestone: Infinity is not grasped. It is defined.|
|You have begun to reach a definition of unknown an impossibility that is wholly your own.|
Noah’s definition took shape as the Sanguine Mana carried it!
To Lucy, Infinity had been abundance, an endless joyful giving. To the earliest existences it had been the edge of their reckoning, a name for the dark past the center. But to Noah?
To THE Human Dreamer, who had lived a single life across time, who dreamed and made the dreams true, who authored narratives and stood outside the line of moments?
To Noah, Infinity was...a DREAM that did not end. His goals. His dream, ideals, purpose, loves, fears, hopes...his Everythings, that did not end.

That was his definition, his own and no one else’s, clear and sufficient and true to the whole of what he was! Infinity was not a substance and not an edge and not an abundance. It was a dream with no far wall, a story that could always add another page, a reverie that time could stretch forever without ever reaching its close! He did not need to hold the infinite. He only needed to dream a dream that never had to stop!
And his Infinite Sanguine Mana, carrying that definition, bled it directly into THE Provenance of THE Human Dreamer!
HUUM!
The crimson-gold tide met the blue-gold depths of his Provenance, and the definition sank into it, and his Provenance DRANK it, understood it, and answered.
|Your definition of Infinity has been carried by your Infinite Sanguine Mana into THE Provenance of THE Human Dreamer.|
|The two have merged. Your understanding of the infinite is now woven into the substance of your Provenance.|
Something new began to rise in Noah’s existence!

His Provenance of THE Human Dreamer had always let him dream, and dream grandly, but now it took his definition of the infinite and wound it into its own foundation, and a new capability began to bloom, vast and quiet and terrible!
|A new understanding awakens within THE Provenance of THE Human Dreamer.|

|THE INFINITE DREAM: your dreams no longer possess a far wall. A dream you begin need never end. A reverie may be extended without limit, a narrative continued without a final page, a stretched instant expanded toward a forever that answers only to you.|

|You do not hold Infinity. You dream it. And a dream that does not end is an infinite you will never lose. Even if you are killed within a Dream, so long as you paid an initial cost to initiate it, you can return even from collapse within that dream.|
Noah’s eyes blazed with blue-gold light!

This was it! He had spent his whole life carrying an infinite that was never truly his, an inherited definition of a thing he could not grasp, and now, at last, he held an infinite that belonged only to him, because he had stopped trying to hold it and had learned instead to Dream it.
And he felt like this was only the tip of the iceberg as if he was able to understand that edge even more, that impossibility...even more wonders would unfold!
But for now...

His Infinite Dreams could now run without end! A reverie could be stretched toward true forever! The 75-Provenance Infinite Dream he had opened to sit among the Immense Ones, the sanctuary of clouds, the stretched instant he stood in right now with Calliope frozen before him, all of it could now be extended without any wall at all!
And more! For if a dream need never end, then the power gained within a dream, the growth, the guiding, the authoring, all of it could compound across a dreaming that had no close.

His existence buzzed with the enormity of it, and somewhere far down he undertood that he had not merely learned a trick! He had changed what Infinity meant to him, and in changing the meaning, he had made the infinite finally, truly his!
The Runestone had said a path would light up before one who reached a definition of their own.

Noah could feel it now, faint and distant, somewhere at the edge of his newly infinite dreaming, a path beginning to glow, a road the stone had promised, leading somewhere unknown even to the stone itself.
He wouldn’t even need to gaze upon this stone again to try and follow that road as it had shown him what it had.
But that was for later.

For now, in a frozen instant that he could stretch toward forever, in a sanctuary of blue-gold clouds, with an obsidian Runestone at her back and her eyes shining brighter than ever, Calliope leaned in toward the man who had just walked out of a memory changed, and she opened her mouth to ask him what in all of existence he had just seen...!

chapters.title: Chapter 5746: A Grand Mythos! I
paragraphs: Noah looked at Calliope who was calm and expectant in the blue-gold clouds, and he answered her at last.
"I learned about Lucy,"he said. "And infinity."
Calliope’s eyes went wide!
"Huh! Really?"She leaned in delighted.

"Little Lucy showed me the impossibilities of stories. The walls I could never write past, the doors that only open one way. But you saw something else entirely! I suppose each of us sees a different thing in the same old stone. Isn’t that just the loveliest proof that a story is never truly finished?"
She clapped her ink-stained hands together once. "Okay! I have given you something now, so it is your turn. It is time for you to reciprocate!"

She waved a hand, and the massive obsidian Hieroglyph Runestone sank slowly back down into the blue-gold clouds of Noah’s sanctuary, folding away into wherever the Writer of Mythos kept the truest thing she owned, until only the two authors remained in the endless soft light.
And then she made her proposal!

"I want to write the ultimate subversion, Dreamer,"she said, and her voice dropped into something reverent and mad all at once. "The one Mythos the rule has always forbidden me. I want to write THE Vestige of THE Fallen Hero."
Noah’s masked existence pulsed!

"But you understand a thing like that does not come cheap," Calliope went on, pacing now through the clouds. "For the myth I have in mind, it takes more than ink! It takes an ocean of sovereign vitality. And it takes a hammer of pure Provenance to drive the whole sentence down through the weavings of this Train until existence has no choice but to agree!"
She turned, and she looked directly at Noah’s blue-gold manifestation, and her eyes glittered!

"I have the syntax. I have an unalterable page, a truth that cannot be edited. But my blood belongs to the Matriarch, and the Matriarch is bound to their frameworks, chained to the very authorities we would be defying! My ink can shape the story. It cannot pay the debt."Her voice sharpened to a point.
"But you? You carry blood that owes nothing to anyone, do you not? Blood generated from your own origin, answering to no one in all of existence!"
She held out her hand across the space between them. "So lend me your power. Give me your red ink."
Noah calculated the trade in a single stretched instant.

To do this was to unleash his foundation in the open, and unleashing his foundation in the open risked drawing the gazes of Immense Ones down onto his masked position at last! It was the great danger, the one he had spent this whole dream avoiding!
And yet...
His Dream was Infinite now.

Even if the seven turned their full gazes upon him, even if their combined weight shredded his existence to nothing in an instant, it would not end him, because he had learned to dream a dream with no far wall, and even death within that dream was not death.
He had paid to open it. He could return from a collapse inside it!
His Tyranny rose in him and Sonder tempered it into something quieter and more certain, and the two together weighed the challenge and found it entirely... acceptable.
Prompts bloomed across his sight.
|COLLABORATIVE SOVEREIGN AUTHORSHIP PROPOSED.|
|Syntactic Architect: CALLIOPE, THE WRITER OF MYTHOS.|
|Sovereign Fuel and Anchor: NOAH OSMONT, THE HUMAN DREAMER.|
|Target Inscription: THE VESTIGE OF THE FALLEN HERO.|
|Required Medium: A SHARD OF VAKOCHEV.|
A Shard of Vakochev?
And then Calliope reached into her existence and produced a thing, and Noah’s masked eye locked onto it in pure astonishment, because he recognized it!

It was a Shard, jagged and cold and old, and it carried a weaving Noah knew intimately, because it was the earliest version of his own Shard that he himself held! This woman, this bored and bleeding Descendant of ink, held in her hand a fragment of Vakochev that was left behind after his proclamation to those...like him.
And she wrapped it in ink, and she began to write!
"Your weavings," Calliope breathed, her concentration absolute. "Give them to me!"
Noah breathed out and unleashed his foundation as he was now...entirely curious. What exactly could she accomplish?

From his blue-gold manifestation a sea of Infinite Sanguine Mana cascaded downward, crimson and gold and boundless, an ocean of self-generated vitality that had no bottom and no end, pouring out of him in a flood that lit the whole sanctuary!
The crimson-gold tide flooded into Calliope’s open codex.

It saturated the pages, soaked into the paper, ran along every line and coatted her black ink until it glistened, ink and Sanguine Mana and Provenance fusing into a single writing-fluid that shone like blood held up to a fire. Every stroke she would make now carried the weight of an existence that owed nothing to anyone.
Calliope laughed!

Her eyes flared with a mad, ecstatic focus as the boundless vitality of Noah’s origin surged through her fingers, filling a well that had been running dry, and she bent to the page, and she wrote, her strokes driven now by the unyielding hammer of Noah’s Provenance behind every letter!
"THE Vestige of THE Fallen Hero,"she wrote, and spoke the words as she carved them, "does not ask the sky for permission to stand!"
And Noah watched brilliantly as he activated THE Meta-Fictional Protagonist Mantle.

He forced his narrative dominance down into the glistening ink, into the sentence taking shape upon the page, and he declared it, declared the written words to be an absolute, un-deletable fact of the immediate domain, a truth that existence was not permitted to argue with!

The whole sanctuary buzzed with the collision of two authorships and an un-editable page, and Noah felt the enormity of what they were writing, and he knew, with magisterial certainty, that he could not hold this.
The stretched instant was already fraying at its edges, the frozen moment beginning to thaw, the dream unable to contain a working this vast for more than a breath.
The instant broke!
BOOM!
And externally, across the whole Cluster of Dimensions, everything went dead silent!

The stretched instant was already fraying at its edges, the frozen moment beginning to thaw, the dream unable to contain a working this vast for more than a breath.
The instant broke!
BOOM!
And externally, across the whole Cluster of Dimensions, everything went dead silent!

chapters.title: Chapter 5747: A Grand Mythos! II
paragraphs: The screaming sea stopped. The falling arrows hung. The pale chains stilled. The smell of scorched starlight and old ozone that had hung over the underworld vanished all at once, replaced by something older and heavier, the suffocating scent of ancient volcanic Source, thick and primordial and wrong for this age!

And deep within the core of the Train, through the Dimensional Cabins, echoed a sound that did not belong to anything living now, the sound of colossal, iridescent scales shifting against iron, something vast turning over in a place it had no right to even be!
|SOVEREIGN COLLABORATIVE INSCRIPTION COMPLETE.|
|Syntax: THE VESTIGE OF THE FALLEN HERO.|
|You have ushered and aided in the emergence of an Unfathomable Narrative.|
|+35 PROVENANCE. +15 VERITAS. +15 PONDUS. +25 OSMONTIAN MOIRAI.|
Upon Calliope’s actual body, down in the burning Cluster, a single page rose.

It lifted off her and expanded, and it expanded for Gigaparsecs, a sheet of writing wider than Dimensions, hanging over the underworld like a second sky! And then it did not dissolve, and it did not burn away.
It OPENED! Like an iron gate swinging wide on ancient hinges!
And rising up out of the page came a COFFIN!
A coffin!

A massive obsidian coffin, black as the space between things, ascending slowly out of the opened page, and the whole Cluster of Dimensions held its breath as the lid began, with a grinding finality, to lift.
Obsidian flames spilled out first, pouring from the seams of the coffin, and then the thing inside it rose.

It...was not perceivable! Noah stared and the weavings of existence could not resolve it, could not draw it, could give him nothing but the shape of the obsidian flames that wrapped it, a humanoid silhouette of pure dark fire standing where a body should be, terrible and vast and impossible.
But Noah knew what it was, knew it in the weavings of his frozen existence, because the weavings that poured off it were the same weavings he had felt on a Shard.
The physical, terrifying Remnant of Vakochev!
Noah looked upon it in astonishment, unable to move his masked eye, and down below, everything stopped.
The Infinity Eater stopped bleeding. The Champion stopped rebelling. The Sealed One’s Vessel stopped its suppression of THE Creature. Adrastia looked up solemnly.

Every hunter, every prey, every collapsed and swirling thing in the whole cluster of underworlds went utterly still, and they all looked UP, at the obsidian coffin and the fire-wrapped titan rising from it, in pure astonishment.
What...had THE Writer of Mythos done?!
Just what, in all of existence, had she written?
And the watching Immense Ones erupted at this time.
The gazes of the Immense Ones blazed, and their weavings crashed across the sky, cold and grand and arrogant, arriving one atop another!
|THE SLEEPLESS FIEND observes the fire-wrapped Remnant, and is amused.|
|"You have brought out another part of your body to die? Good. I did not enjoy killing parts of you the first time as much as I should have."|
|THE OVERSEEING ONE recoils. This was not written into his Narrative. A Descendant has authored something he did not permit.|
|"Impossible. A measly Descendant of ink, raising THAT? Who lent her the hand? WHO?"|
|THE UNPAID COLLECTOR studies the Shard-weavings with cold, greedy interest.|
|"That is his true remnant. Not a memory. Not a ghost. Oh boy..."|
|THE GLOATING JAILER counsels caution.|
|"Careful, brethren. We buried this one for a reason. Twice-buried is a Narrative I do not wish to author a third time."|
|THE CACKLING BUTCHER is delighted. THE STARVING CONNOISSEUR, for the first time in an age, is not bored...|
And through all of it, the fire-wrapped Remnant of Vakochev did not react.

He did not look at Calliope who had written him, and he did not look down at the dying underworld beneath his feet. Slowly, deliberately, with the terrible calm of a being who had already died once and found nothing in death worth fearing, the Remnant turned his head UPWARD!
His gaze locked directly onto the observation gallery.
Directly onto the Immense Ones who had slaughtered him an unknown time ago!
Vakochev raised his right arm.
And he swung it, once, horizontally, across the whole span of the tracks of the Dimensional Provenance Train!

His Dimensionality was so unfathomably, monstrously high that in the instant of the swing he vanished from the perception of every existence present, hunters and prey alike, gone from all sight as the movement outpaced the ability of the weavings to hold him.
There was...no explosion!
There was no blast, no fire, no eruption of force!
There was only the sound of reality parting along an unstitched seam, a single clean and terrible sound, as THE Dimensional Provenance Train SPLIT CLEANLY IN TWO!
BOOM!

The residual force of that swing rolled outward in a wave, and Noah, hanging masked at the edge of the gallery, was directly in its path, far too close to the Immense Ones, far too close to the parting of the Train itself.
And it eviscerated him!
The residual wave shredded his masked existence in an instant, tearing his eye apart, unmaking his dreaming presence, obliterating the whole of him where he hung as an eye.
Before, before the forest and the stone and the definition he had made his own, this would have ended him completely, would have collapsed his existence and killed him for good.
But his Dream...was Infinite now.
|Your presence within an Infinite Dream has been destroyed.|
|An Infinite Dream does not end, even in death. The initial cost was paid. You return.|
Noah’s eye reformed!

It bloomed back into existence at the edge of the sky, whole and masked and watching, his dreaming presence stitched back together out of the very dream that could not end, and he gazed out upon what he had helped to make with an existence that had just died and come back.
The other eyes of the Immense Ones buzzed and blazed in fury and shock all around the split, their gazes whipping across the two halves of the sundered Train.
|THE Dimensional Provenance Train has been cleaved and brought to a halt.|
And down in the burning, dying Cluster, upon her own bleeding body, THE Writer of Mythos threw back her head and LAUGHED!

Blood leaked from her nose and ran from the corner of her mouth, painting her chin red, her reserves spent, her ink run dry, her whole existence trembling from the price she had paid, and she laughed and laughed with a wild and ecstatic joy.
"Oh, now THIS," Calliope gasped through the blood, her eyes shining with mad delight, "now this can be considered a Mythos worth observing!"

chapters.title: Chapter 5748: You Freed Me!
paragraphs: Vakochev floated upon the sundered weavings of the Dimensional Provenance Train, and the space around him was no longer space.

The cleaving of the Train had unmade the very definition of the region, and where reality had been there was now only undefinition, a churning obsidian foam that filled everything, existence itself boilng where the seam had parted! And within that foam the Remnant hung, wrapped in his obsidian flames, a silhouette of dark fire standing at the center of a wound in creation, unhurried, unbothered, waiting!
And at the edge of the breach, The Immense Ones gathered!

They came, and they were not entirely perceivable, because beings such as these did not fit inside the sight of anything lesser! At one moment they were massive eyes hanging in the dark, and the next they were gone entirely, present only as pressure, as weight, as a wrongness in the boiling foam.

THE SLEEPLESS FIEND stepped forward, his form an undulating silhouette of brilliance that would not rest, flanked by the gathered gazes of THE OVERSEEING ONE, THE UNPAID COLLECTOR, THE GLOATING JAILER, THE CACKLING BUTCHER, and THE STARVING CONNOISSEUR!
A chilling silence gripped the void!
And into that silence, Vakochev spoke!

His voice did not rumble with theatrical rage. It did not roar or thunder or shake the foam. It carried instead the cold, measured cadence of a man presenting a failure to the ones responsible for it.
The obsidian flames turned slowly around him!

"Across uncounted epochs, you who Remain have extinguished decillions of living beings. Whole Observable Existences and Dimensions, pulverized to nothing. Whole civilizations, ancient and striving and full of small warm lives, harvested down to the bone for a portion of their weavings, their entire histories reduced to a resource and then to silt."

His voice never rose. "And you wrote every one of those deaths into your weavings as meaningless. Unworthy of a second thought. Dust swept from a floor. Decillions upon decillions, and not one of them was ever weighed as anything at all."
He looked from one indistinct gaze to the next.

"And yet. If a single one of you were to bleed. If one Immense One, one, were to die here today, every one of you would shake with hysterical horror! You would call it an impossible crime! You would name it an atrocity against the whole of Existence and hunt the cause of it across every age until the end of things."
The foam boiled around the Remnant.

"So tell me, by what weaving is this measured? By what law is the life of a mortal who owns no borrowed authority weighed as lesser than one of you? Show me the reckoning. Show me the line in existence that says a striving thing with no crown is worth decillions-to-one against a thing like you."

His dead quiet eyes swept them. "You cannot. Because it does not exist. Existence itself does not recognize your hierarchy. Only your violence does. You did not discover that you were worth more. You decided it, and then you killed everything that might have argued."
THE SLEEPLESS FIEND answered him.
The Fiend spoke with terrifying scale, with an absolute and sterile condescension that made the foam itself seem to cringe, and there was no anger in it at all.
|A mountain does not hold council with the gravel beneath its base.|
|The lung does not ask permission of the air it consumes.|

|You speak of a reckoning, little ghost, as though the weak and the mighty were entries in the same book. They are not. Those without authority, or with less of it, are not a lesser party to a negotiation. They are scenery. Backdrop. The texture against which the real story unfolds.|
Existence writhed!

|You misunderstand what an Immense One is, and you always did, which is why you died the first time. An Immense One does not merely live within the architecture of existence. An Immense One IS the architecture. And you would have us weigh the scaffold against the dust swept out the door as though they were equals?|
The Fiend’s threads gathered into something almost like a face, and it looked upon Vakochev with a contempt colder than the void!
|That is the delusion of a peasant who discovered how to strike a spark, and in the striking, believed he had invented the sun.|
Vakochev looked at the Fiend with dead quiet eyes!
He did not flinch, and he did not argue the point, because he had not come to win a debate! He had come to correct a record!
"You slaughtered many of my weavings," Vakochev said, and now his voice changed, went lower and more terrible, though it still carried no rage.
"You broke all of it because you told yourselves a story about it and you believed the story."
The obsidian flames flared!

"You believed that if you stripped away everything I loved, you would break my will. That grief would bring me to my knees. That a being with nothing left to protect would beg, or bend, or surrender the road I walked."His dead eyes did not blink. "You thought my loves were the handles by which you could steer me."
He spread his fire-wrapped arms slowly!
"But you did not break me. You freed me. You...freed me."
HUUM!
Vakochev delivered a vow.

"So here is what I will do today," he said, quiet as the grave he had risen from."I am going to look upon an Immense One with the exact same gaze you have cast upon the weak since the beginning of things. The careless gaze. The indifferent one. The gaze that does not even bother to weigh what it is destroying."
He looked at the Fiend, and at the gathered gazes, and for the first time something moved behind his dead eyes, and it was not hatred, and it was not grief!
It was indifference!
"I am going to treat your existence," Vakochev said, "as common cattle."
The debate ended, and it ended with the total collapse of local dimensional existenceas...Vakochev MOVED!
Oh, he moved.

His speed exceeded all perception, exceeded Seam-tier sight and Hem-tier sight and everything beneath, and he did not traverse the space between himself and the Fiend, because traversal was for lesser things! He simply forced the coordinate to arrive beneath his boots, willed the destination to become where he already was, and the distance ceased to be relevant.
The clash of Dimensionality detonated across the severed Train.
And the gathered Immense Ones unleashed their combined authority all at once, and as they did, the faint weavings of their eyes vanished from all perception entirely.

Their actions and their power left the realm of the perceivable completely, a war fought at an altitude no lesser existence could witness, the foam itself screaming as titans beyond sight collided within it!
Below, survival became a lottery.

The shockwaves alone, the mere residual ripples of the clash far above, shattered existence for vast spans! Lesser Descendants on the nearby Cabins were flattened into paste before they could draw a single breath, whole ranks of them unmade by a war they could not even see, dying to the backwash of a battle happening somewhere beyond their comprehension.
Down below, amid the shattering, the figure of Calliope appeared!

She rose from the wreckage of her own bleeding body, and she wiped the blood from her face with the back of an ink-stained hand, and she looked up at the churning foam where titans warred beyond sight, and she smiled with pure, radiant fascination.
"Now this," she breathed, her eyes shining. "This is a grand story. Okay!"

And around her, seas of Existential Narrative began to wrap, layer upon layer, a cocoon of authored protection descending over the Writer of Mythos, as THE MATRIARCH OF INK moved at last to shield her Descendant from the storm she had unleashed.
At the rim of it all, Noah tried to see!

He tried to observe the core exchange, the true clash between Vakochev and the Immense Ones, and he could not, because the density of the colliding authorities was blinding, a wall of pure destruction that his sight could not pierce.
And so he reached for the thing he had just made his own.
Infinity!

He thought of it, his own definition, his dream with no far wall, and he conjured a grand and impossible vision within his mind, a dream of a gaze that could stretch forever, an eye that could open onto a vista with no horizon and no edge, a seeing that simply did not stop.

He infused his Provenance with that definition, poured his infinite dreaming into the single act of looking, because he wanted, more than almost anything, to see what a risen Fallen Hero did to the ones who killed him!
He wanted to see!
But even an infinite gaze caught only fragments.
The clash was beyond the threshold where any mind, even his, could assemble the data into a picture.

He caught disjointed, terrifying pieces, flashes torn out of a chaos too vast to hold! An arm tearing clean through a curtain of Dimensionality! The sound of a jaw breaking, somewhere, alongside a roar that had no source he could find! The silhouette of the obsidian coffin, drifting serene and empty through storms of pure and endless Source.
Fragments, only fragments, consequences without their causes, the aftermath of blows he could not perceive being struck.
Then a stray ripple of the Overseeing One’s Dimensionality clipped his masked eye!

The pressure was catastrophic, a mere edge of a mere ripple of one Immense One’s power, and it was enough! Noah’s dreaming form VAPORIZED in a fraction of a nanosecond, unmade before he could even register the touch!
|Presence destroyed. THE INFINITE DREAM remains active. Reconstitution initiated.|
Noah reformed instantly at the perimeter.

And he did not release a single thread of offensive intent! He refused, absolutely, to draw attention, to flare with power, to do anything at all but hang there and watch, a quiet masked eye at the rim of an apocalypse.
Within three seconds a second shockwave, this one from the Fiend’s Dimensionality, tore him apart again.
Noah reconstituted a second time!

And then a third, his eye blooming back into being again and again at the edge of the storm, persisting, immovable, a silent witness who could be destroyed a thosand times and would simply keep returning, watching, saying nothing, doing nothing, refusing to be anything but present.
High in the chaos, two gazes noticed him!
|THE CACKLING BUTCHER observes the masked presence at the rim, destroyed and reformed thrice over.|
|"Ha! Look at this little thing. Blown to nothing and back again, and again. What a stubborn, useless Immensity it has."|
|THE GLOATING JAILER regards him with mild, dismissive interest.|
|"Some eccentric from a backwater domain, come to gawk. No weapon drawn. No Immensity raised. No intent to strike. He is nothing. Leave him to flicker."|

They saw no weapons and no flaring Immensity and no attempt to strike, and so they dismissed him entirely, an eccentric and weak peer from some forgotten corner of existence who happened to possess an irritating immortality technique and not a scrap of combative relevance.
And Noah, dying and returning, dying and returning, let them believe exactly that.
Because he was not here to fight!
He was here to SEE!
