She rose from the wreckage of her own bleeding body, and she wiped the blood from her face with the back of an ink-stained hand, and she looked up at the churning foam where titans warred beyond sight, and she smiled with pure, radiant fascination.
"Now this," she breathed, her eyes shining.
"This is a grand story.
Okay!"

And around her, seas of Existential Narrative began to wrap, layer upon layer, a cocoon of authored protection descending over the Writer of Mythos, as THE MATRIARCH OF INK moved at last to shield her Descendant from the storm she had unleashed.
At the rim of it all, Noah tried to see!

He tried to observe the core exchange, the true clash between Vakochev and the Immense Ones, and he could not, because the density of the colliding authorities was blinding, a wall of pure destruction that his sight could not pierce.
And so he reached for the thing he had just made his own.
Infinity!

He thought of it, his own definition, his dream with no far wall, and he conjured a grand and impossible vision within his mind, a dream of a gaze that could stretch forever, an eye that could open onto a vista with no horizon and no edge, a seeing that simply did not stop.

He infused his Provenance with that definition, poured his infinite dreaming into the single act of looking, because he wanted, more than almost anything, to see what a risen Fallen Hero did to the ones who killed him!
He wanted to see!
But even an infinite gaze caught only fragments.
The clash was beyond the threshold where any mind, even his, could assemble the data into a picture.
He caught disjointed, terrifying pieces, flashes torn out of a chaos too vast to hold!
An arm tearing clean through a curtain of Dimensionality!
The sound of a jaw breaking, somewhere, alongside a roar that had no source he could find!
The silhouette of the obsidian coffin, drifting serene and empty through storms of pure and endless Source.
Fragments, only fragments, consequences without their causes, the aftermath of blows he could not perceive being struck.
Then a stray ripple of the Overseeing One’s Dimensionality clipped his masked eye!
The pressure was catastrophic, a mere edge of a mere ripple of one Immense One’s power, and it was enough!
Noah’s dreaming form VAPORIZED in a fraction of a nanosecond, unmade before he could even register the touch!
|Presence destroyed.
THE INFINITE DREAM remains active.
Reconstitution initiated.|
Noah reformed instantly at the perimeter.
And he did not release a single thread of offensive intent!
He refused, absolutely, to draw attention, to flare with power, to do anything at all but hang there and watch, a quiet masked eye at the rim of an apocalypse.
Within three seconds a second shockwave, this one from the Fiend’s Dimensionality, tore him apart again.
Noah reconstituted a second time!

And then a third, his eye blooming back into being again and again at the edge of the storm, persisting, immovable, a silent witness who could be destroyed a thosand times and would simply keep returning, watching, saying nothing, doing nothing, refusing to be anything but present.
High in the chaos, two gazes noticed him!
|THE CACKLING BUTCHER observes the masked presence at the rim, destroyed and reformed thrice over.|
|"Ha!
Look at this little thing.
Blown to nothing and back again, and again.
What a stubborn, useless Immensity it has."|
|THE GLOATING JAILER regards him with mild, dismissive interest.|
|"Some eccentric from a backwater domain, come to gawk.
No weapon drawn.
No Immensity raised.
No intent to strike.
He is nothing.
Leave him to flicker."|

They saw no weapons and no flaring Immensity and no attempt to strike, and so they dismissed him entirely, an eccentric and weak peer from some forgotten corner of existence who happened to possess an irritating immortality technique and not a scrap of combative relevance.
And Noah, dying and returning, dying and returning, let them believe exactly that.
Because he was not here to fight!
He was here to SEE!

chapters.title: Chapter 5749: The Long Night I
paragraphs: In the heart of the storm, Vakochev chose his target.

He ignored the Sleepless Fiend’s bindings entirely, let the white-hot threads scrape uselessly across his obsidian flames, and drove his path straight toward one gaze and one gaze alone. He went for THE OVERSEEING ONE.
And THE OVERSEEING ONE panicked.

For cycles uncounted, this one had sat in comfort behind protective glass, reaching down to manipulate the small tragedies of mortals, staging their sorrows for his own amusement, arranging their doomed little stories and never once bleeding for any of it! He had authored a decillion deaths from a balcony and paid for none!
Now the glass was gone!

Now the protagonist of his worst and most recent failure, the risen Remnant of the one Narrative he could never fully bury, was coming straight for him through a storm no lesser thing could witness, and there was no railing to lean over and no script to hide behind.
Far at the rim, Noah tried desperately to see!

He poured his infinite gaze into the storm, strained his dreaming sight against the wall of colliding authority, and he caught only fractions, only slivers, disjointed pieces of a thing too vast to hold.
The suggestion of a lunge! A curtain of Dimensionality torn aside! A shape closing on a shape! Fragments, always fragments, the storm too dense and too high for even an infinite eye to pierce.
But he saw enough to know that Vakochev had reached him.
Vakochev’s hands closed around THE OVERSEEING ONE’s throat!
And the coffin answered.

The single obsidian coffin that had risen from Calliope’s page transformed in an instant into INFINITE coffins, countless obsidian caskets unfolding out of one another and wrapping around the two combatants, sealing them together inside an existential grave, a tomb of endless black boxes that closed over the architect and the ghost and shut the rest of existence out!
And inside that grave, the struggle was brutal.
It was unadorned! It was utterly devoid of majesty! There was no grand engineering here, no cascade of complex weavings, no dazzling display of a titan’s full art!

In the barely-perceivable dark of those infinite coffins, Vakochev simply HELD the thrashing architect, gripped him with the exact cold, dismissive strength of a butcher holding a squealing pig over a drainage trough, indifferent to its terror, unbothered by its struggle, waiting only for the moment to do the necessary thing!
And then he did the necessary thing.
With a sharp, concussive twist of his wrists, Vakochev snapped THE OVERSEEING ONE’s neck!

And as he did, unknown seas of THE Primordial Source and raw Dimensionality poured out of the Remnant and INTO the dying architect, flooding him, drowning him from within with something that even Noah, straining every fiber of his infinite gaze, could not perceive!
Whatever Vakochev truly did in that instant, whatever authority he drove into his enemy along with the killing twist, it happened behind a veil that no eye present could lift.
CRACK!
THE OVERSEEING ONE’s scream shattered across the whole of the Dimensional Skies!

His chest cavity caved inward, collapsing as though a hand the size of an existence had closed on it! His eyes burst into blinding silver light, and out of that light his stolen records began to unravel, ages of harvested history spilling out of him and coming apart.

And Vakochev, holding the ruined and screaming thing, drew back a fire-wrapped fist and drove it into the dying architect’s skull, extinguishing his Trueness completely, snuffing the last of what he was!
THE OVERSEEING ONE died.
An architect had FALLEN!
Vakochev dropped the limp corpse!

It fell away into the infinite coffins, a dead Immense One, a thing that was never supposed to be possible, and the Remnant turned his dead quiet gaze upon the stunned, indistinct faces of the Immense Ones who remained.
And he spoke a single word into the ringing silence, a quiet and terrible parting sentence.
"One."
Then Vakochev stepped backward into the unstitched void.
His fire-wrapped body dissolved into the cracks of Existence itself, sinking into the seams his own swing had torn, vanishing back into the wound in creation from which he had come.
And THE SLEEPLESS FIEND roated in fury!

The white-hot threads erupted, and the Fiend surged into the dark after the vanishing Remnant, and THE UNPAID COLLECTOR surged with him, and THE CACKLING BUTCHER too, three of the mightiest gazes in existence plunging into the cracks in violent, howling pursuit of the ghost who had just killed one of their own!
An Immense One had been killed!

Noah gazed upon the impossible from the rim, his masked existence rigid with astonishment, and around him many other perceptions did the same! Was Vakochev truly so grand? Truly so terrible that a mere Remnant of him, a Vestige written back into being by a bleeding Descendant’s pen, could reach into the gathered Immense Ones and simply snap the neck of one?
But even as Noah and all the others reeled with that thought...
Existence itself began to shake!
|The historical mass of a fallen architect does not vanish cleanly.|
|An Immense One’s weavings and folded dimensions have begun an immediate, uncontrolled gravitational collapse...|
The whole region trembled and groaned, and the collapse of the dead architect’s immense volume rippled outward, and existence shuddered around them all!
It looked like something was about to happen to the corpse of the Immense One.
Some process was about to start due to this death.
But...it was interrupted. Or more aptly, it was superseded.
Because in the very next instant, something happened that had not happened before in all of existence.

Every single existence present that held any access to authority, any weaving at all capable of communicating with the surrounding fabric of existence, which was to say every being grand enough to perceive the changes rippling through reality, received a message.

It came in a language older than any tongue, older than agreement itself, and yet every one of them understood it inherently, understood it the way a body understands that the air around it has grown warmer, not through translation but through sensation, a direct communication between a living thing and existence itself.
And the message that every perceiving existence received in that moment, felt in the core of their weavings, was this!
|All conditions have been fulfilled.|
All conditions have been fulfilled?

What conditions? What conditions had been set, and by whom, and when, and what did their fulfillment mean? Noah’s mind raced, grasping at a thing with no handle, a message from existence itself with no context and no source and no...
HUUM!
Right after, Noah’s manifestation in that space began to SHIVER!
He blinked, confused, and he looked up, and...
Snow began to fall!
Snow?!

Noah stared upward in disbelief as, out of the murky obsidian foam, out of the churning undefinition all around, snow came drifiting down! A storm of it! White flakes descending in their countless millions across the boiling dark, falling over the shattered remnants of the Dimensional Provenance Train, over the sundered Cabins that stretched away for Gigaparsecs, settling upon the wreckage of a battle beyond perception.
A blizzard, blooming into being across a region of existence that had never known such a thing.
It did not stem from the dead Immense One as much as...it seemed to stem from Existence itself!
And the descent of that snow came with a terrible coldness.
It wrapped over everyone, over everything, a cold that sank past skin and past weaving and into the very substanace of an existence, and Noah himself, hanging masked at the rim, truly felt it.
Cold!
For the first time in what seemed like forever, Noah Osmont felt cold!

How could he feel cold? He, who had bathed in scorching springs and endured the torture of Immense Ones and walked out of the collapse of his own dream. How could a drifting flake of snow reach past all of that and touch him with a chill?
And it was not only him! It was not only the cold!
Prompts bloomed across his sight, and they were not comforting!
|Your existence is being affected by an unknown weaving, established across existence as an EXISTENTIAL CONDITION.|
|Source: unknown. Scope: pervasive. This Condition is spreading.|
|THE CONDITION OF THE DESCENDING COLD:|
|All attributes are being suppressed. All authority is being slowed, dimmed, and made heavy.|
|The suppression scales with the authority held. The mightier the existence, the deeper the cold reaches, and the more it takes.|
|Those who hold the most are affected the most...|
Those who held the most were affected the MOST?
Noah read those words with a chill that had nothing to do with the snow, because he understood, dimly, the shape of what that meant.
A cold... that hunted power? A weather that fell hardest upon the mighty? A Condition that would press lightest on a peasant and crush hardest upon an Immense One?
And below him, layer upon layer of white snow descended.

It fell upon the burning Cluster of underworlds! It fell upon Calliope, who looked up at it with a somber frown, her fascination gone quiet, and shivered where she stood inside the Matriarch’s protection.
Far in the distance, even THE Creature shivered, the coldness wrapping around his titanic frame, and his obsidian-white flames flickered, dimming, guttering against a chill they had never met!

And further still, THE SEALED ONE raised his hands, and around his Vessel a storm of snow circled and howled, frost creeping across everything he was, ice climbing the edges of a being who had walked across existence untouched by anything, now touched at last by a cold that did not care what he had conquered!
A catastrophe had begun.

At this moment, no one understood why! No one understood how! No one could name the conditions that had been fulfilled or the hand that had set them or the weaving that now fell as snow across the murky dark.
But it was pervasive.
And it was occurring across the whole of Existence!

chapters.title: Chapter 5750: The Long Night II
paragraphs: Far beneath the war of titans, far beneath the dying architect and the cracking Train and the murky obsidian foam, in a small Universe folded inside a small Observable Existence, upon a small world that had never once heard the name of an Immense One or any glimpses of authority, there was a desert.
And in that desert, there was a fire!

Around the fire sat a tribe, men and women and children wrapped in the hides of desert beasts, their brown faces lit warm and orange by the flames, and they sat close together against the cool of the night and they listened.
For it was the hour of stories, and the Wisewoman had begun to speak.

She was old, older than anyone could remember being young, her hands like knotted roots and her eyes like two dark wells that had seen every star wheel across the sky a thousand times. She sat at the head of the fire, and her voice was low and worn and beautiful, and she told the story that had been told at this fire since before her grandmother’s grandmother had first heard it!
"Listen now," the Wisewoman said, "and remember, for a story remembered is a life saved. I will tell you of The Long Night."
The children leaned in.

"There will come a time," she said, "long foretold and long feared, when the world turns cold. When the warmth that has always been simply begins to leave, first from the edges of things, and then from the heart of them. When a coldness that no fire can answer permeates the desert and the sea and the high places and the low, creeping into the sand and the water and the very breath in your chest."
The fire crackled, and the shadows danced!

"And in that time," she went on, her old eyes moving across the ring of faces, "the night will grow long. Not one night, but a night that does not end, a darkness that stretches on and on past every dawn that should have come, until the sun itself seems to forget the way back. This is The Long Night. When the cold comes and the night will not lift. And the old stories say that when it comes, all the world must huddle close, and wrap itself in every warmth it has hoarded, and endure, and wait, and hope that the dawn remembers us at the end."
Then a child rose up!
He was a small boy, bold and bright-eyed, and he stood at the edge of the fire with his little chin lifted, and he pointed at the old woman as snot leaked from his nose.

"Wisewoman!" he said. "I know why you tell us this! You only tell it to make us afraid, so that we behave and stay close to the fire! But this story has never come true, not once, not for all the generations! My father heard it, and his father, and his father’s father, and the night has always ended and the sun has always come back! It is only a story to frighten little snotty children!"
Some of the adults chuckled softly, and a few frowned at the boy’s boldness, but the Wisewoman only smiled!
She smiled at him with all the patience of her long years, and she opened her mouth to answer him, to tell him gently that a story does not need to have come true to be worth the keeping...
And then she blinked!
For she had felt something!

Something small and cold and impossible had landed upon the withered skin of her cheek, a tiny pinprick of chill in the warm desert night, and she paused, her smile faltering, and she raised one old knotted hand and touched her face and drew it back and looked at it.
And there, melting upon the dark root of her fingertip, was a snowflake.
A snowflake!
The Wisewoman stared at it, and her ancient heart went still!

And a moment later, another fell! And another! And then more, and more, drifting down out of the black desert sky in their impossible countless numbers, white flakes descending upon a land that had never in all its histroy known a single one, settling on the sand, on the hides, on the upturned faces of the tribe as one by one they felt the cold touch and looked UP!
Snow!
Snow was falling in the desert!

A ripple of shock ran through the tribe, and then of fear, and then of a horror that had no words! The children cried out! The men surged to their feet! The women clutched their little ones close! They stared up at the falling white as it thickened, as the warm orange firelight caught the drifting flakes and turned them to sparks of gold falling out of the endless dark, beautiful and terrible, a thing that should not be, a thing that could not be, falling and falling upon a desert that had known only sun and heat since the world began.
And the bold boy who had stood to mock the story stood frozen now, his little face turned upward, a snowflake melting on his cheek, his eyes wide with a terror he could not name.
The Wisewoman trembled!

Her old body shook, and for a moment she was only an old and frightened woman under a sky that had broken its oldest promise. But then her eyes shone, because she was the Wisewoman, and she carried the story, and the story had a second half that was not for frightening children but for saving them.
For generations, they had prepared.
She rose from her place at the fire!

She moved through the tribe, through the crying and the shouting and the upturned faces, moving with a purpose that stilled them as she passed, and she went to one hut at the edge of the circle, an old hut, a hut the children had always been told never to open.
And she opened it!

Inside, stacked and waiting, were furs! Thick hides and heavy woven things, layers upon layers of warmth, gathered and cured and stored accross untold generations by keepers of the story who had never once seen them used.
Warmth hoarded for a night that had never come, waiting patient in the dark for the day the old woman’s smile would falter and a snowflake would land upon her cheek!
The Wisewoman turned back to her people!

She looked upon the men and the women and the frightened children beneath the falling snow, and she spoke, and her worn old voice carried across the whole trembling tribe with the weight of every generation that had kept the tale alive!

"Come," she said. "Come now, all of you, and wrap yourselves in layers of protection. Take the furs your fathers’ fathers saved for you and cover yourselves against the cold, and gather close, and do not let the fire die!"
She held the old hut open, and the snow fell past her into the warm firelight, and her shining eyes swept them all!
"The Long Night... has come."
Deep within THE Infiniverse, in a Realm folded inside the Helios Elsedimension, the sun hung warm and golden over a beach of soft golden sand, and no one there had a single worry in all of existence.
For this was the safest place there was.

This was inside the very heart of THE True Human Emperor’s own empire, a domain sealed away from every gaze and every hunter and every architect, a paradise where the sheltered lived their sheltered lives and wanted for nothing.
Elizabeth reclined upon a beach chair near the shimmering water, and she was at ease.

She had been someone of power once, back in Noah’s homeworld, a figure of standing in the days before he had cleared away every threat that world held and departed for The Beast World and beyond. She had crossed paths with him in The Blessed Empire, and now she dwelled here, in comfort, in safety, one of the countless souls the Emperor had gathered under his boundless wing.

Above her, a great eagle wheeled slow and lazy across the golden sky, and up and down the beach, other humans went about their peaceful business, walking the sand, floating in the bright shallows, dozing in the sun, and every single one of them was wrapped in slow-flowing rivers of blue mana, saturated in it, swimming in an abundance of authority that made the harshness of the old worlds a distant and half-forgotten dream.
It was warm! It was golden! It was perfect!
And then, all at once, it was not.
Snow fell.

Out of the warm golden sky, out of the clear and cloudless blue over that sheltered beach, white flakes came drifting down, and with them came a coldness sweeping across the golden sand and the bright water and the lazy sunbathers in an instant!
Elizabeth’s eyes flew open, and she sat up sharply in her chair!
Cold?

She rose to her feet, staring up at the impossible snow, and her long experience took over before her confusion could! She raised one hand and called upon her mana, and the blue rivers that flowed around her answered instantly, gathering and weaveng at her gesture, forming into a thick and luxurious robe of fur that wrapped itself around her shoulders and settled warm against her skin.
And still she felt cold!
She frowned! The robe should have been more than enough, a working of pure mana, warmth conjured from abundance, and yet the chill sank straight through it as though it were nothing.

So she gathered her mana again, and wove a second layer over the first, thicker and heavier, and when that too was not enough she wove a third, piling authority upon authority, wrapping herself in layer after layer of conjured warmth!
Only then, beneath three thick robes of woven mana, did she feel some small measure of protection from the cold!
Some. Not all. The chill still pressed at the edges of her, patient and deep!
Elizabeth stood on the golden beach in her three heavy robes, her breath misting now in the air of a paradise that had never once been cold, and she looked around in growing bewilderment!
What was going on?
Why was it so cold, here, in THE Infiniverse? Cold did not come here! This place was sealed, protected, perfect, a haven where nothing bad had ever reched!

How could she feel cold at all?

And a child nearby, a small thing with only the faintest trickle of mana to its name, stood in the falling snow looking merely puzzled, barely troubled by the cold at all!
The more mana one held, the heavier the cold pressed.
The stronger you were, the colder you became!

Something, somewhere, had gone terribly wrong!

sentences.text: Far beneath the war of titans, far beneath the dying architect and the cracking Train and the murky obsidian foam, in a small Universe folded inside a small Observable Existence, upon a small world that had never once heard the name of an Immense One or any glimpses of authority, there was a desert.
And in that desert, there was a fire!

Around the fire sat a tribe, men and women and children wrapped in the hides of desert beasts, their brown faces lit warm and orange by the flames, and they sat close together against the cool of the night and they listened.
For it was the hour of stories, and the Wisewoman had begun to speak.
She was old, older than anyone could remember being young, her hands like knotted roots and her eyes like two dark wells that had seen every star wheel across the sky a thousand times.
She sat at the head of the fire, and her voice was low and worn and beautiful, and she told the story that had been told at this fire since before her grandmother’s grandmother had first heard it!
"Listen now," the Wisewoman said, "and remember, for a story remembered is a life saved.
I will tell you of The Long Night."
The children leaned in.
"There will come a time," she said, "long foretold and long feared, when the world turns cold.
When the warmth that has always been simply begins to leave, first from the edges of things, and then from the heart of them.
When a coldness that no fire can answer permeates the desert and the sea and the high places and the low, creeping into the sand and the water and the very breath in your chest."
The fire crackled, and the shadows danced!
"And in that time," she went on, her old eyes moving across the ring of faces, "the night will grow long.
Not one night, but a night that does not end, a darkness that stretches on and on past every dawn that should have come, until the sun itself seems to forget the way back.
This is The Long Night.
When the cold comes and the night will not lift.
And the old stories say that when it comes, all the world must huddle close, and wrap itself in every warmth it has hoarded, and endure, and wait, and hope that the dawn remembers us at the end."
Then a child rose up!
He was a small boy, bold and bright-eyed, and he stood at the edge of the fire with his little chin lifted, and he pointed at the old woman as snot leaked from his nose.
"Wisewoman!" he said.
"I know why you tell us this!
You only tell it to make us afraid, so that we behave and stay close to the fire!
But this story has never come true, not once, not for all the generations!
My father heard it, and his father, and his father’s father, and the night has always ended and the sun has always come back!
It is only a story to frighten little snotty children!"
Some of the adults chuckled softly, and a few frowned at the boy’s boldness, but the Wisewoman only smiled!
She smiled at him with all the patience of her long years, and she opened her mouth to answer him, to tell him gently that a story does not need to have come true to be worth the keeping...
And then she blinked!
For she had felt something!

Something small and cold and impossible had landed upon the withered skin of her cheek, a tiny pinprick of chill in the warm desert night, and she paused, her smile faltering, and she raised one old knotted hand and touched her face and drew it back and looked at it.
And there, melting upon the dark root of her fingertip, was a snowflake.
A snowflake!
The Wisewoman stared at it, and her ancient heart went still!
And a moment later, another fell!
And another!

And then more, and more, drifting down out of the black desert sky in their impossible countless numbers, white flakes descending upon a land that had never in all its histroy known a single one, settling on the sand, on the hides, on the upturned faces of the tribe as one by one they felt the cold touch and looked UP!
Snow!
Snow was falling in the desert!
A ripple of shock ran through the tribe, and then of fear, and then of a horror that had no words!
The children cried out!
The men surged to their feet!
The women clutched their little ones close!

They stared up at the falling white as it thickened, as the warm orange firelight caught the drifting flakes and turned them to sparks of gold falling out of the endless dark, beautiful and terrible, a thing that should not be, a thing that could not be, falling and falling upon a desert that had known only sun and heat since the world began.
And the bold boy who had stood to mock the story stood frozen now, his little face turned upward, a snowflake melting on his cheek, his eyes wide with a terror he could not name.
The Wisewoman trembled!
Her old body shook, and for a moment she was only an old and frightened woman under a sky that had broken its oldest promise.
But then her eyes shone, because she was the Wisewoman, and she carried the story, and the story had a second half that was not for frightening children but for saving them.
For generations, they had prepared.
She rose from her place at the fire!

She moved through the tribe, through the crying and the shouting and the upturned faces, moving with a purpose that stilled them as she passed, and she went to one hut at the edge of the circle, an old hut, a hut the children had always been told never to open.
And she opened it!
Inside, stacked and waiting, were furs!
Thick hides and heavy woven things, layers upon layers of warmth, gathered and cured and stored accross untold generations by keepers of the story who had never once seen them used.
Warmth hoarded for a night that had never come, waiting patient in the dark for the day the old woman’s smile would falter and a snowflake would land upon her cheek!
The Wisewoman turned back to her people!

She looked upon the men and the women and the frightened children beneath the falling snow, and she spoke, and her worn old voice carried across the whole trembling tribe with the weight of every generation that had kept the tale alive!
"Come," she said.
"Come now, all of you, and wrap yourselves in layers of protection.
Take the furs your fathers’ fathers saved for you and cover yourselves against the cold, and gather close, and do not let the fire die!"
She held the old hut open, and the snow fell past her into the warm firelight, and her shining eyes swept them all!
"The Long Night... has come."

For this was the safest place there was.

This was inside the very heart of THE True Human Emperor’s own empire, a domain sealed away from every gaze and every hunter and every architect, a paradise where the sheltered lived their sheltered lives and wanted for nothing.

chapters.title: Chapter 5751: The Long Night III
paragraphs: Across the whole of THE Infiniverse, the two sisters worked to shield the dreamers.

Upon the boundless blue-gold sea, THE Infiniverse and Ruination moved their hands in vast and patient rhythm, and waves of infinity and seas of THE Primordial Source surged out from them, rolling across the folded Realms toward the great chrysalis and the countless sleeping bodies within the empire.

The authorities wrapped around each dreamer, layer upon layer, a blanket of the oldest powers there were laid over the people Noah loved and cherished as they lived their centuries in dream, holding the descending cold at bay.
And yet, even as they worked, Ruination’s crimson eyes were troubled!

"A condition was supposedly fulfilled," she said, her voice its usual calm and analytical self, and yet somber beneath it now. "The weaving of existence declared it plainly to all who could perceive, and it came in the very instant that Immense One died. The two are linked. Of that there is no doubt. The question that remains, is the one I cannot yet close."
Her hands never stopped their work!
"Why?"
She turned the problem over as she wove!

"I currently hold a hypothesis. That after a certain number of Immense Ones fell, paired perhaps with other conditions I cannot yet perceive, something was triggered. Something that, in the deep weavings of existence, tied somehow to IT. Atlas was killed. Other Immense Ones have likely been killed across the ages. Vakochev was killed. And now, today, with another Immense One killed before the eyes of his own kind, whatever their deaths mean in the reckoning of existence has tipped a scale that was already tipping."
Her crimson gaze sharpened!

"It has been tipping for a long time. And this last death was the weight that finished it. But why? Why should the deaths of the mighty summon a cold that hunts the mighty? Why?"She said it again, quietly. "Why?"
And at that moment, Noah’s body appeared upon the golden shore!

He came into the Realm calm and unhurried, but his expression was heavy. He raised his hands, and from him a tide of Infinite Sanguine Mana poured out, crimson and gold, and he wove it into thick, warm coats, and he wrapped them around the ones he loved.

He wrapped his floating mother, sleeping in her pool, in a heavy coat of his own vitality! He wrapped little Seo-yeon, and Henry, and Riya, and one by one every other soul dreaming within his empire, layering the warmth of his own blood over them, shielding them with the one authority that answered to nothng but himself.
And as he worked, Noah reflected!
He wondered about his own hand in all of this! He had dreamed, and he had reached across the Cluster and lent his red ink to Calliope.

That lending had led to the emergence of Vakochev! And Vakochev’s emergence had led to the death of an Immense One. And that death had tipped the scale that Ruination spoke of, had fulfilled some final unknown condition, had called down this cold across the whole of existence.
His actions were part of this causality!
And yet...

So were the actions of a great many others! So were the deaths the Immense Ones themselves had dealt across the ages! So was the killing of Atlas, and the killing of Vakochev, and every weight the mighty had ever laid upon the scale! He was one hand among countless hands, one cause among an ocean of causes, and the scale had been tipping long before he ever lent his ink to a bleeding writer.
But that changed nothing about the question at the heart of it all.

Just what was this? What was this emergence of coldness that ignored authority itself, that fell hardest upon the strongest, that reached even into the sealed heart of his empire and touched the skin of a being like him?
Noah finished wrapping the last of the dreamers, and he turned to his Ruination.
"Give me your confirmed analysis of this Condition,"he said. "Fully. Everything you have so far."
And Ruination answered,.
|No barrier of THE Infiniverse has been able to halt its emergence. No authority, no sealing, no Elsedimension, no weaving has stopped it or slowed it.|

|It has covered every Realm across the whole of THE Infiniverse. It has covered THE Ymnaros. It has covered every Dimension and Observable Existence over which our influence has ever spread. It is everywhere our reach extends, and it is beyond it also.|

|Effect confirmed: those who hold no authority are affected LEAST. The strongest lifeforms must enact the strongest protections merely to steer clear of the cold. Power is not a shield against this Condition. Power is a target.|
Ruination’s voice continued, and it grew heavier.

"And it is not only the suppression, Master. I have begun monitoring your own existence, and I must tell you what I find there, because you will feel it soon yourself. Your biological systems have already begun to respond. Even now, energy is being metabolized within you, burned and spent, consumed to hold the cold at bay from the inside."
|Master’s biological systems are metabolizing energy at an accelerating rate to resist the Condition.|
|You will begin to feel hunger. Soon.|

"For now," Ruination went on, "the Infinity running through your existence can feed your cells and your quarks faster than the cold can drain them. You can sustain yourself on your own boundlessness, or so I first believed."

Her tone tightened. "But my monitoring shows that even your Infinity is not fully reclaiming everything the cold takes. There is a loss. A leak that your boundlessness cannot entirely close. Which means that in time, even you, Master, may need to consume biological matter to protect yourself from this cold."
|Projection: authority alone will not sustain existence against the Condition indefinitely.|

|All existences, whether of the Finite Verse, the Ineffable Verse, or the Immense Ones themselves, will likely feel the need to consume biological life to sustain themselves against the cold, in addition to spending their authority.|

"And I must be honest with you about the limits of what I say,"Ruination finished. "All of this, everything I have told you, is only what we have been able to grasp in the first few minutes of its emergence. We do not yet understand the full scope of this Existential Condition. We understand almost nothing of it. We only see the edges of a thing that is still arriving."
And even Ruination, who was never anything but composed, seemed somber and serious as she spoke those last words.

Beside her, THE Infiniverse stood with her starlit eyes closed, utterly still, her whole vast attention turned inward and outward at once, sensing every change occurring across the whole of her boundless existence, feeling the cold creep into every Realm she held, cataloging a catastrophe she could not stop from spreading through her own body.
And Noah stood upon the golden sands of his shore, and he looked up!

Snowflakes drifted down out of the golden sky and settled upon his skin and did not melt, and the cold pressed at him even through all that he was, and his expression was heavy, heavy with the weight of a thing he had helped to cause and could not yet understand, a catastrophe with no name and no source and no cure, falling silent and white and terrible across the whole of Existence.
Another of Noah’s bodies arrived in a place where time had come apart.

It stepped out of a conceptual tear and into a Dimension of deep purple and drifting green, and it was a broken and beautiful ruin of a place! Scattered through the twilight air hung the hands of clocks, thousands upon thousands of them, some vast as mountains and some small as needles, spinning and stopped and spinning backward all at once.

And through them drifted meteorites, tumbling slow across the purple dark, and every one of those meteorites was shaped like a number, ancient figures of stone and starlight wheeling through a sky that had forgotten how to keep time!
This was a Dimension lost to time itself, one of the most profound Elsedimensions Atlas had ever made.
And yet even here, even in this sanctuary of shattered hours, the cold had come.

Noah looked, and he saw a storm of snow gathering, wrapping itself around the drifting clock-hands, frosting the numbered meteorites, and creeping even up his own arm to wreath the illusory ring upon his finger.
Even Atlas was affected! Even a Dimension outside of time could not keep the descending cold from its door!
But first, Noah turned his attention inward, and he analyzed.

He examined the cold as it pressed against him, studied the way it sank past his skin and reached toward the deep structure of his existence, and he traced its effect through every layer of himself. His Perpetual Baryogenesis was running, the weight of existence trickling down onto his two hundred decillion quarks without pause, and he could feel the cold trying to slow that trickle, trying to press heavy upon each quark and dim its generation.

His Nine Teloi burned steady against it, holding the lattice of his existence firm, and his Provenance surged warm and boundless through the whole of him, feeding his cells and his quarks against the chill.
For now, he held! For now, his foundation was more than the cold could take.
And as he took stock of himself, the prompts of his recent trials bloomed before him, the gains he had earned in the writing of a Fallen Hero!
|For your role in aiding and ushering the emergence of an Unfathomable Narrative, and for witnessing the fall of an Immense One, your existence has been enriched.|
|Your foundation, tempered by Perpetual Baryogenesis and the guiding of grand dreams, has climbed.|
Noah pulled up the full account of himself, and read where he now stood.
|THE True Human Emperor / THE Human Dreamer|
|VERITAS: 223|
|PROVENANCE: 275|
|POTENTIA: INFINITE|
|PONDUS: 223|
|OSMONTIAN MOIRAI: 251|
| THE Enduring Gu Elsedimension Ring +20 all; THE Existential Foundational Narrative Inscription +50 all, folded into the totals above.)|
His Provenance had surged well past everything else, climbing faster than his other attributes with every dream he guided and every narrative he touched.
A few dozen points gained in these last trials alone, his authorship swelling toward something the rest of him could not yet match.
He was becoming, more and more, a creature of pure Provenance, of pure infinity and dreaming, and the numbers only confirmed what he already felt.
But even reading his own grand ascent, Noah felt it.
A small thing! A slow and growing emptiness deep in the core of him, rising patient beneath all his boundless power.
Hunger!

It was beginning, exactly as Ruination had warned! The cold was metabolizing him from within, burning his energy to hold itself at bay, and even his Infinity could not fully close the leak as it was not even for lack of its authority or brilliance.
It was as if this Existential Condition purposefully made things this way.
Slowly, softly, Noah Osmont was beginning to grow hungry.
Then he turned to the ring upon his finger!
"Atlas," Noah said. "Do you know what this is all about? This Existential Condition? This coldness?"
The illusory old body of Atlas flickered up out of the ring, and snow gathered around his translucent shoulders even as he formed, dusting his ancient projected frame with white!
|I cannot say for sure,| Atlas said. |But it should be linked to IT. Maybe. I have heard musings, across my long life, that I never once thought I would need.|
The clock-hands turned in the cold behind him!

|One musing was this. That if a certain threshold of something is reached across the whole of Existence, if Existential Narrative is abused, or torn, or spent and then discarded, time and time again, across enough ages, then something would arise to correct it. A response. A balancing. Existence, pushed too far, pushing back.|
His projected eyes were distant!

|Another musing I know is older still. You know how we speak of Those Who Remain, the Immense Ones who stayed? There were Immense Ones who leapt across an uncrossable barrier, once, in the earliest age. And the others, the ones we call Those Who Remain, are the ones who FAILED to make that leap. And in that failure, in whatever they did all those ages ago when they tried and could not, something was done to Existence itself. Something was broken, or bent, or spent. And IT was involved then, at that failure, just as I believe IT is involved now.|
Atlas lowered his hand slowly!

|No Immense One holds IT. Not truly. You have told me yourself how your girl came back from a future where THE Sealed One was given IT by the Immense Ones, and even that cannot be entirely true, because IT cannot be given. Perhaps he was granted a grasp of some power related to it. Perhaps that action, in that future, abused something and fulfilled yet another condition of the many. I cannot be certain of the shape of any of it.|
He looked up, into the drifting clocks!
|But this coldness spreading across existence is a point of change. A great one. What this change will entail, even I do not know. But time.|He almost smiled, and there was iron beneath it.

|Time will have all answers, and time will give them, to those patient and clever enough to ask. That is why we are here, in this body of yours, in this Dimension of mine that stands outside the flow. We are here to look for solutions using time itself. And there is much to do before either of us understands what just changed in the bones of Existence...|
Even Atlas could not be sure.

Noah stood among the broken hours and the falling snow and turned it all over in his mind! An Existential Condition tied to IT, to the failure of the ones who Remained, to the abuse of Existential Narrative across the ages, to the death of Immense Ones, to a scale tipped at last.
A change in the very bones of existence, and no one, not Ruination, not Atlas, not the Immense Ones themselves, understood it.
He needed to understand!

His masked portion of existence, his eye that dreamed among the Immense Ones, the presence within his Infinite Dream that could be destroyed and destroyed again and would always return, that may be the best instrument he had for gathering the truth of this.
For where better to learn what an Immense One knew, than to sit among them and watch and listen as their own certainties crumbled in the falling snow?
He had to understand!
He had to understand exactly what this change meant, before existence itself grew cold enough to answer the question for him.

Because...nobody knew if it would continue to get colder. Nobody knew if there was a future where it grew so cold...that Gilded Lifeforms, Source Lifeforms, Infinite Lifeforms, Primeval Ones, Descendants, Provenance Lifeforms, Gu...or even Immense Ones...would become frozen blocks of ice.

"And I must be honest with you about the limits of what I say,"Ruination finished.
"All of this, everything I have told you, is only what we have been able to grasp in the first few minutes of its emergence.
We do not yet understand the full scope of this Existential Condition.
We understand almost nothing of it.
We only see the edges of a thing that is still arriving."
And even Ruination, who was never anything but composed, seemed somber and serious as she spoke those last words.

Beside her, THE Infiniverse stood with her starlit eyes closed, utterly still, her whole vast attention turned inward and outward at once, sensing every change occurring across the whole of her boundless existence, feeling the cold creep into every Realm she held, cataloging a catastrophe she could not stop from spreading through her own body.
And Noah stood upon the golden sands of his shore, and he looked up!

Snowflakes drifted down out of the golden sky and settled upon his skin and did not melt, and the cold pressed at him even through all that he was, and his expression was heavy, heavy with the weight of a thing he had helped to cause and could not yet understand, a catastrophe with no name and no source and no cure, falling silent and white and terrible across the whole of Existence.
Another of Noah’s bodies arrived in a place where time had come apart.
It stepped out of a conceptual tear and into a Dimension of deep purple and drifting green, and it was a broken and beautiful ruin of a place!

Scattered through the twilight air hung the hands of clocks, thousands upon thousands of them, some vast as mountains and some small as needles, spinning and stopped and spinning backward all at once.

And through them drifted meteorites, tumbling slow across the purple dark, and every one of those meteorites was shaped like a number, ancient figures of stone and starlight wheeling through a sky that had forgotten how to keep time!
This was a Dimension lost to time itself, one of the most profound Elsedimensions Atlas had ever made.
And yet even here, even in this sanctuary of shattered hours, the cold had come.

Noah looked, and he saw a storm of snow gathering, wrapping itself around the drifting clock-hands, frosting the numbered meteorites, and creeping even up his own arm to wreath the illusory ring upon his finger.
Even Atlas was affected!
Even a Dimension outside of time could not keep the descending cold from its door!
But first, Noah turned his attention inward, and he analyzed.
He examined the cold as it pressed against him, studied the way it sank past his skin and reached toward the deep structure of his existence, and he traced its effect through every layer of himself.

His Perpetual Baryogenesis was running, the weight of existence trickling down onto his two hundred decillion quarks without pause, and he could feel the cold trying to slow that trickle, trying to press heavy upon each quark and dim its generation.

His Nine Teloi burned steady against it, holding the lattice of his existence firm, and his Provenance surged warm and boundless through the whole of him, feeding his cells and his quarks against the chill.
For now, he held!
For now, his foundation was more than the cold could take.
And as he took stock of himself, the prompts of his recent trials bloomed before him, the gains he had earned in the writing of a Fallen Hero!
|For your role in aiding and ushering the emergence of an Unfathomable Narrative, and for witnessing the fall of an Immense One, your existence has been enriched.|
|Your foundation, tempered by Perpetual Baryogenesis and the guiding of grand dreams, has climbed.|
Noah pulled up the full account of himself, and read where he now stood.
|THE True Human Emperor / THE Human Dreamer|
|VERITAS: 223|
|PROVENANCE: 275|
|POTENTIA: INFINITE|
|PONDUS: 223|
|OSMONTIAN MOIRAI: 251|
| THE Enduring Gu Elsedimension Ring +20 all; THE Existential Foundational Narrative Inscription +50 all, folded into the totals above.)|
His Provenance had surged well past everything else, climbing faster than his other attributes with every dream he guided and every narrative he touched.
A few dozen points gained in these last trials alone, his authorship swelling toward something the rest of him could not yet match.
He was becoming, more and more, a creature of pure Provenance, of pure infinity and dreaming, and the numbers only confirmed what he already felt.
But even reading his own grand ascent, Noah felt it.
A small thing!
A slow and growing emptiness deep in the core of him, rising patient beneath all his boundless power.
Hunger!
It was beginning, exactly as Ruination had warned!
The cold was metabolizing him from within, burning his energy to hold itself at bay, and even his Infinity could not fully close the leak as it was not even for lack of its authority or brilliance.
It was as if this Existential Condition purposefully made things this way.
Slowly, softly, Noah Osmont was beginning to grow hungry.
Then he turned to the ring upon his finger!
"Atlas," Noah said.
"Do you know what this is all about?
This Existential Condition?
This coldness?"
The illusory old body of Atlas flickered up out of the ring, and snow gathered around his translucent shoulders even as he formed, dusting his ancient projected frame with white!
|I cannot say for sure,| Atlas said. |But it should be linked to IT.
Maybe.
I have heard musings, across my long life, that I never once thought I would need.|
The clock-hands turned in the cold behind him!
|One musing was this.

That if a certain threshold of something is reached across the whole of Existence, if Existential Narrative is abused, or torn, or spent and then discarded, time and time again, across enough ages, then something would arise to correct it.
A response.
A balancing.
Existence, pushed too far, pushing back.|
His projected eyes were distant!
|Another musing I know is older still.
You know how we speak of Those Who Remain, the Immense Ones who stayed?
There were Immense Ones who leapt across an uncrossable barrier, once, in the earliest age.
And the others, the ones we call Those Who Remain, are the ones who FAILED to make that leap.
And in that failure, in whatever they did all those ages ago when they tried and could not, something was done to Existence itself.
Something was broken, or bent, or spent.
And IT was involved then, at that failure, just as I believe IT is involved now.|
Atlas lowered his hand slowly!
|No Immense One holds IT.
Not truly.
You have told me yourself how your girl came back from a future where THE Sealed One was given IT by the Immense Ones, and even that cannot be entirely true, because IT cannot be given.
Perhaps he was granted a grasp of some power related to it.
Perhaps that action, in that future, abused something and fulfilled yet another condition of the many.
I cannot be certain of the shape of any of it.|
He looked up, into the drifting clocks!
|But this coldness spreading across existence is a point of change.
A great one.
What this change will entail, even I do not know.
But time.|He almost smiled, and there was iron beneath it.
|Time will have all answers, and time will give them, to those patient and clever enough to ask.
That is why we are here, in this body of yours, in this Dimension of mine that stands outside the flow.
We are here to look for solutions using time itself.
And there is much to do before either of us understands what just changed in the bones of Existence...|
Even Atlas could not be sure.
Noah stood among the broken hours and the falling snow and turned it all over in his mind!
An Existential Condition tied to IT, to the failure of the ones who Remained, to the abuse of Existential Narrative across the ages, to the death of Immense Ones, to a scale tipped at last.
A change in the very bones of existence, and no one, not Ruination, not Atlas, not the Immense Ones themselves, understood it.
He needed to understand!

His masked portion of existence, his eye that dreamed among the Immense Ones, the presence within his Infinite Dream that could be destroyed and destroyed again and would always return, that may be the best instrument he had for gathering the truth of this.
For where better to learn what an Immense One knew, than to sit among them and watch and listen as their own certainties crumbled in the falling snow?
He had to understand!
He had to understand exactly what this change meant, before existence itself grew cold enough to answer the question for him.
Because...nobody knew if it would continue to get colder.

Nobody knew if there was a future where it grew so cold...that Gilded Lifeforms, Source Lifeforms, Infinite Lifeforms, Primeval Ones, Descendants, Provenance Lifeforms, Gu...or even Immense Ones...would become frozen blocks of ice.

chapters.title: Chapter 5752: A Stranger! I
paragraphs: The chase had scattered them.

Across the two sundered halves of the Dimensional Provenance Train, the gathered gazes had broken formation and thrown themselves into the cracks of existence after the ghost who had killed one of their own.

THE SLEEPLESS FIEND, THE UNPAID COLLECTOR, THE CACKLING BUTCHER, all of them gone into the dark, howling and blazing after what remained of Vakochev, chasing a Fallen Hero back into the wound he had vanished through!
An Immense One had been slain! Every one of them wanted to be the hand that made certain it did not happen twice.
So the region emptied.

Noah watched it empty from the far rim, his masked eye hanging quiet in the falling snow. Where the sky had been crowded with the eyes of monsters, now there were only a few, and then fewer, gazes flickering out and vanishing into the deep dark, each one gone on its own hunt or its own retreat from the cold that had begun to fall.

While one of his bodies stood at the threshold of the Atlas Elsedimension of shattered time, ready to begin the search for something, this body, this masked dreaming eye, simply watched the aftermath of a thing that should never have been possible.
He watched Calliope.

Down in the wreckage of the Cluster, the Writer of Mythos sat in the ruin of her own spent existence, and she was cold. The fascination had gone out of her, worn down by the snow and the blood she had lost.

She lifted an ink-stained hand and wrote a single flowing line upon the air, and out of it unfolded a fur coat, thick and warm, that wrapped itself around her thin shoulders. She pulled it close and huddled down into it against the chill. Even she, who had just written the death of an architect, sat shivering like anyone else, wrapped in a coat she had written for herself!
In the distance, THE Creature still stood.
The titanic King had endured the storm and the suppression and the fall of the Overseeing One, and he remained, a silent mountain, his obsidian flames guttering low against the cold!
But he did not stay long. Slowly he turned, gathered the tatters of his conquered army and began to retreat slowly, watching in the corner of his eyes.
Adrastia, The Sealed One, The Infinity Eater...many seemingly sensed the sudden change and began pulling back slowly, as if they were being cautious first to see what else would happen!
And above it all, Noah looked up.
He turned his gaze toward the place where the corpse of the slain Immense One hung in the churning obsidian foam, and he strained his infinite sight upon it, and he could not see it!

Not truly. Not even now. The Overseeing One was dead, snuffed out, his Trueness put out by a fire-wrapped fist, and still the corpse sat past the reach of Noah’s eye, a wrongness in the foam, a shape his sight slid off of and could not hold, there only as a pressure and an absence and a low buzz in the weavings around it.
And that, more than anything, made him think about what an Immense One truly was.

He had watched a battle between titans, and he had seen almost none of it. His gaze was Infinite now. His sight was a dream with no far wall. And still, when Vakochev and the Immense Ones had truly clashed, they had simply left the reach of the perceivable behind.

He had caught fragments. Slivers torn out of a chaos too big to hold. An arm through a curtain. The sound of a jaw breaking. A coffin drifting through storms of Source. He had seen what their blows left behind and never the blows themselves. He had watched Vakochev seem to close his hands on a throat and seem to snap a neck, and even that, even the killing, had come to him in broken pieces, like a man trying to watch lightning by the shape of the burnt ground it left behnd.
That was what an Immense One was!

What did it mean when a mind that possessed hundreds of attributes could not even form a complete image of a dead lifeform? Was the gap between a Provenance Lifeform and an Immense One merely a count of numbers, or was it a gap of category so profound that standard perception broke upon contact with their physical remains?

Their power did not just beat his. It beat his ability to see it happen! They fought at a height where sight itself gave out, where even a being of Infinite dreaming caught only the wreckage after, because the true shape of their war was simply too vast and too high to be held by any eye below their own. He had spent this whole stretch thinking of himself as something grand, an author sitting unseen among them, steering their stories from the dark, and he was.
But he had just been reminded, hard, of the gulf that still lay between a masked watcher at the rim and the beings whose battle he could not even watch.

The Overseeing One was dead, and Noah still could not see the corpse! A dead Immense One was more than his living sight could hold. What did that say about the ones still breathing? About THE SLEEPLESS FIEND, whose brightness he had barely dared to look at? About the gazes chasing Vakochev through the dark right now?

He had watched one of them die, and he had not really seen the death, and he could not really see the body, and if he ever meant to stand against such beings instead of just hiding from them, he had a very long road left to walk.
But even as that settled into him, he felt something else.
Existence was buzzing around the corpse he could not see!

The weavings near the dead architect were stirring. Gathering. Trembling, as though the death were not an ending but the start of something, as though somethng were about to come out of the ruin of a fallen Immense One that had not yet shown its face.
So Noah did the thing he was best at.

He watched. Masked, quiet, unseen, a patient eye at the rim of an emptying battlefield, snow falling silent across his dreaming form, he fixed his gaze on the buzzing weavings around a corpse he could not perceive, and he waited to see what would rise from the death of an Immense One!
The battlefield was somewhat empty now, and the snow kept falling.
Noah looked out over the ruin of a thing that should never have happened as he watched it!
And then the cold began to move.

It did not fall on the corpse like how the snow fell on everything else, soft and scattered. It gathered. Across the whole vast region the descending cold drew together, thickening, condensing, and it began to flow toward the dead architect in rivers, great pale currents of it pouring in from every direction, rushing into the corpse and vanshing inside it!

Noah watched the white streams converge and drain into the thing he could not see, and a deep wrongness crawled through his dreaming existence, because a corpse should not drink. A death should not pull the cold into itself like a mouth pulling at water. A dead thing should lie still!
This one drank, and drank, and drank!

The cold poured into the unperceivable corpse for a long moment, more and more of it, concentrations that would have flattened lesser existences gathering into a single dead point. And Noah, watching, felt something begin that he had no name for, a pressure building where an ending should have been, a held breath that would not release.
Then, where a death had been, a life bloomed!
Something formed from the corpse. Something titanic!

Noah strained his infinite gaze upon it, poured his whole definition of endless sight into the single act of looking, and even so he could barely perceive the thing that rose. It came up out of the drinking corpse slow and vast, a shape of blue-white cold and jagged rime, humanoid and utterly wrong, its edges never resolving, its features refusing to hold under his sight!

Where its eyes should have been, there were only two points of pale ice, cold and depthless. It moved with a terrible unhurried grace, a thing in no hurry at all, a thing with all the time in Existence.
And Noah knew the face!

He knew it, and he could not make himself believe it, because he had seen this face before, once, in a vision inside a Runestone, walking through a Primordial forest and scattering worlds to feed fish in a river!

It was Lucy. It was the small rough caveman-being who had smiled and given the infinite away like feed. But it was frozen now. Ancient and hollowed and rimed with a cold that had eaten the warmth out of it, the same face turned to ice, the same shape emptied of everything that had made it kind.
The visage did not look at him.

It did not look at anything. Not at Noah masked and staring at the rim. Not at the few frozen survivors who had not yet fled. Not even at the corpse it had risen from, the dead architect whose death had somehow become its cradle. It simply stood there in the falling snow, vast and indifferent, a thing that had come up out of a death and did not care about a single living gaze upon it.
It raised its hands.
And a forest came!

Out of nothing, out of the frozen dark, trees erupted across the whole of the region and planted themselves in the empty space. Boundless, countless, they rose and spread, vegetation climbing outward for Gigaparsecs, a forest blooming across a battlefield in an instant as it spread for countless Gigaparsecs.
They were the trees from the vision!

The Dimension-bearing trees, the ancient boughs that grew Observable Existences and Dimensions like ripening fruit, the orchard of realities Lucy had walked through in the beginning of things. But these were not budding with warm and swirling worlds!

These were rimed and dormant, their fruit frozen hard upon the branches, whole Observable Existences and Elsedimensions hanging still and cold and asleep in their boughs, a forest of frozen Domains spreading silent accross the ruin.
Prompts bloomed across Noah’s sight, and they gave him no comfort at all.
|An unfathomable event has occurred. A life has bloomed from the death of an Immense One.|
|The region is being reclassified. Existence here is being overwritten by an unknown weaving.|
|A frozen growth has taken root: dormant Observable Existences and Dimensions are forming within it, held still and cold.|
|This is beyond current understanding. The nature of the emerged existence cannot be perceived or measured...|
Noah read the words seriously!
And the frost-visage of Lucy, having planted its forest, was done.

It did not linger. It did not survey its work or turn to see who watched. It simply took a single step, one unhurried stride into the falling snow, and it was gone, vanished as completely as if it had never been, indifferent to the very end, leaving behind only a growing frozen forest over the disappearing corpse of an Immense One turning into flickers of nothing!
Noah hung there, staring.

Below him, slow and silent, the frost-trees began to grow. Their frozen boughs stretched a fraction wider. Their rimed fruit swelled a fraction fuller. The forest of dormant worlds crept outward across the ruined region, patient and cold and unstoppable, and Noah watched it spread and felt the weight of a thing far larger than any battle settling onto his masked existence!
He needed to think. He needed to be still and try to understand what he had just seen!
He was beginning to spread his eye away when a voice reached him.
"Osmont."
It came soft, threaded into his Provenance the way only another author could place it there. Calliope.
Noah waited.
Down in the wreckage, wrapped in the fur coat she had written for herself, THE Writer of Mythos was looking up at the spreading frost-forest.
"I did not expect it to lead to this," she said. "When I wrote him back. THE Vestige of THE Fallen Hero. I wanted a grand story, and I got one, and then the story kept going somewhere I never wrote."

She gave a small breath of a laugh, cold and genuine."A dead titan killing a living one. And now this. A forest of frozen Domains growing out of a corpse. I have been writing for a very long time, and I have never once seen a Mythos wander this far off its own page."
She was quiet a moment, and the snow fell on her, and she pulled the coat tighter.
"But I want to be honest with you, Osmont, since you are the only one here who might understand it."
Her voice steadied, and beneath the tiredness there was majesty!

"I do not regret it. Not one stroke of it. I have spent an eternity knowing every ending before I ever wrote it, bored to the bone with a story I had already read. And for one moment, back there, I wrote something even I could not predict. Do you know what that is worth, to a thing like me? To finally not know what happens next?!"

A wondering hush entered her words."I would do it again. I would do it a thousand times. Whatever this becomes, whatever this cold is, whatever grows out of that corpse and spreads across all of existence, at least it is a story worth watching.."
She looked up at the frozen trees climbing the ruined sky, and her strange eyes shone.
"I will see exactly what changes across existence, and I will hope, in my odd little way, that the Mythos forming here is a grand one."

Then her voice sharpened, and she asked the question that had been sitting under everything. "But tell me, Osmont. I barely grasped it with my Matriarch’s Narrative. That thing that rose. That was the likeness within the Runestone, was it not? That was Lucy?"
BOOM
Her puzzlement was real now!
"Why? Why would a lifeform from the earliest age of existence have its likeness rise up out of the corpse of a murdered Immense One? What does the first thing have to do with the last?!"
Noah did not answer.
He hung masked and silent in the falling snow, staring at the growing frost-forest, the question turning over and over in the quiet of his existence and finding nothing to catch on.
Because for once, THE True Human Emperor did not know either!
