Their frozen boughs stretched a fraction wider.
Their rimed fruit swelled a fraction fuller.

The forest of dormant worlds crept outward across the ruined region, patient and cold and unstoppable, and Noah watched it spread and felt the weight of a thing far larger than any battle settling onto his masked existence!
He needed to think.
He needed to be still and try to understand what he had just seen!
He was beginning to spread his eye away when a voice reached him.
"Osmont."
It came soft, threaded into his Provenance the way only another author could place it there.
Calliope.
Noah waited.
Down in the wreckage, wrapped in the fur coat she had written for herself, THE Writer of Mythos was looking up at the spreading frost-forest.
"I did not expect it to lead to this," she said.
"When I wrote him back.
THE Vestige of THE Fallen Hero.
I wanted a grand story, and I got one, and then the story kept going somewhere I never wrote."
She gave a small breath of a laugh, cold and genuine."A dead titan killing a living one.
And now this.
A forest of frozen Domains growing out of a corpse.
I have been writing for a very long time, and I have never once seen a Mythos wander this far off its own page."
She was quiet a moment, and the snow fell on her, and she pulled the coat tighter.
"But I want to be honest with you, Osmont, since you are the only one here who might understand it."
Her voice steadied, and beneath the tiredness there was majesty!
"I do not regret it.
Not one stroke of it.
I have spent an eternity knowing every ending before I ever wrote it, bored to the bone with a story I had already read.
And for one moment, back there, I wrote something even I could not predict.
Do you know what that is worth, to a thing like me?
To finally not know what happens next?!"
A wondering hush entered her words."I would do it again.
I would do it a thousand times.
Whatever this becomes, whatever this cold is, whatever grows out of that corpse and spreads across all of existence, at least it is a story worth watching.."
She looked up at the frozen trees climbing the ruined sky, and her strange eyes shone.
"I will see exactly what changes across existence, and I will hope, in my odd little way, that the Mythos forming here is a grand one."
Then her voice sharpened, and she asked the question that had been sitting under everything.
"But tell me, Osmont.
I barely grasped it with my Matriarch’s Narrative.
That thing that rose.
That was the likeness within the Runestone, was it not?
That was Lucy?"
BOOM
Her puzzlement was real now!
"Why?
Why would a lifeform from the earliest age of existence have its likeness rise up out of the corpse of a murdered Immense One?
What does the first thing have to do with the last?!"
Noah did not answer.
He hung masked and silent in the falling snow, staring at the growing frost-forest, the question turning over and over in the quiet of his existence and finding nothing to catch on.
Because for once, THE True Human Emperor did not know either!

chapters.title: Chapter 5753: A Stranger! II
paragraphs: Upon the shore inside THE Infiniverse, where the great chrysalis hummed and the sleeping bodies floated in their warm pools of Infinite Sanguine Mana, Ruination came to Noah with shining, heavy eyes.
"Master," she said."I have found something. I do not fully know what it means, and that is precisely why I have come to you at once."
"What is it?"

"Since the cold began, I have been searching."Her manifestation flickered with the immensity of the work behind her words. "Every Realm we hold. Every Dimension our weavings touch. Every Observable Existence within our reach. I have pulled and cross-referenced trillions of threads of information, looking for a single thing, any existence anywhere that has a name for what is happening to us. A record. A word. Anything."
"And?"

"Across trillions of threads, across every mighty lineage and archive and sovereign memory in our reach, not one has a name for this phenomenon. The great powers of existence are experiencing this catastrophe with the same blind astonishment we are."
Her crimson gaze steadied.
"Except for one place."
Noah waited.

"I got lucky enough to check...in a single small world," Ruination said, "inside an Observable Existence, within a Dimension our weavings barely reach, there is a legend. A story, passed down among a lifeforms with no authority. And the legend is about a coldness that comes, and a night that does not end. They call it THE LONG NIGHT. And so far, the few lines I have managed to grasp... matches the Condition."
Noah was quiet for a long moment.
He had already asked Thalia, and she had said with astonishment how the future she came from...did not have anything like this occur. Nor did she have knowledge of this Existential Condition!
Neither did her Father or Rosalia. So even Provenance Lifeforms didn’t know as Immense Ones might be on the same boat.
But then, why would a tiny tribe know?
"I will go myself," he said.
Ruination inclined her head as she nodded.
He wove a single body, unassuming and plain, and he sent it far away.
In an unknown World hidden in a small corner of an Observable Existence.

The desert was cold now as it should not have been. Noah’s body arrived in the twilight at the edge of a sea of red sand, and the land stretched away in long dunes toward a horizon that had known nothing but sun and heat since the world began. But out of the darkening sky, drifting slow and impossible over the endless sand, came the snow.
The tribe was small, a cluster of hide tents pitched in the lee of a great dune, and it was awake and frightened. Fires burned high against the cold.

Beasts, long-legged and shaggy, lowed and shifted in their pens, uneasy in weather they had no memory of. And the people moved among it all wrapped in furs, thick heavy hides pulled from somewhere and thrown over shoulders that had never in a hundred generations needed them, men and women and children huddling close to the flames and looking up, again and again, at the snow that should not be faling.
Noah walked into the firelight as a plain traveler, and the tribe saw him and they grew wary.

But they did not turn him away. A hunter came forward and looked him over, and after a moment gestured him toward the warmth. There was food pressed into his hands. There was a place made for him at the fire.
Noah saw a boy near the flames, small and bold-faced, the kind of boy who was always the loudest at any fire. But the boy was not loud now.
He sat close to his mother with a fur pulled up to his chin, watching the snow fall with wide and frightened eyes, and he did not say a word.
And then they brought Noah, a stranger to a Wisewoman.
She sat apart, near the largest fire, and she was old beyond old. Her hands were like knotted desert roots, dark and cracked and strong, and her body didn’t even carry a shred of mana.
And she was not afraid.

The snow fell and her people trembled and the Wisewoman sat by her fire with a terrible calm, because she had already seen the sky break its oldest promise tonight, and after that, a strange traveler was a small thing indeed!
She looked at Noah, and she saw more than most would have. She only gestured him to sit.
"I heard of a legend," Noah said, settling by her fire, "passed down in your tribe. I came a long way to listen for it if that is all right."
The Wisewoman studied him with her deep old eyes.
"You came for the story," she said. "Onthe very night it comes true...haha!" A dry, worn almost-laugh moved in her chest!
She looked into the fire, and she began.

"Long ago," she said, "in the time of my grandmother’s grandmother’s grandmother, hundreds of years gone, a stranger came to my people. A stranger...not unlike you. He fell out of the empty sky and into the sand, and when the hunters found him he was broken and bleeding, hurt in ways no fall could explain, dying by the look of him. They carried him to the fire, as is our law, and they tried to mend him."
Her root-hands turned slowly in her lap.

"He was not one of us. He was not one of anything my forefathers had a name for. And as he lay dying by this same fire, or one like it, he spoke as if he were reciting something branded into his soul..."
The snow fell past the firelight, and the Wisewoman’s voice changed, dropping into an old cadence, a rhythm worn smooth by hundreds of years of telling, the words no longer quite her own.
"When the scale is shattered, the shards become the floor.
When belief is spent, the cold comes walking.
What was counted shall come uncounted.
The high shall be set upon the balance and asked what they weighed,
and the balance shall not lie, for the balance is winter,
and winter does not warm the full hand. It climbs it.
The was and the will-be shall pour into one cup,
and no throat shall taste which it drank first.
That which remains shall cease to remain.
That which was laid down shall rise, and be laid down, and rise again,
until no one recalls which was the standing and which the fall.
Behind every wall there sleeps a pen.
One hand alone ever wrote with it, and what that hand saw, it did not keep.
The pen may unpick the whole cloth, or stitch it past the last thread of light.
No eye has read the page. Every eye burns to.
And at the turning, count three.
One shall look upon all that is, and grieve.
One shall take up every weight, and not set it down.
One shall no longer remain, and yet remain.
By their three hands the cloth is torn, or the cloth is woven anew,
and no living soul may say which
Hoard your warmth.
And when the snow falls upon the sand,
know the Long Night has come, and was always coming,
and that only the True walk out the far side of it."
HUUUM!
The fire crackled. The Wisewoman fell silent.
Noah sat very still!
The words were cryptic, but somewhat discernible!

The winter that climbed the full hand. The was and the will-be poured into one cup. And the three at the turning, and the sleeping pen behind every wall, the one hand that ever wrote with it and did not keep what it saw.

He knew that last part. He had touched a Runestone and been shown that exact thing, a being who held the pen at the beginning and looked upon what it wrote and ended itself, and here it was, folded into an old woman’s chant hundreds of years before Noah was born, to a people who could not have understood a word of what they were keeping.

"That is it," the Wisewoman said, quieter now. "He gave us the story, and then he gave us one last thing. He told my forefathers to hoard warmth and food, and to keep the story, and to pass both down and never let either be forgotten."
She gestured toward a hut at the edge of the camp, and Noah knew that inside it were the furs and foods, generations of them, cured and stored by keepers who never once saw the snow themseleves.

"And then," the Wisewoman said, "he was gone. Some say he died and we buried him. Some say he walked into the desert and the desert took him. My grandmother told me he simply was not there one morning, as though the sand had never held him at all. We do not know who he was. We only know what he left us."

Her deep eyes found Noah’s. "And tonight, for the first time in all the years since, the story is true, and the furs are on our backs, and an old woman who did not truly believe until this very night is very glad her forefathers did."
Noah looked at her for a long moment.
A dying stranger, hundreds of years ago, who fell bleeding out of the sky into the smallest place in existence and gave a prophecy no power would ever hear.
Who knew all of this was coming!
"Thank you,"Noah said quietly. "For remembering and for telling it to a stranger on the night it came true."
Then he rose and he raised his hand.
It was a small motion, an unremarkable gesture, and the tribe did not understand it. But the desert answered.

Around the cluster of tents, out across the cold red sand, the land began to change. Green rose from the dunes. Farmland unrolled itself across the desert in wide dark rows, rich soil where there had been only sand, and seeds sank into it and split and grew, crops rising in moments, food enough to feed the tribe through any winter that came.
Small warm stars kindled in the air above the fields, low and gentle, hanging over the new-grown green and pouring down a soft and steady heat that pushed back the cold.
And at the edge of the new fields, water welled up out of the ground and ran, rivers forming where no river had ever been, bright and clear and warm, winding through the farmland in the falling snow!

The snow still fell. Noah did not stop it, because he could not, not even here. But beneath it now there was warmth, and green, and water, and food, a small oasis of protection blooming around a tribe that had waited a hundred generations in the cold.

The people stared, and some of them wept, and the bold frightened boy stood up from his mother’s side and looked out at the impossible green with his mouth open and, for the first time that night, something in his eyes that was not fear!
The Wisewoman looked at the fields, and then she looked at the traveler.
Noah gave her the smallest nod, and then his plain body dissolved quietly into the snow, and he was gone.
He returned to himself with the name in his hands.
THE LONG NIGHT. The name the mightiest beings in existence did not have, held all this time by the smallest. And with it, the knowledge that hundreds of years ago, someone had known this was coming.
Who was the Stranger, to know a catastrophe that hunted the powerful, and to carry that knowledge to the powerless?
And how did a mortal tribe in a desert come to hold the only true prophecy of the transformation of an Age?
Noah did not know.
But he intended to find out!

chapters.title: Chapter 5754: ECG!
paragraphs: Far from THE Infiniverse.
Noah’s Dream body hung above the Primordial ice forest, and he looked at all of it with shining eyes.

Below him the frost-trees spread for Gigaparsecs, their rimed boughs heavy with frozen domains, dormant Observable Existences and Elsedimensions hanging still and cold as buds that would never bloom themselvs.
The snow fell through his masked existence and did not stop. And he thought and thought and thought!
Why?

Why had a coldness that seemed woven into the very structure of existence caused Lucy to emerge from the corpse of an Immense One? Lucy, who carried a definition of Infinity so complete she had scattered Dimensions from her hands like feed, Lucy who was tied somehow to IT, to the pen behind every wall.

Why had her likeness risen out of a death and planted a forest of frozen Domains across the ruin? And the prophecy, the one the dying Stranger had left in a desert hundreds of years ago, the shattered scales and the balance that was winter and the three at the turning.
How did all of it fit together? The cold. The pen. The first thing wearing a frozen face. The Runestones!
He could feel that there was a shape to it, a single grand pattern beneath the cold and the forest and the chant. He simply could not yet see it!
And as he turned it over in the falling snow...
HUUM!
A certain crystal within his existence began to buzz.
Noah’s shining eye flickered. It was the one left behind by Vakochev, the crystal elevated when he had aided Masamuk in freeing a fragment of Vakochev. It buzzed now!
And in the midst of the falling snow, around Noah’s brilliant and barely-perceivable eye, an illusory existence began to form.

It came together slowly out of the drifting white, a thing that no ordinary gaze could have caught, a flaming outline of a humanoid figure whose features would not resolve, whose edges burned and shifted and refused to be held. It was faint, and it was vast, and it was unmistakable.
Noah’s existence shone with resplendence as he looked upon the unfathomable figure of Vakochev!
The Remnant, or an echo of it, stood in the snow above the frozen forest and gazed out across the endless white, and for a moment it said nothing. Then it spoke.

"I did not know something like this could arise from the collapse of another Immense One,"Vakochev said, his flaming gaze on the frost-trees."I did not predict it. I did not even consider it possible. But such are the weavings of existence. Always unfathomably unpredictable, no matter how high one climbs."
The snow fell between them.

"In my rage, I did many things I would not normally do. I moved without accounting for the surroundings. I stood there and spoke of the injustice of life, of decillions killed and weighed as nothing, and I did not spare a thought for the small existences here my own war would grind to paste beneath it."

A dry, tired note entered his voice."It was a bit hypocritical of me. Anyway. There is a favor owed, for what you did not long ago, when you gave a fragment of me back to the light. I have come to settle it, and so I will offer you a-"
"If I forego the favor,"Noah said, cutting him off, "and instead ask you to simply tell me what is happening in existence right now, could you do that?"
The being who had just massacred an Immense One went quiet!

For a long moment Vakochev only stood in the snow, his flaming visage turned toward the frozen forest, considering the question that a lesser being would have thought was the wisest thing to ask. Then, slowly, he shook his head.

"It would be a disservice for me to do that,"he said. "Because even someone of my power and standing cannot say with certainty what is happening in existence right now. Whatever I told you today could be wrong in a matter of days. Or years. I know only this much: every single lifeform is out for itself. I am out for my own weavings and my own interests. The Immense Ones are out for theirs. That is all that is certain."
His gaze did not leave the snow.

"A great many of us, when we reach a certain height of Dimensionality, come to believe that we understand existence. That existence is at our beck and call. We believe it so completely that the belief has blinded us. Because we can alter reality with a thought, conjure flames and constructs, distort time and lineages, manipulate the fundamental structure of what is, we decide we must be above it."

His voice went quiet and hard. "We are sorely mistaken. We do not know what we do not know. We do not even have a grasp of the shape of our own ignorance. All we have, in the end, are impossibilities."
BOOM!
Noah’s existence buzzed at the words.
His already-active reverie caught and blazed, and profound brilliance rolled out of him as boundless epiphanies bloomed one after another in the deep of his existence!

Impossibilities. Unknowns. The edge of understanding, the place where the mind gives out and names the dark past it. Infinity! It was the same truth the Runestone had shown him, the same truth Lucy had lived, spoken now by a titan in the snow, that no being ever grasps the impossible, it only ever names its own not-knowing and calls the name a mastery.
And here was one of the mightiest existences ever to live, telling him that all his immensity had bought him was a longer list of things he could not comprehend!
As Noah’s existence radiated immensity and reverie, Vakochev waved his flaming hand.

The dark crystal that had rested within Noah’s existence floated out into the snow, hung between them for a moment, and shattered. And from the breaking bloomed something Noah could not see. He strained his infinite gaze upon it and caught nothing, no shape, no color, no edge, only an absense with weight, and yet the snow whipping around the two of them buzzed, and Noah felt a sensation he had no words for, a pressure and a presence and a wrongness his existence could sense but not hold.
Vakochev cupped the invisible thing in his flaming hands.

"In lifeforms that hold no authority,"he said, "there is something called human chorionic gonadotropin. The hormone a growing embryo makes from its earliest days. Its whole task is one thing. It signals the body to sustain the pregnancy. It tells the mother’s system to keep the environment stable, to hold, so that the new life keeps growing without the mother ever consciously doing a thing. It is the molecule that says, quietly and endlessly, keep growing this. Do not stop. It works below awareness. It is the signal of becoming."
The invisible thing pulsed in his hands, and the snow buzzed with it.

"In my hands is what I believe, after a great many experiments, to be the critical factor in the emergence of an Immense One and many other things. The Existential Chorionic Gonadotropin. ECG, for short. It is the hormone of Immensity’s own gestation. It is the signal an existence produces that tells reality itself to keep growing that existence into something greater, without conscious effort, the way that other hormone tells a body to grow a child without the mother lifting a finger...among other things even I haven’t fully grasped."
Noah listened intently!

"It is not a physical substance but an authority-substance,"Vakochev went on, "produced in vanishingly small amounts within the existence of an Immense One. Where a hormone circulates in blood, this circulates in an existence’s weavings. And it is imperceptible to any being of lower Dimensionality, genuinely beneath their capacity to sense, the way an ant cannot perceive a mana. It is one of the reasons a lesser existence can stand before an Immense One and feel only pressure and wrongness rather than understand what it is looking at. Part of what it cannot perceive is this, quietly saturating the mightier being’s whole existence."
His flaming gaze turned to Noah.

"Even Immense Ones do not fully understand the thing in their own existences. It is nearly impossible to study, harder still to isolate. But this is a single unit of it, isolated externally, which I do not think anyone before me has done."

He weighed the invisible thing in his hands."It has roughly one turning of a day before it disperses back into existence and is gone. If you can understand or grasp anything of it in that time, you may make advances no one has made before!"
He was silent a moment.

"I am staunch about giving things away for free. It goes against Adversity, and Adversity is the core of my existence. So understand what this is. It is not a gift. It is an adversity, holding its own difficulty, that you may or may not benefit from, depending entirely on your own capability. There is no promise in it. There is only a chance, and a hard one.Good luck. And..."
The flaming visage turned back to the snow, and his gaze changed.

It went soft, and sorrowful, and old, a look Noah would not have expected on a being who had just torn an Immense One apart with his bare hands, and Vakochev watched the white snow fall over the frozen forest for a long moment before he spoke again, almost gentle.
"Hold those you love close. You never know when they will be gone." The snow fell through his burning outline. "In existence, there are no guarantees."
HUUM!

With those words, he took the invisible thing from his own hands and moved it toward Noah, and Noah’s masked existence unfurled to receive it, and in the taking, the flaming figure of Vakochev was gone, dissolved back into the falling snow as though he had never stood there at all.
Noah was alone above the frozen forest.

The snow fell around his brilliant unseen eye, and his Dream body held onto something it could not see, something with a terrible weight, and the instant it settled into him his existence STRAINED. It was as though the mere holding of the thing was trying to tear him apart, as though a single isolated unit of the hormone of Immensity, one drop of the substance that grew titans, was too vast and too dense for even his existence to cradle without breaking!
He roared inside himself.

There was so much he had wanted to do here. Speak with THE Creature, who had withdrawn into the cold. Reach for the weavings of THE Sealed One, or study Adrastia, the Vessel that had refused. He had planned all of it. None of it mattered now. He had one day and a thing in his hands that was trying to unmake him, and there was room in his existence for nothing else!
He had to survive what he had just been given!

So Noah pulled his infinite dream inward, out of the falling snow and the frozen forest and the sight of anything at all, drawing himself down into the space between things where nothing could reach him and nothing could bother him, a space that was his and his alone.
And there, holding an impossibility that was trying to break him, THE True Human Emperor vanished completely from all perception!

sentences.text: Far from THE Infiniverse.
Noah’s Dream body hung above the Primordial ice forest, and he looked at all of it with shining eyes.

Below him the frost-trees spread for Gigaparsecs, their rimed boughs heavy with frozen domains, dormant Observable Existences and Elsedimensions hanging still and cold as buds that would never bloom themselvs.
The snow fell through his masked existence and did not stop.
And he thought and thought and thought!
Why?
Why had a coldness that seemed woven into the very structure of existence caused Lucy to emerge from the corpse of an Immense One?
Lucy, who carried a definition of Infinity so complete she had scattered Dimensions from her hands like feed, Lucy who was tied somehow to IT, to the pen behind every wall.
Why had her likeness risen out of a death and planted a forest of frozen Domains across the ruin?
And the prophecy, the one the dying Stranger had left in a desert hundreds of years ago, the shattered scales and the balance that was winter and the three at the turning.
How did all of it fit together?
The cold.
The pen.
The first thing wearing a frozen face.
The Runestones!
He could feel that there was a shape to it, a single grand pattern beneath the cold and the forest and the chant.
He simply could not yet see it!
And as he turned it over in the falling snow...
HUUM!
A certain crystal within his existence began to buzz.
Noah’s shining eye flickered.
It was the one left behind by Vakochev, the crystal elevated when he had aided Masamuk in freeing a fragment of Vakochev.
It buzzed now!
And in the midst of the falling snow, around Noah’s brilliant and barely-perceivable eye, an illusory existence began to form.

It came together slowly out of the drifting white, a thing that no ordinary gaze could have caught, a flaming outline of a humanoid figure whose features would not resolve, whose edges burned and shifted and refused to be held.
It was faint, and it was vast, and it was unmistakable.
Noah’s existence shone with resplendence as he looked upon the unfathomable figure of Vakochev!
The Remnant, or an echo of it, stood in the snow above the frozen forest and gazed out across the endless white, and for a moment it said nothing.
Then it spoke.
"I did not know something like this could arise from the collapse of another Immense One,"Vakochev said, his flaming gaze on the frost-trees."I did not predict it.
I did not even consider it possible.
But such are the weavings of existence.
Always unfathomably unpredictable, no matter how high one climbs."
The snow fell between them.
"In my rage, I did many things I would not normally do.
I moved without accounting for the surroundings.
I stood there and spoke of the injustice of life, of decillions killed and weighed as nothing, and I did not spare a thought for the small existences here my own war would grind to paste beneath it."
A dry, tired note entered his voice."It was a bit hypocritical of me.
Anyway.
There is a favor owed, for what you did not long ago, when you gave a fragment of me back to the light.
I have come to settle it, and so I will offer you a-"
"If I forego the favor,"Noah said, cutting him off, "and instead ask you to simply tell me what is happening in existence right now, could you do that?"
The being who had just massacred an Immense One went quiet!
For a long moment Vakochev only stood in the snow, his flaming visage turned toward the frozen forest, considering the question that a lesser being would have thought was the wisest thing to ask.
Then, slowly, he shook his head.

Or years.
I know only this much: every single lifeform is out for itself.
I am out for my own weavings and my own interests.
The Immense Ones are out for theirs.
That is all that is certain."
His gaze did not leave the snow.

That existence is at our beck and call.
We believe it so completely that the belief has blinded us.
Because we can alter reality with a thought, conjure flames and constructs, distort time and lineages, manipulate the fundamental structure of what is, we decide we must be above it."
His voice went quiet and hard.

All we have, in the end, are impossibilities."
BOOM!

Impossibilities.
Unknowns.

Infinity!

It is the signal of becoming."

The Existential Chorionic Gonadotropin.

It is the hormone of Immensity’s own gestation.

chapters.title: Chapter 5755: Gonadotropin! I
paragraphs: In the space between things, the space that was his and his alone, Noah held an impossibility and felt it trying to kill him.

There was nothing here but him. He had drawn his whole attention down into a place no gaze could reach, and in the quiet of it he cradled the invisible unit of Existential Chorionic Gonadotropin that Vakochev had pressed into his hands, and his existence strained around it like a rope pulled to its last fiber!
One day. That was all the Fallen Hero had given him before the thing dispersed and was gone, and every moment of it, the holding alone was a weight that threatened to tear him open from the inside.
So he began with what he was best at.

He reached for THE Provenance of THE Human Dreamer. He dreamed. He turned his greatest craft upon the invisible unit and reached for a definition of it, like how he had reached for the shape of Infinity in the Runestone’s forest.
And he caught nothing.

No shape. No edge. No dream to read. His Provenance closed on the ECG and found only absence, not because the substance resisted him but because his dreaming could not perceive it at all. It was beneath his native craft entirely, in a register the Dreamer had no access to!
He persevered as...hours passed.

He tried again, and again, and each time came back empty, and slowly a humbling wonder settled beneath the frustration. His greatest Provenance was blind to this. The hormone that grew titans was invisible even to a being who had crossed into the Ineffable, who had authored the death of an architect, who could dream forever. He held it in his hands and could not see it!
Then Noah reached for the other Provenance.

THE Provenance of THE Immense Sovereign. The stolen thing! It never felt like his the way the Dreamer’s did. He used it rarely. Even now Thalia was working it far away upon the Vasiliou Lineage, reaching into their existential genomes and remaking them into Elselifeforms.
That was its nature. Sovereign editing, cut from an Immense One and fluent in the language of the mighty and the deep makeup of how an existence was assembled.
Noah turned it upon the invisible unit alongside his Infinity and Provenance of THE Human Dreamer, and for the first time, he barely perceived the Existential Chorionic Gonadotropin!

Barely. It came faint and wrong-angled, a thing glimpsed through a keyhole cut for a different eye. But he could sense its shape, the way it did not run in blood but in the weavings of an existence, and he could feel the single quiet task it carried into reality without pause. Keep growing this. Do not stop. Sustain the becoming!
But perceiving it was not grasping it.
He could barely sense the ECG now, but he could not hold it, could not take it into himself, because it was an Immense One’s substance and his existence was not an Immense One’s existence.
When he tried, it strained and pushed back and threatened again to tear him open, a thing of the wrong grammar forced into a vessel that could not receive it.

The turning of the day burned down toward its end, and Vakochev’s warning came back to him. This is not a gift. It is an adversity, and you may or may not benefit from it, depending entirely on your own capability.
Noah thought about impossibilities.

That was what this was. Another edge, another thing he could not seize by force no matter how much force he brought. You do not grasp the impossible. You reach a definition of it that is your own, and in the reaching, it becomes yours.
He could not take the ECG.
But perhaps he did not need to take it. Perhaps he needed to become something that could hold it!
HUUM!

The epiphany bloomed, and his straining existence caught fire with it. He would not force a thing of the wrong grammar into himself and break. He would do the only thing he had ever truly known how to do.
He would generate his own!
Noah drove both Provenances at once, and the space between things blazed with the collision of them.

The Immense Sovereign’s Provenance held the perceived ECG steady. And the Human Dreamer’s Provenance...it generated. From the deepest place of him, from nothing at all, it began to make something that was his.
He studied the model, and he found its limit.
The ECG was an infinite signal. It never stopped whispering, never ceased telling reality to grow its bearer.
But it was produced in vanishing quantities, a substance so rare even Immense Ones could barely study it in their own existences. An infinite signal, starved by a finite source.

That was its wall, and it was why immensity gestated across ages rather than instants, because the hormone that grew the mighty was endless in what it said and starved in how much of it there was to say it.
And Noah, who had spent this whole descent learning the impossible, asked the impossible question.
What if the signal itself were infinitely generated?!

Not a finite drop of an infinite hormone. An always-generating one. A source that never emptied, a thing that made itself forever and never ran dry, and yet was a single discrete substance he could own and root into himself. Infinite in its making. Finite in its being. Boundless and bounded at once.
An impossibility!

Infinity, to him, had been many things. But this was stranger. This was a thing that held two truths at once, two truths that contradicted each other, and was true in both. Finite and infinite. A contradiction that did not resolve, that did not collapse into either side, that simply stood true in both directions at the same time and did not need to choose.
Some contradictions, Noah understood in that blazing instant, are genuinely true!
His definition of the impossible was no longer only endlessness. It was also...DIALETHEIC.
The infinite that is also finite. He had struggled with this before days ago!
It simply meant he no longer had to choose between what a thing was and what it could not be. He could make a thing that was both.
So he made it!

From THE Provenance of THE Human Dreamer, from his Infinite Sanguine Mana surging warm through his weavings, from his Nine Teloi burning steady in every quark, something began to be dreamed based on the structure of THE EXISTENTIAL CHORIONIC GONADOTROPIN, and it did not stop.

His own hormone of becoming. Born, not stolen. An always-infinitely-generating authority-substance that spoke his grammar and no one else’s, a signal that told reality to keep growing him without pause or limit, made forever from the well of his own self-made existence, an impossibility that was finite and infinite at once.
|You have generated an impossibility of your own.|
|THE OSMONTIAN CHORIONIC GONADOTROPIN: an always-infinitely-generating authority-substance; the self-made hormone of your own Immensity’s gestation.|
|Your understanding of Infinity is recategorized as it has added another definition: DIALETHEIC INFINITY. A truth that is also its opposite. Finite and infinite at once.|
And it rooted!

chapters.title: Chapter 5756: Gonadotropin! II
paragraphs: It did not sit upon him like a boon bolted on from outside. It sank into him, wove down through his foundation, threaded into his two hundred decillion quarks, fused itself to his Provenance and his Teloi and the deep structure of what he was, an engine of his own ascension seated at his core and turning, and turning, and never stopping!
He would grow now. Not for free, never for free, but forever!
The Immense Ones grew on a hormone they were born to and did not understand. Noah would grow on one he had made and understood completely.
And only now, only after his own hormone was emerging infinitely within him, did he reach at last for the invisible thing Vakochev had given him.
He wanted to take it!
So he would take it!

Not because he had grown strong enough to hold an Immense One’s substance in a being that was not an Immense One. He no longer needed to. He had made a place for it. He took the Existential Chorionic Gonadotropin, the stolen impossibility of the mighty, and folded it down into his own, poured the borrowed hormone of Immensity into the endless self-made hormone of himself, and his own generation received it cleanly and made it one more thing it generated forever.
The straining stopped!
The thing that had spent a whole day trying to tear him open simply settled, quiet and whole, absorbed into a vessel built precisely to receive it!
Noah breathed out in the space between things, alone and unseen and changed.
Then... his existence began to fray at the edges.
He felt it before he understood it, a loosening, the seams of him coming apart, because a being cannot seat a thing this vast at its core and remain the being it was.
POOF!
In an instant, everything about him ceased!

In the same instant, his existence ceased. In the dream, in the sealed space between things, in THE Infiniverse where his body stood upon the golden shore, in Atlas’s Elsedimension of shattered hours, everywhere across existence that his weavings reached, every one of them ceased at once, all of him gone in a single breath!
<Sir Moriarty>
Far from anything, in a domain that existence itself had misplaced, an octopus wearing spectacles was dissecting the corpse of an Immense One.

The domain had no coordinates that any map still held. It drifted lost in existence and time both, a pocket that the ages had walked past and forgotten, and through it ran slow rivers of white and gold, currents of pure authority winding between islands of nothing.

Dimensions floated in the empty air of it, whole domains turning gently untethered, and over all of it, impossibly, fell snow, soft and constant, dusting the drifting worlds and the slow bright rivers with a fine cold white.
At the center of it all hung Moriarty.

He was vast, a titan of dark coiling flesh, a great octopus whose innumerable tentacles moved with unhurried precision, and upon what passed for his face sat a pair of spectacles, small and neat and absurd against his enormity, catching the gold of the rivers.

Before him, splayed and pinned in the drifting air, lay the corpse of an Immense One, a thing that should not have been touchable, opened and parted and studied, and Moriarty’s tentacles worked through it with the patience of a scholar who had all the time that had ever been!
He drew threads of white authority out of the dead architect, examined them, set them aside, and reached for more, murmuring to himself as he worked.
And beside his workbench of a corpse, spinning slow in the air, stood an hourglass.

It was old past reckoning, and its two bulbs were filled not with sand but with Dimensions, countless tiny domains pouring grain by grain from the upper glass to the lowwer, an entire drift of existences measuring out some span only Moriarty knew. It had turned quietly for as long as the domain had drifted.
And now, all at once, it began to buzz!

The hourglass pulsed. The Dimensions within it flared, bright and urgent, and a low resonant hum rose off the glass and spread through the snow-fall and the gold rivers, an alarm sounding in a domain that had known only silence for an age!
Moriarty’s tentacles went still.

Behind the small neat spectacles, his eyes shone, bright and sudden and cold. A pulse of pure authority released from his vast body and rippled outward through the domain, a summons flung across whatever distance needed crossing!
In the next moment, a Golden Slime appeared!

It dropped into the domain out of nothing, a shapeless blob of pure shimmering gold, and it landed upon the air and rose, and as it rose it changed. The gold flowed upward and took a shape, and the shape refined itself, and where a formless slime had been there now stood a young woman, delicate and slight, with a fall of golden hair and a face of quiet loveliness.

She held herself lightly, and the strangest thing about her was what could not be felt from her at all whatsover. No aura. No pressure. No weight of authority, no register of power, nothing. She stood in a domain built of white-gold rivers and dissected architects and gave off less presence than a candle, and she too turned her eyes toward the buzzing hourglass, and her eyes shone as brightly as his had!
"Sir Moriarty," she said softly, looking at the flaring domains pouring through the glass. "Is that..."
"The emergence of another impossibility."Moriarty’s tentacles pulsed as he spoke, rippling in slow waves down their great length.
His voice was dry and old.
"Somewhere across existence, a thing that should not be has been made. Find it, Poona. Find it before any of the others do and it is devoured yet again."
He turned one eye upon her, and the gold caught in his spectacles.
"The last impossibility I sent you to find, you failed to bring me. I have not forgotten that. If you fail this time..."
He did not finish. He did not need to.
Poona bowed, and she was smiling as she did it, a small easy smile with no fear in it at all.

"The last one was difficult, Sir. Truly it was." She straightened, unhurried. "But you needn’t worry about this one. Consider what has happened. First THE LONG NIGHT begins, and then, barely a breath later, another impossibility blooms right on its heels. That is not a coincidence. Her smile widened a fraction."I will find this impossibility for you. Until then..."
Boundless Provenance surged, and then...
WAP!
She was gone, the golden woman vanishing from the domain as suddenly as the slime had come, leaving only the falling snow and the humming glass and the vast spectacled titan among his rivers of gold.

Moriarty regarded the empty air where she had stood for a moment. Then he turned back to the corpse of the Immense One, and his tentacles resumed their patient work, drawing threads of dead authority from the opened architect, examining them in the gold light, setting them aside.
And as he worked, quietly, to himself, Moriarty spoke.
"When the scale is shattered, the shards become the floor,"he said. "When belief is spent, the cold comes walking."

A tentacle drew a long white thread from the corpse and held it up to his spectacles."What was counted shall come uncounted. The high shall be set upon the balance and asked what they weighed, and the balance shall not lie, for the balance is winter."
The snow fell over him, and the hourglass hummed, and the Dimensions poured through the glass grain by grain.

"And at the turning, count three,"Moriarty murmured, setting the thread aside and reaching into the corpse for another. "One shall look upon all that is, and grieve. One shall take up every weight, and not set it down. One shall no longer remain, and yet remain."
His shining eyes narrowed behind the small neat glasses.
"By their three hands the cloth is torn," he said softly, "or the cloth is woven anew."

He would grow now.

The Immense Ones grew on a hormone they were born to and did not understand.
Noah would grow on one he had made and understood completely.

chapters.title: Chapter 5757: The Sky Has Opened!
paragraphs: <THE True Human Emperor>
There was only darkness, and in the darkness, there was a question.
Who am I?

It drifted in the endless dark with no answer, no shape, no voice to speak it. There was nothing here. No body, no weaving, no empire, no cold. Only the dark, and the question turning slowly inside it, patient and vast and afraid!
Afraid!
What am I?
I Am, the darkness answered, faint as the first breath of anything. I Am... I Am...
HUUM!
And in that dark, a light began to blink.

It bloomed small and steady, a single point of brilliance in the endless black, and it grew, and as it grew it spoke, and its voice was grand beyond grandeur, rolling out through the dark like the first word ever said.
"I am life," it said. "I am thoughts. I am emotions, and purposes, and aims, and immensity. I am Human!"
HUUM!
The light spread, and the voice deepened, and it filled the whole of the dark with its slow tremendous certainty.

"I was born, as all life is born, as all humans are born. And I may die. This is only nature. But between life and death... I Am Osmont. And I...can feel. So much. Everything I do feel. I do not need to understand all of it. I only need to understand impossibilities."
BOOOM!
And out of the dark, existence began to build a being.

It started with a network of consciousness, a vast web of light unfolding across the black, and around that web came the quarks, two hundred decillion of them, each one a point of radiance, arranging themselves into the shape of a body.

Around the quarks flowed Provenance, blue and gold, winding through the forming lattice in slow bright rivvers. And around the Provenance flowed Infinity, crimson and gold, a boundless tide of it, pouring through and around the whole assembling shape.
And all of it, the quarks and the Provenance and the Infinity, flowed around one thing at the center. THE Osmontian Chorionic Gonadotropin.

It sat at the core of the forming existence, small and single and quiet, and it was growing. It grew infinitely, expanded infinitely, multiplied infinitely, and yet, impossibly, it remained a single Gonadotropin, one thing that was also endless, finite and infinite at once.

And every second, it pulsed. And every time it pulsed, the Infinity and the Provenance and everything gathering around the forming body swelled, grander and grander, lifted a little higher by the beat of the Root at its heart.
Prompts bloomed across the dark, vast and slow.
|THE Osmontian Chorionic Gonadotropin has formed. It is a Unique Existential Root of Immensity.|

|You are perceiving information you did not otherwise know. You now understand that across existence, there can be different types of Existential Roots of Immensity. You have now, and have always, formed your own.|
|Your Infinity will rise steadily. Your Provenance will rise steadily. Simply by existing, you will continuously elevate.|
HUUM!
And Noah felt many things.

He felt knowledge arriving in him that he had never sought, understanding pouring into his forming existence from the very act of coming into beeing, and he felt himself comprehend, all at once, so very much.

His body took its shape in the light. He looked at himself, and he saw a form that wore nothing at all, muscular and whole and bare, floating in the brilliance with its arms stretched wide, and where his eyes should have been there were two beams of blinding blue light, pouring out into the dark.
He looked at existence with those blazing eyes, and he began to understand it, and he spoke.

"For eons, lifeforms have looked into the dark and spoken the word Infinity as though it were an ocean to be crossed, or a crown to be seized, or a well that never empties. It was none of those things. It was simply the perimeter of their own exhaustion. It was the word a child uses when they can no longer count the pebbles on the shore. They met the edge of their own ability to resolve the geometry of reality, and because they could not bear to name their own blindness, they called the fog an absolute. They built thrones upon an admission of ignorance. But when the fog clears, there is no infinite abyss. There is only an unbroken, seamless equation, turning quietly in the dark, waiting for a mind vast enough to read the syntax without flinching."
And he could see it.
He could see the equation of existence, or at least the first glimpse of it, the whole of reality laid open as a single turning structure, and he read it, and he did not flinch.

"I can hear the two hundred decillion quarks in this arm agreeing with one another,"he said. "And I hear them in the exact same instant that I perceive the birth of my cells years ago, the pain why my bones grew, and the freezing of a grain of sand beneath a mortal woman’s foot in a desert I have never walked. I can feel myself then, and now, and even a little of myself in the future. They...are not separated by distance."
HUUM!

"Distance is a fiction invented by systems with localized biology to keep all of reality from happening to them at once. To an observer trapped in a single Dimension, time feels like a river, dragging you from a remembered shore toward an unknown bend. But standing here, time does not flow. It is a crystalline block. The First Sundering is occurring right now, three inches to the left of where my body rests. My birth is occurring now. My first death is happening now. My first skill book, I cast it now. The Overseeing One is dying in this exact breath, screaming, and he will always be dying there, forever preserved in the fold of that existence. I am making love right now, and I am forging the Root of my existence right now."

"Everything can be happening right now, so long as I perceive it. Many are terrified of the dark outside the room because they never realize the walls were made of their own fear. They built a cage of logic and called it an empire, never understanding that a prison with ten thousand gilded halls is still an enclosure. You do not conquer existence by accumulating its rooms. You...simply realize that you are the space in which the house was built."
BOOM!
And he felt all existence near him spread out around him like different rooms, and he understood that he could be in one of them, or in all of them at once!
He had been doing a shadow of this with his clones, his many bodies scattered across Existence.

But he saw now that he did not need the clones. A single body could do it. A single existence could stand in different places and different times at once, because separation was only a story that lesser things told themselves.
He turned his blazing gaze inward, to the Provenance rivering through him, and he spoke again.

"They treat Provenance as if it were currency. An architect hoards Causes like a miser stacking gold in a cellar, believing that if his mountain of debt grows high enough, reality will grant him a permanent seat at the table. But debt is not origin. When an Immense One speaks, his voice is layered with the stolen momentum of a trillion extinguished Dimensions. It sounds grand. It sounds terrifying. But it is entirely derivative. It is an echo bouncing between mirrors in an empty corridor. Remove the mirror, put out the borrowed lantern, and what remains? A soft, shivering lump of existence that never once learned to generate its own heat."

"Provenance is not power. It is the stubborn, irreducible refusal to exist on someone else’s terms. It is the moment an existence stops asking the sky for the parameters of its own breath and says, I am the coordinate. When my blood moves, it does not cycle because an ancient law commands the pulse. It moves because I have willed the concept of motion into my own foundation. That is why they could never break Vakochev. And that is why they will never comprehend what I have become. They are sentences written in the margins of an ancient book. I...am the hand that closed the cover, set the volume aside, and stepped out into the quiet of the morning. I Am...True."
BOOM!
And around him, pages unfurled.

Boundless, endless, they spilled out from him across the whole of the dark, sheet after sheet of light unrolling for gigaparsecs, and the darkness where he had been born filled entirely with brilliance as the pages spread. He looked down at his own hands, and his hands were pages too, countless leaves of light, and he understood that they could become countless more, that he could unfold himself across existence without end.
He looked at the pages, and he thought of a forest, and he spoke a last time, softer now.

"In the orchard where Lucy walked, Dimensions hung from the boughs like heavy plums. She did not pluck them to conquer them. She did not count them to be sure her wealth exceeded her neighbor’s. She took a Dimension in her calloused, primitive palms and scattered it across the water, simply to watch the silver fish rise and feed. She understood what all our grand philosophy has spent epochs hiding. That abundance is only monstrous when you try to own it."

"The moment you close your fist around a dream to claim it as private property, you give it a far wall. You give it a ceiling, a floor, and a date of expiration. All my life I was guilty of the same small, terrified thought. I believed Infinity was a weapon I carried in my existence. I believed my dreams were shields I had to keep raising against a hostile sky. But a dream does not need a fortress to survive. A dream needs only the absence of a final page."

" I do not hold Infinity in my hands. I dream it. And because the reverie has no boundary, even if this flesh is scattered as light across ten thousand dead Dimensions, the dreamer does not cease. The dream only expands to fill the dark. There is...no longer any separation between what I desire, and what I am, and what existence must become. The stage has dissolved. The actors have gone home. And the sky has finally opened."
He drew one breath in the endless light.
"The sky has opened."
BOOM!

chapters.title: Chapter 5758: Glorious Capabilities I
paragraphs: In the space where there had been only darkness, Noah’s brilliance spread out in every direction, and he brought his hands together.
Between his palms, a singularity bloomed!

It was blinding, a point of impossible density and light, and it was not empty. Noah drew it wider, and within it turned a whole domain, an empire vaster than hundreds of Dimensions laid together, seas of blue-gold, realms upon realms, a chrysalis of sleeping dreamers, an ocean that turned quietly with two sisters weaving upon it. THE Infiniverse!
He had reached and drawn the whole of his home into the singularity between his hands, into this space that was only his!
He looked at it, cradled in the brilliance, and he named the space that held it.
"Here, my existence can stand across time and space at once," he said.

"It is mine. Entirely mine. And unless a thing bears my signature and my power, and unless I wish it, nothing will ever enter here. Let this be the one place in all of existence that answers to no one but me. My...Existential Root."
WAA!
Then he waved his hand.

From THE Infiniverse, countless strings erupted, threads of light that stretched outward from the singularity and reached across the dark to touch illusory points hanging in the distance, every one of them a Dimension over which his empire had spread its influence! The strings connected, taut and bright, a web of belonging strung between his home and everything it had ever reched.
He could pull them here if he wished. He could draw every Dimension he held into this space and make it all safe with him.
He did not.

A life had to draw its boundaries. This was his space, and it would hold only what it needed to hold, no more. He would not hoard existence the way the architects hoarded it. His home was here, secure, and that was enough.
And it was truly secure now!

What had been his home, and was his home, and would always be his home, was sealed inside a space that answered to him alone. Even the beings whose Dimensionality stood higher than his own at this moment, even they could not reach this place, for a simple and absolute reason. They were not him!
With that done, Noah turned his blazing eyes outward again, and the sense of the vast turning equation of existence returned to him, and he spoke on.

"Time is relative. Distance is relative. Even now I am perceiving countless things at once, receiving knowledge that flows into me depending on where I am, and where I have been. And where I am and where I have been can be considered the same thing, the moment I set distance aside. Which means I should, in theory, be able to..."

He waved his hand, slow, as though rewinding something. But he was not rewinding anything. He was only taking himself, one point of his own existence, and displacing it toward another point, moving through the crystalline block of time the way a reader moves a finger down a page!
Existence flickered. It was as though pages were being unwound around him, leaf after leaf turning back.
And in an instant, because time was relative, Noah found himself gazing once more upon a Primordial forest.

The trees stood ancient and vast, budding Dimensions and Observable Existences upon their boughs like ripening fruit. And at the edge of a bright, quick river knelt an unfathomable existence, a small rough figure with her calloused hands cupped over the water, producing an endless stream of genuine Dimensions and pouring them down to the silver fish, who rose and gobbled them up as fast as she could make them!
He had been here before. He had been shown this, once, in a Runestone’s vision, as a distant observer.
This time, Noah took a step!
He moved from being a watcher of the record into the record itself, one clean stride across the impossible, and he appeared beside her on the riverbank!
The contrast between them was stark. Noah stood tall and radiant, a being of blazing blue light and blue-gold Provenance, freshly reforged, brilliant and new.
And she was small, and hunched, and rough, a caveman thing of thick limbs and unadorned skin, and yet she was beautiful, a terrible ancient beauty that had never once needed anything to make it so.
She turned her head and looked at him.
And she smiled. Fiendishly, exactly as the record had smiled at him before, a small knowing curve that should not have been possible on the face of a thing inside a memory!
"We are standing at a moment in time that can be considered a memory," Noah said.

"A record. And also, existence. I have never stood here, and I have stood here, because I am standing here right now. This is a record drawn from a Hieroglyph Runestone, and I have imposed my existence into it, so that I might learn more. Hello. I Am..."
"Osmont."
BOOM!
Lucy spoke, for the first time ever, and her voice alone was resonant and grand, a sound with the weight of the beginning of things in it.

She turned to him and rose from the river, and even as she rose she did not stop, her hands still cupped, still pouring out an endless stream of Dimensions into the water behind her without a single thought given to it.

"I have always had this conversation with you,"she said. "Whether from a record of information or not. And I can see you have only just formed your Root, little guy, because you are looking at everything through that lens of past, present, and future, turning it over and over as though the distincton meant something."
Her fiendish smile softened, just barely.

"Relax. You are at the very beginning of your existence, only now setting out to gather what there is to know. In the beginning, all of us feel this way, this sense of being invincible, of having finally seen the whole shape of things. Be careful of it. Be cautious. Your existence is new, and a new existence can still be attacked in a great many ways."

" This beginning stage of life you are experiencing now is also the stage that has the highest rate of mortality. All because of that feeling of invincibility that makes you feel like you can go anywhere and do anything. While somewhat true it is also not. You are only starting out as there are others much grander than you. Be careful."

chapters.title: Chapter 5759: Glorious Capabilities II
paragraphs: Noah looked at her with shining eyes, and it was a surreal thing, and all the while his newly-forged existence drank knowledge from the record around him, more and more of it, pouring in. He nodded, slow and thoughtful.
He had felt an overwhelming sense of control and power that almost gave this feeling of invincibility!
He definitely needed to still be cautious as he continued to absorb waves and waves of knowledge.
"You are a record of something that happened in the past," he said. "Even though we now talk, you are..."
"I am not here. Yes." She interrupted him gently, still walking now, moving away from the river.
"This is my record. My existence itself left long ago. And in words that will mean something to you now, I am not one of Those Who Remain. Because I did not remain."
She glanced back at him, and there was something old and unreadable in it. "But you came here for information. So ask away."
And then she stopped pouring the Dimensions.

The endless stream ceased, and the fish scattered sated into the bright water, and Lucy turned and began to walk across the river and into the forest, her bare feet passing over the surface as though it were ground, and Noah drifted beside her, floating over the water, radiant and new beside the small ancient thing.
"An endless cold has begun to spread across existence," Noah said, keeping pace with her through the trees of budding worlds.

"It hunts the mighty. And from the corpse of a slain Immense One, your likeness, your image, rose up out of the death and planted a forest of frozen Domains across existence...just like what we see here. Why? What can you tell me about THE LONG NIGHT?"
Noah asked the question without expecting much of an answer.

But he knew he had come to the right place. The moment this entity had confirmed she had once stood upon the same stage he had only just climbed onto, he understood that whatever she gave him would be worth the hearing, even if it came wrapped in riddles.
Lucy was thoughtful for a moment. Then she spoke, and she did not stop walking as she did.

"Existence is not static," she said, moving through the forest of budding domains with her bare feet passing light over root and water alike. "For weaker lifeforms, for those like you were before you took this recent step, existence looks as though it has always been the way they found it. They simply have not lived long enough to know better."

She lifted a hand as she walked, and where she gestured a dead grey tree at the forest’s edge shuddered and bloomed, budding a fresh Dimension upon a new-grown bough. She did not so much as glance at it. It was nothing to her, a habit, the way a person might trail a hand along a wall in passing.
"The Long Night was something many knew was coming, if they were old enough. Because they know existence is not static. Because they know that existence moves in cycles."

She glanced back at him, and there was that old unreadable thing in her eyes. "You may notice my words are cryptic. That is because even I do not fully know what The Long Night will bring. Consider it a change in existence, arriving after certain conditions have been met. No more than that, because I know no more than that."
They walked on, and around her the forest answered her presence without her willing it, Dimensions ripening and falling and rising again in her wake.

"As for why a manifestation of my existence would bloom out of a dead thing," she went on, "my immensity left a mark. Existence remembers what was exceptional in it, and my weavings were exceptional enough to be rememberd. So a memory of them was chosen, called up out of the deep of things. I would likely be only one among many memories that might see a resurgence, before this is done."

She waved her hand again, idly, and a river some distance off changed its course to flow the other way! "But...I am not here. Not your version of here. You are young, and you have only just forged your Root. Take the time to explore, and to understand."
Noah listened, and drank in every word, and the record around him poured knowledge into his newborn existence as she spoke.

"You will come to find," Lucy said, "that trying to grasp the secrets of existence by asking a senior will never be quite so pleasurable as finding them out yourself. Existence is grand. It is more beautiful than you can yet imagine."

She stopped, and turned, and looked at him fully. "You have not even left your Existential Root Domain, have you? Seeing how impatient you are for answers, you must have come here the very instant it formed."
He said nothing.

Her fiendish smile returned, gentler this time. "Do not get lost in old records and old pasts, little guy. Even though we experience time differently, we of the Root, the present is always the grandest thing there is. Even we cannot change the past by very much. A friend of mine used to tell me to focus on the present. It is a gift. That is why it is called the present."
She turned back toward the forest and walked on. "Go and experience existence for the first time, now that your Root has emerged. You will find that it is beautiful."
Noah’s eyes shone at that, and he nodded slowly.

"I will not keep you much longer,"he said. "So I will ask only one last thing. For someone like me, who is just emerging, just being born into what I now am, what is the single most important thing I should know right now, for my survival?"
What was the most important thing he should know?
The question lit Lucy’s eyes, and she smiled, and this time it was almost fond.

"In existence, there are two kinds of Root," she said. "Conceptual Existential Roots, and Physical Existential Roots. The first gives rise to Empyros Immense Lifeforms. The second to Fiend Immense Lifeforms. Most Roots are conceptual, as yours is, as most of what you will meet will be."

She paused, and the fondness in her face sharpened into something like a warning. "So for your survival...do not offend those who bear a Physical Existential Root. And in the future to come, do not offend a Fiend Immense Lifeform. Take it step by step, and attain your Immensity in your own time. And know that there is sometimes no harm at all in being low key."
She began to turn away.
"Good luck, Osmont. I hope you do not become one of Those Who Remain."Her voice dropped. "That would be such a shame. Such a shame."
HUUM!
She took a single step, and everything began to shake!

The forest trembled. The river shivered. The budding domains swayed upon their boughs, and Noah understood, without being told, that she simply did not wish to share anything more. The conversation was over because she had decided it was over!
He nodded, and he did not press her.
"Thank you,"he said.

And then Noah looked at the figure of Lucy one last time, the small rough ancient thing pouring Domains from her hands at the beginning of all existence, and he held her image in his newborn existence as though ingranining it there, a thing he did not want to forget.
Then he took a step of his own, and he left the grand record behind.
He had gathered more threads of knowledge than he had come for, and now, he wanted only one thing.
He wanted to see, for the first time, just how different existence looked through the eyes of what he had become!
