chapters.title: Chapter 5760: Existence Is Not Empty!
paragraphs: Noah stepped out of the record and back into the present.

He arrived where the Dimensional Provenance Train had been cut open, where Vakochev had cleaved it in two and an architect had died and a frost-visage had planted its forest. Hours had passed here while he had been figuring out the Existential Chorionic Gonadotropin.

The frost-forest had grown thicker, its rimed boughs heavier with frozen Dimensions, and the region for gigaparsecs around had emptied out, the hunters gone, the watchers gone, the snow still falling silent over the ruin. It looked, at a glance, like an abandoned place. A dead one.
Then Noah looked at it with the eyes he had now, and he saw that it was nothing of the kind.
Existence was not empty. It had never been empty! He simply had never been able to see.

Above him, through the foamy void that he had always taken for a formless dark, there rose pillars. Vast ones. They climbed up out of the deep of existence and stretched away in every direction, structures so enormous that a single one dwarfed whole clusters of Dimensions themselvs, and they were everywhere, a forest of them far grander than the frozen one below, reaching endlessly across the void. And they coursed with authority!
Some shone blue from root to unseen peak, boundless Infinity pouring up their length. Others ran obsidian with THE Primordial Source, dark and dense and old.
Others gleamed white with the woven light of THE Argent Loom. And others still burned in colors Noah had no names for, flowing endlessly upward, downward, and outward through the structures.

They were strange to look at, because they were solid and they were not. He could see the shape of each pillar clearly, and yet he could see through it too, as though it were both a thing and the absence of a thing, hollow and present at once. He reached out and laid his hand against the nearest, a great blue column of pure Infinity, and the moment he touched it, prompts bloomed across his sight.
|You are perceiving an EXISTENTIAL CONDUIT.|

|The Conduits are the channels through which the authorities of existence flow, threaded through the whole of the void the way rivers and seas are threaded through a world. Infinity, THE Primordial Source, THE Argent Loom, and authorities beyond your knowing move along them without end.|
|They are the veins of existence itself.|
Noah drew his hand back slowly.

Existence was not a formless dark scattered with worlds. It was this. It was an endless architecture of flowing authority, seas and rivers of power moving through the deep in structures grander than anything he had ever built, and it had always been here, all around him, in every place he had ever stood!
And it now stood surrounded by whites of snow.

He had walked through it his whole existence and never once seen it, because to see it, one had to stand where he now stood. The cruelest part of that beauty was that almost nothing alive could perceive it. Only the very greatest existences could look at the deep of things and see how unfathomably lovely it truly was.
And it was not only the Conduits!
Something moved along them.
Across the void, across miles and light years and gigaparsecs, drifting between the great pillars and perched upon them, were living things. Small ones.

They were the equivalent of the flies and critters and birds a person might see drifting through any forest on any world, and they were everywhere, thousands of them turning lazily through the space of a single nearby light year alone.

Each one was incandescent, a small bright shape of pure light, delicate and strange, with wings or fins or trailing streamers of radiance that caught the colors of the Conduits they drifted near. Many were perched upon the great pillars, still and peaceful, and Noah understood, watching them, that they were drinking.

They sipped at the flowing authorities like how insects sip at nectar, feeding quietly on the rivvers of Infinity and Primordial Source and THE Argent Loom, minding their own small business in the veins of existence.
Prompts settled across his sight as he watched them.
|You are perceiving CONDUIT LIFEFORMS.|

|They dwell in the flow of the Existential Conduits and feed upon the authorities that move there, and the authority feeds on them. They are imperceptible to beings of insufficient Dimensionality and standing. Dimensionality alone is not enough. One must also hold the standing to perceive them, and only once perceived can they perceive you in turn, and interact.|
And their measures opened to him.
|CONDUIT LIFEFORM|
|VERITAS: ~150. POTENTIA: ~150. PONDUS: ~150. PROVENANCE: 0.|

Noah went still with the wonder of it. These small drifting critters, these flies of the deep that no lesser being could ever even see, carried attributes at a hundred and fifty across the board. Every one of them!

They were, by the raw numbers, mightier than most of the beings he had fought his whole climb, mightier than kingdoms and lineages and armies, and they did nothing with it at all! They only drifted, and drank, and buzzed peacefully through the veins of existence, because they held not a single point of Provenance between them. They had never generated a thing. They simply were, at that height, the way a fish simply is at the bottom of a sea, born to a depth that would crush anything not made for it.
One of them, wrapped in trailing rivers of light, came drifting curiously toward him.

It floated close as its wings flapped, turning about his radiant form as though it had never seen a thing quite like him, and Noah, moved by something he could not name, raised his hand. The little creature came and perched upon his outstretched finger, light as nothing, incandescent, and it made a single melodious sound, a small clear note that rang through the void like struck crystal!
Then it lifted from his finger and drifted away, back to its Conduit, back to its peaceful drinking, indifferent and lovely.
Noah watched it go.

Existence was abundant! It was vast! It was so much more, and so much more beautiful, than the empty dark he had always believed it to be. Everywhere he had ever looked and seen nothing, there had been this, oceans of authority and small bright living things drifting through them, a whole existence beneath the Existence, waiting for eyes grand enough to find it.
And at such a thought... his gaze hardened!

He rolled his neck slowly, and the wonder in him cooled into something colder and more familiar, because a thing this beautiful was a thing that had to be protected. His own existence was beautiful. His empire, sealed now in the space that was only his. His people, dreaming their centuries. His mother, his children, all of it.

And there were things in existence that threatened what was his, that had always threatened it, and Noah found himself wondering, standing here newly-born among the veins of existence, whether he could do something about them now.
THE Sealed One. THE SLEEPLESS FIEND. THE UNPAID COLLECTOR, who had sworn to rip Thalia in half at any moment he held her.

He was not an Immense One. He knew that. He had only just forged his Root, only just begun. He was not so foolish as to think a single step of becoming had made him the equal of the beings whose war he could not even perceive. But he wanted to know where he stood now!

He wanted to know if he could mount an offensive against even the weakest of the things that hunted him, against THE Sealed One at the least. It was one of many things he meant to test as he grew into what he had become.
And that raised the simplest question of all.
Where did his attributes even stand, now that his Root had emerged?!

He closed his eyes. He breathed in, drawing the cold and the light and the flowing authority of the deep into his newborn existence. And he turned his gaze inward, upon himself, to see exactly what he had become.
And he could not help it.
He smiled!

sentences.text: Noah stepped out of the record and back into the present.
He arrived where the Dimensional Provenance Train had been cut open, where Vakochev had cleaved it in two and an architect had died and a frost-visage had planted its forest.
Hours had passed here while he had been figuring out the Existential Chorionic Gonadotropin.

The frost-forest had grown thicker, its rimed boughs heavier with frozen Dimensions, and the region for gigaparsecs around had emptied out, the hunters gone, the watchers gone, the snow still falling silent over the ruin.
It looked, at a glance, like an abandoned place.
A dead one.
Then Noah looked at it with the eyes he had now, and he saw that it was nothing of the kind.
Existence was not empty.
It had never been empty!
He simply had never been able to see.
Above him, through the foamy void that he had always taken for a formless dark, there rose pillars.
Vast ones.

They climbed up out of the deep of existence and stretched away in every direction, structures so enormous that a single one dwarfed whole clusters of Dimensions themselvs, and they were everywhere, a forest of them far grander than the frozen one below, reaching endlessly across the void.
And they coursed with authority!
Some shone blue from root to unseen peak, boundless Infinity pouring up their length.
Others ran obsidian with THE Primordial Source, dark and dense and old.
Others gleamed white with the woven light of THE Argent Loom.
And others still burned in colors Noah had no names for, flowing endlessly upward, downward, and outward through the structures.
They were strange to look at, because they were solid and they were not.
He could see the shape of each pillar clearly, and yet he could see through it too, as though it were both a thing and the absence of a thing, hollow and present at once.
He reached out and laid his hand against the nearest, a great blue column of pure Infinity, and the moment he touched it, prompts bloomed across his sight.
|You are perceiving an EXISTENTIAL CONDUIT.|
|The Conduits are the channels through which the authorities of existence flow, threaded through the whole of the void the way rivers and seas are threaded through a world.
Infinity, THE Primordial Source, THE Argent Loom, and authorities beyond your knowing move along them without end.|
|They are the veins of existence itself.|
Noah drew his hand back slowly.
Existence was not a formless dark scattered with worlds.
It was this.

It was an endless architecture of flowing authority, seas and rivers of power moving through the deep in structures grander than anything he had ever built, and it had always been here, all around him, in every place he had ever stood!
And it now stood surrounded by whites of snow.
He had walked through it his whole existence and never once seen it, because to see it, one had to stand where he now stood.
The cruelest part of that beauty was that almost nothing alive could perceive it.
Only the very greatest existences could look at the deep of things and see how unfathomably lovely it truly was.
And it was not only the Conduits!
Something moved along them.
Across the void, across miles and light years and gigaparsecs, drifting between the great pillars and perched upon them, were living things.
Small ones.

They were the equivalent of the flies and critters and birds a person might see drifting through any forest on any world, and they were everywhere, thousands of them turning lazily through the space of a single nearby light year alone.
Each one was incandescent, a small bright shape of pure light, delicate and strange, with wings or fins or trailing streamers of radiance that caught the colors of the Conduits they drifted near.
Many were perched upon the great pillars, still and peaceful, and Noah understood, watching them, that they were drinking.

They sipped at the flowing authorities like how insects sip at nectar, feeding quietly on the rivvers of Infinity and Primordial Source and THE Argent Loom, minding their own small business in the veins of existence.
Prompts settled across his sight as he watched them.
|You are perceiving CONDUIT LIFEFORMS.|
|They dwell in the flow of the Existential Conduits and feed upon the authorities that move there, and the authority feeds on them.
They are imperceptible to beings of insufficient Dimensionality and standing.
Dimensionality alone is not enough.
One must also hold the standing to perceive them, and only once perceived can they perceive you in turn, and interact.|
And their measures opened to him.
|CONDUIT LIFEFORM|
|VERITAS: ~150.
POTENTIA: ~150.
PONDUS: ~150.
PROVENANCE: 0.|
Noah went still with the wonder of it.
These small drifting critters, these flies of the deep that no lesser being could ever even see, carried attributes at a hundred and fifty across the board.
Every one of them!
They were, by the raw numbers, mightier than most of the beings he had fought his whole climb, mightier than kingdoms and lineages and armies, and they did nothing with it at all!
They only drifted, and drank, and buzzed peacefully through the veins of existence, because they held not a single point of Provenance between them.
They had never generated a thing.
They simply were, at that height, the way a fish simply is at the bottom of a sea, born to a depth that would crush anything not made for it.
One of them, wrapped in trailing rivers of light, came drifting curiously toward him.
It floated close as its wings flapped, turning about his radiant form as though it had never seen a thing quite like him, and Noah, moved by something he could not name, raised his hand.

The little creature came and perched upon his outstretched finger, light as nothing, incandescent, and it made a single melodious sound, a small clear note that rang through the void like struck crystal!
Then it lifted from his finger and drifted away, back to its Conduit, back to its peaceful drinking, indifferent and lovely.
Noah watched it go.
Existence was abundant!
It was vast!
It was so much more, and so much more beautiful, than the empty dark he had always believed it to be.

Everywhere he had ever looked and seen nothing, there had been this, oceans of authority and small bright living things drifting through them, a whole existence beneath the Existence, waiting for eyes grand enough to find it.
And at such a thought... his gaze hardened!
He rolled his neck slowly, and the wonder in him cooled into something colder and more familiar, because a thing this beautiful was a thing that had to be protected.
His own existence was beautiful.
His empire, sealed now in the space that was only his.
His people, dreaming their centuries.
His mother, his children, all of it.

And there were things in existence that threatened what was his, that had always threatened it, and Noah found himself wondering, standing here newly-born among the veins of existence, whether he could do something about them now.
THE Sealed One.
THE SLEEPLESS FIEND.
THE UNPAID COLLECTOR, who had sworn to rip Thalia in half at any moment he held her.
He was not an Immense One.
He knew that.
He had only just forged his Root, only just begun.
He was not so foolish as to think a single step of becoming had made him the equal of the beings whose war he could not even perceive.
But he wanted to know where he stood now!
He wanted to know if he could mount an offensive against even the weakest of the things that hunted him, against THE Sealed One at the least.
It was one of many things he meant to test as he grew into what he had become.
And that raised the simplest question of all.
Where did his attributes even stand, now that his Root had emerged?!
He closed his eyes.
He breathed in, drawing the cold and the light and the flowing authority of the deep into his newborn existence.
And he turned his gaze inward, upon himself, to see exactly what he had become.
And he could not help it.
He smiled!

chapters.title: Chapter 5761: Grand!
paragraphs: Noah opened his eyes upon himself!
|THE True Human Emperor / THE Human Dreamer|
|VERITAS: 500|
|PROVENANCE: 500|
|POTENTIA: INFINITE|
|PONDUS: 500|
|OSMONTIAN MOIRAI: 500|
|Provenances: THE Provenance of THE Human Dreamer (native, generated), THE Provenance of THE Immense Sovereign (claimed).|
|Infinity: DIALETHEIC INFINITY. A truth that is also its opposite; finite and infinite at once.|
|Existential Root: THE Osmontian Chorionic Gonadotropin. A Unique Existential Root of Immensity. A clear determination has not been made on whether it is Conceptual or Physical. |
He looked at the numbers for a while, and then he smiled. But...was his Root not a Conceptual one?
He only hung on this for a moment before he moved to the numbers.

Five hundred! Across the board, save for the Potentia that had always been Infinite and always would be. He had walked into that darkness carrying attributes in the two hundreds and walked out with five hundred, and the jump alone should have staggered him.

It did not, quite, because some part of him beneath the numbers already knew he was no longer the thing that had gone into the dark. The count was only existence catching up to a fact he had felt in his weavings the moment he reformed.

He turned the panel over. Two Provenances threading through him now, the Dreamer’s warm and his own, the Immense Sovereign’s cold and borrowed. His Infinity, which had stopped being merely endless and become Dialetheic, true in two directions at once. And under all of it, turning and pulsing and refusing to stop, the Root.
He reached in and tapped THE Osmontian Chorionic Gonadotropin, and it answered him, and more of it opened.
|THE Osmontian Chorionic Gonadotropin: preliminary functions.|
|TONIC DIMENSIONAL HYPERTROPHY (passive growth without effort).|

|Through the Root, your existence behaves as an embryonic system undergoing spontaneous expansion. It continuously secretes new layers of dimensional thickness. It increases the mass of individual quarks without the ingeston of any foreign energy. It raises your baseline Provenance, Veritas, and Pondus through metabolic background alone.Approximate range: an increase of 30 to 50 or more across all attributes per day, scaling upward as the Root grows.The range depends upon your state. Slumbering or passive, you grow at the floor. Actively moving to influence existence, you grow at the ceiling. You may grow without effort. But existence remains full of adversity, and the fastest climb is still to meet adversity and expand your knowledge.|
Noah read that twice, and then he laughed!

He could sit still and grow. He could lie down in the snow and slumber for an age and do absolutely nothing, and he would rise regardless, thirty to fifty points a day welling up out of him without a single act of will, and more than that as the Root deepened.
He read on.
|THE PREVENTION OF CAUSAL LUTEOLYSIS (inhibition of structural decay).|

|An existence that ceases to fight, cultivate, or refine itself normally suffers structural atrophy, bleeding density back into existential entropy. Your Root constantly pulses to reject this. Your foundation will never regress, never degrade, and never leak authority back into the surrounding existence, no matter how many epochs you spend motionless.|
|CAUSAL INFORMATIONAL ANGIOGENESIS.|
|Your Root passively communicates with the bodies of existence around you and draws information from them. It may be prompted to reach as far as your existence can bear, to receive more.|
So he would grow, and never rot, and drink the knowledge of wherever he stood without asking. A hard thing not to feel pleased about!
He let himself feel pleased about it for exactly a moment, and then he made himself set the pleasure down.

His power was grand, and it was terrifying, and he had genuinely not expected the leap to be this large. But then, he had not done this alone. Vakochev had handed him a gateway and called it an adversity. A single unit of the hormone that grew titans, pressed into his hands with a warning and a shrug, and Noah had done the only thing he had ever known how to do with adversity, which was to build something of his own out of it.
The Existential Chorionic Gonadotropin had never become his power. It had become fuel, folded down into a Root that was entirely his make.

Whether he would have formed the Root at all in so short a span without the favor, he could not say. Perhaps in a month or year. And looking now at the weavings of time in the strange new way his existence perceived them, he found he could no longer see Vakochev as a chance encounter.

The Fallen Hero had been a piece of a puzzle, and so had Noah, the hand that saved the a part of him that rose and cleaved the Train and killed an Immense One. He saved a piece of Vakochev, and it led to all this!
But the power changed everything about how he could move.

He held a Root of Immensity. And it was, for now, exactly that, and no more. A root. A seed cracked open, not a tree. It had to grow, endlessly, until it bloomed into something Immense, and until then he was a very strong sapling in a forest full of things that ate saplings.
So caution. He told himself, because the feeling underneath it did not want to hear it.
The feeling was invincibility!
It flooded his whole newborn existence, above everything else, an absolute conviction that he could do anything.
Lucy had named it to his face not long ago.

In the beginning, all of us feel this way. The sense of having finally seen the whole shape of things. He felt so grand and so untouchable that his mind was already racing ahead of his good sense, wanting to hunt down every vessel of THE Sealed One across all of time and space at once, wanting to fling his existence after the Immense Ones who had chased Vakochev into the dark, wanting to do a dozen mad and glorious things and feeling, in the weavings of his new Root, that he could do every one of them without a shred of worry.
He breathed in. He paused. He held himself still.

His people were safe. He was safe. His empire was sealed in a space that answered to no one but him. So why go kicking over stones the moment he had learned to walk again, before he had digested a single thing about what he now was?
He could hunt the truth of The Long Night without lighting a war he was not yet built to survive. Because he could feel what his Root allowed, and in the same breath he could feel where it stopped.

He counted himself lucky, honestly. The Immense Ones gathered here had never once looked twice at him, their whole attention on themselves and then on Vakochev, and a masked eye at the rim had been beneath their concern.

But a few more minutes of any one of those gazes settling on him would have made it clear enough that he was not one of them. That he was something else, wearing the shape of a harmless watcher. He had survived on being small. He would keep being small a little longer.
So. For now...
Noah smiled, and raised his hand, and countless illusory pages flickered off of him and drifted through the falling snow.
"I could find and grasp rare Gu easily now," he murmured, "and see whether that path has anything in store for me. And when it comes to Atlas and Time..."
His eyes shone.
Because after his cessation and his reforging, he had chosen a few places across existence for his newborn self to occupy at once, and Atlas’s Elsedimension of shattered hours was one of them.

Even now a part of him stood among the broken clocks and the numbered meteorites, and he turned that attention there, and he compared. The Existential Conduits that threaded those frozen hours. The Conduit Lifeforms drifting through them. He set them against what he saw here, in the veins of existence above the sundered Train, and read the differences between them, and learned.
And then his gaze settled on the illusory ring he had worn all this while. The ring that was Atlas.
He could see it clearly now! For the first time, Noah could see the ring for exactly what it was!

chapters.title: Chapter 5762: A Delectable Treat! I
paragraphs: Noah held the illusory ring in his hands, and turned it, and looked at it with the eyes he had now.

"You are a glimmer of an Existential Chorionic Gonadotropin," he said slowly, "worn inside the shape of a ring. That is what you are. That is what you have always been, and I could never see it until now."

He turned it again in his fingers. "So tell me. How did you manage that, when the Immense Ones shattered your existence to pieces? Or is your own Root of Immensity so grand that even they could not shatter it?"
For a long moment, there was only silence.
The snow fell. The clock-hands of Atlas’s Dimension turned somewhere far away in another of his bodies. And the ring sat quiet in his hands, and Noah waited.
Then the old engineer spoke.
|It seems you have had quite a leap,| Atlas said.

|A major one, in a very short span. When you ceased, all of you at once, I will admit I braced for the worst. I thought an Immense One had finally caught your scent and made a move. But no. You were only grasping your own Root of Immensity.|

|Which, for the record, I had intended to help you form much, much later. After we had raised your Provenance and the depth of your existence a great deal higher. How you jumped that many steps in a little, I have no idea, and I have decided not to think too hard about it, because thinking too hard about you gives me a ringache.|
Noah’s mouth pulled at one corner.

|But you asked me a question,| Atlas went on, quieter. |So. Yes. In the tools I engineered, I spread my Root of Immensity. Every relic, every workshop, every ring, every hidden thing I ever made. I wove glimmers of my own Existential Chorionic Gonadotropin into all of them. Do you understand what that means?|

He did not wait to find out.|It means that as long as one of my tools survived anywhere in existence, some fragment of my Root survived with it. They broke my body on their anvil. They collapsed my homes into ash. And they thought they were done. But they could never find every tool. And if they could never eliminate my tools, then they could never, truly, eliminate me.|
Noah looked at the ring in his hands calmly.
"So this whole time," Noah said."I have been carrying part of you."
|A small part. A glimmer. Enough to talk, to teach, to scheme. Not enough to walk out and reforge myself, which is the great inconvenience of my situation.|
Noah let that sit a moment and then he asked the thing underneath everything.

"What is your purpose, really? With me. You spread yourself through your tools, and you gave a great ring to THE REMINISCING WIDOW, which means you may even have her help now. Existence is give and take. You told me I could make the impossible possible, and I suppose I have just proven a little of that."
He held the ring up."But what is the endgame? What are you actually after?"
And there was silence again!

|When an Immensity is destroyed,| Atlas said at last,|it does not simply come back. No matter how grand the being was. No matter how much of it survives in glimmers and tools. When you rebuild an Immensity that was broken, you never get the same power back. You come back smaller. Diminished. A great fire relit from one saved ember, and it never burns as tall as it did before.|
The ring pulsed faintly.

|Which means that even if I clawed my way back into a body, I would not be able to do the thing I most need to do. I could not take down the ones I need to take down. Not the way I am now. Not the way I would come back.|

|So there is revenge in it. There is a great deal of revenge in it. But there is also the simpler thing. The capability to do what I no longer can. If you grow grand enough, Dreamer. If you become truly, unfathomably grand. Then maybe, one day, you will be grand enough to fully restore an Immensity that was broken. To relight the fire without losing the height. Maybe. Who knows.|
The old engineer’s voice was quiet and honest and unashamed.
|It is all for my own selfish reasons, in the end. Even as I help you along. Do not ever mistake me for a kind old man. I am a very selfish one who happens to be teaching you.|

Noah listened to all of it, and he did not flinch from it, because a selfish reason honestly stated was a thing he could trust far more than a kind one. He looked at the ring once more, and opened his mouth to answer.
And Atlas blinked.
|Oh, fuck.|
The old engineer’s projection went rigid, as though he had forgotten something and only just remembered it in the worst possible moment.

|Right. Right, I am an idiot. Dreamer, listen to me. Hide yourself. All of you, every body, get all of your existence into your Existential Root Domain right now, this instant. How did I forget this? How did I forget the single most obvious thing?!|

The words came fast and alarmed. |Inside an Elsedimension they have no access to, you are hard to reach. But out here, a newly formed Root of Immensity? Some Immense Ones can smell that! A fresh Root reaching its weavings out into open existence is a scent, and it is a rare and delicious one, and you are broadcasting it right now like a lit fire in a dark forest!|
Noah’s eyes pulsed as his teacher had a gift for delivering the worst news at the last possible second.
HUUM!
Because in that instant, he felt his existence buzz, the part of him still standing in the frozen forest where the Train had been split, and information came flooding in from that body all at once.
|THE UNPAID COLLECTOR smells something unique left behind in this place.|
|THE SLEEPLESS FIEND is surprised. He says that whatever has been found here is his.|

Noah’s newborn Root drank the information from that body in a single breath, and he sensed it the malicious weavings of Immensity surging back toward the frozen forest, two of the beings whose war he could not perceive turning their terrible attention toward the fresh scent of a Root that should not exist!
He moved decisively.
He hurled his existence toward his Existential Root Domain, toward the sealed space that answered to no one but him, the one place in all of existence that not even an Immense One could enter!
HUUM!

His existence had already begun to fade, in the span of an instant, dissolving out of the frozen forest toward safety, and he could feel the tug of his impenetrable space reaching to receive him, pulling him home.
But.
An undeniable force closed around him and pulled him back!

It was not a thing he could fight. It seized his fading existence the way a hand seizes a fleaf in the wind, absolute and effortless, and it dragged him back out of his retreat, back toward the frozen forest, back into the open where the scent of his Root hung bright and exposed.
|THE SLEEPLESS FIEND says: friend. Do not go quite yet. Come back out here.|
An undeniable force pulled him, and Noah’s eyes went cold.
He set his newborn will against the impossible grip, and in the same instant he made his decision!
Because he would not be caught, would not be held, would not be dragged before an Immense One to be studied and cracked open.

If he could not escape, then he would simply cease. He would dissipate his existence here completely, this body, this presence, all of it, scatter himself to nothing before any Immense One could close a hand around what he had become!

"You are a glimmer of an Existential Chorionic Gonadotropin," he said slowly, "worn inside the shape of a ring.
That is what you are.
That is what you have always been, and I could never see it until now."
He turned it again in his fingers.
"So tell me.
How did you manage that, when the Immense Ones shattered your existence to pieces?
Or is your own Root of Immensity so grand that even they could not shatter it?"
For a long moment, there was only silence.
The snow fell.
The clock-hands of Atlas’s Dimension turned somewhere far away in another of his bodies.
And the ring sat quiet in his hands, and Noah waited.
Then the old engineer spoke.
|It seems you have had quite a leap,| Atlas said.
|A major one, in a very short span.
When you ceased, all of you at once, I will admit I braced for the worst.
I thought an Immense One had finally caught your scent and made a move.
But no.
You were only grasping your own Root of Immensity.|
|Which, for the record, I had intended to help you form much, much later.
After we had raised your Provenance and the depth of your existence a great deal higher.
How you jumped that many steps in a little, I have no idea, and I have decided not to think too hard about it, because thinking too hard about you gives me a ringache.|
Noah’s mouth pulled at one corner.
|But you asked me a question,| Atlas went on, quieter. |So.
Yes.
In the tools I engineered, I spread my Root of Immensity.
Every relic, every workshop, every ring, every hidden thing I ever made.
I wove glimmers of my own Existential Chorionic Gonadotropin into all of them.
Do you understand what that means?|
He did not wait to find out.|It means that as long as one of my tools survived anywhere in existence, some fragment of my Root survived with it.
They broke my body on their anvil.
They collapsed my homes into ash.
And they thought they were done.
But they could never find every tool.
And if they could never eliminate my tools, then they could never, truly, eliminate me.|
Noah looked at the ring in his hands calmly.
"So this whole time," Noah said."I have been carrying part of you."
|A small part.
A glimmer.
Enough to talk, to teach, to scheme.
Not enough to walk out and reforge myself, which is the great inconvenience of my situation.|
Noah let that sit a moment and then he asked the thing underneath everything.
"What is your purpose, really?
With me.
You spread yourself through your tools, and you gave a great ring to THE REMINISCING WIDOW, which means you may even have her help now.
Existence is give and take.
You told me I could make the impossible possible, and I suppose I have just proven a little of that."
He held the ring up."But what is the endgame?
What are you actually after?"
And there was silence again!
|When an Immensity is destroyed,| Atlas said at last,|it does not simply come back.
No matter how grand the being was.
No matter how much of it survives in glimmers and tools.
When you rebuild an Immensity that was broken, you never get the same power back.
You come back smaller.
Diminished.
A great fire relit from one saved ember, and it never burns as tall as it did before.|
The ring pulsed faintly.
|Which means that even if I clawed my way back into a body, I would not be able to do the thing I most need to do.
I could not take down the ones I need to take down.
Not the way I am now.
Not the way I would come back.|
|So there is revenge in it.
There is a great deal of revenge in it.
But there is also the simpler thing.
The capability to do what I no longer can.
If you grow grand enough, Dreamer.
If you become truly, unfathomably grand.
Then maybe, one day, you will be grand enough to fully restore an Immensity that was broken.
To relight the fire without losing the height.
Maybe.
Who knows.|
The old engineer’s voice was quiet and honest and unashamed.
|It is all for my own selfish reasons, in the end.
Even as I help you along.
Do not ever mistake me for a kind old man.
I am a very selfish one who happens to be teaching you.|
Noah listened to all of it, and he did not flinch from it, because a selfish reason honestly stated was a thing he could trust far more than a kind one.
He looked at the ring once more, and opened his mouth to answer.
And Atlas blinked.
|Oh, fuck.|
The old engineer’s projection went rigid, as though he had forgotten something and only just remembered it in the worst possible moment.
|Right.
Right, I am an idiot.
Dreamer, listen to me.
Hide yourself.
All of you, every body, get all of your existence into your Existential Root Domain right now, this instant.
How did I forget this?
How did I forget the single most obvious thing?!|
The words came fast and alarmed. |Inside an Elsedimension they have no access to, you are hard to reach.
But out here, a newly formed Root of Immensity?
Some Immense Ones can smell that!
A fresh Root reaching its weavings out into open existence is a scent, and it is a rare and delicious one, and you are broadcasting it right now like a lit fire in a dark forest!|
Noah’s eyes pulsed as his teacher had a gift for delivering the worst news at the last possible second.
HUUM!
Because in that instant, he felt his existence buzz, the part of him still standing in the frozen forest where the Train had been split, and information came flooding in from that body all at once.
|THE UNPAID COLLECTOR smells something unique left behind in this place.|
|THE SLEEPLESS FIEND is surprised.
He says that whatever has been found here is his.|

Noah’s newborn Root drank the information from that body in a single breath, and he sensed it the malicious weavings of Immensity surging back toward the frozen forest, two of the beings whose war he could not perceive turning their terrible attention toward the fresh scent of a Root that should not exist!
He moved decisively.
He hurled his existence toward his Existential Root Domain, toward the sealed space that answered to no one but him, the one place in all of existence that not even an Immense One could enter!
HUUM!

His existence had already begun to fade, in the span of an instant, dissolving out of the frozen forest toward safety, and he could feel the tug of his impenetrable space reaching to receive him, pulling him home.
But.
An undeniable force closed around him and pulled him back!
It was not a thing he could fight.

It seized his fading existence the way a hand seizes a fleaf in the wind, absolute and effortless, and it dragged him back out of his retreat, back toward the frozen forest, back into the open where the scent of his Root hung bright and exposed.
|THE SLEEPLESS FIEND says: friend.
Do not go quite yet.
Come back out here.|
An undeniable force pulled him, and Noah’s eyes went cold.
He set his newborn will against the impossible grip, and in the same instant he made his decision!
Because he would not be caught, would not be held, would not be dragged before an Immense One to be studied and cracked open.
If he could not escape, then he would simply cease.
He would dissipate his existence here completely, this body, this presence, all of it, scatter himself to nothing before any Immense One could close a hand around what he had become!

chapters.title: Chapter 5763: A Delectable Treat! II
paragraphs: The undeniable force held Noah’s fading existence in the open, and would not let it go!
He hung there, half-dissolved, dragged back from the threshold of his own sealed Domain, and above him in the churning obsidian snowy foam loomed the two of them.

They were vast and indistinct, present one moment as enourmous eyes and gone the next, THE SLEEPLESS FIEND and THE UNPAID COLLECTOR turning their terrible attention upon the small bright thing that should not exist.
|What a scent,| the Fiend said.

|A fresh Root of Immensity, reaching its little weavings out into the open. I have not smelled one of these in an age. And a unique one, at that. How fortunate for us that you did not have the sense to stay hidden.|
Noah did not struggle against the grip. Struggling would have told them how weak he was, and they did not need to know that yet!
"You have me confused with something worth your time,"he said, and his voice came level with no fear in it at all."I am a watcher who wandered in. There is nothing here for you."

|A watcher who ceased and reformed at the rim of my Narrative, many times over, and now wears the scent of a newborn Root. No.|The Fiend’s threads gathered, almost amused. |You are something rarer than a watcher. Come here, little friend. Come out into the open where I can look at you properly. I only want... to look.|
The grip tightened. Noah felt himself dragged another fraction back from safety, felt the tug of his sealed Domain reaching for him and losing him, and he made his decision then.
Dissipation it was!
HUUM!
And that...was when something unique bloomed!
Existence buzzed and turned upside down.
He recieved and overabundance of new information!
Shockingly, a slime arrived!

It dropped into the frozen forest out of nowhere, a shapeless blob of pure golden light, and the moment it appeared, both of the vast indistinct figures above went still. Not surprised, quite. Cautious!

The Fiend’s writhing threads slowed. The Collector’s looming shape drew back a fraction. The golden slime landed upon the air between Noah and the two Immense Ones, small and bright against their enormity, and it announced itself!
|THE DIMENSIONAL DEVOURER, Poona, has arrived. She says that this time, she will not fail!|

The golden blob rose, and it flowed upward, and it changed. The gold took a shape and refined itself, and where a slime had been there stood a young woman, delicate and slight, with a fall of golden hair and a face of quiet loveliness and no aura at all, nothing, less presence than a candle.
She was tiny before the two indistinct titans hanging in the foam ahead of her, a slip of a thing against beings vaster than Dimensions!
She did not look tiny when she spoke.

"Do the two of you really want to fight just as the cold has come?" Poona said, "Look at yourselves. As grand and immense as you have grown, as high as you have climbed, and here you are, the both of you, ganging up to snatch at a little junior who has barely opened his eyes. How despicable are you, truly? Will your greed have no end at all?"
|Move aside, Slime,|the Collector said, and the way he said the word slime....frankly, it was very off putting as if he wss using it as a derogatory word!
|This one was found in our Narrative. That makes his disposition a matter for those who found him. Not for a scavenger who arrives late.|
|The Root is unclaimed,| the Fiend agreed, mild as ever. |What is found belongs to the finder. Step back, little Devourer, and I may let you keep the parts we do not want.|
Poona smiled.

It was a dangerous smile, and it did not touch the ease in her voice at all. "Well. I have laid a claim to the protection of this junior. As of this moment, he stands under... a certain umbrella. You understand what that means, I think, both of you. You offend me here, and you do not merely offend me. You offend a great many as you should know where I stem from. So..."
She tilted her golden head. "What will it be?"
Silence actually came down!

The two Immense Ones did not move, and Noah, hanging held in the cold, watched two of the most terrifying beings in existence weigh a slip of a golden woman with no aura and choose, against every instinct their greed was screaming at them, to do nothing.
The grip on his existence did not release, but it did not tighten either. They watched. They watched threateningly, their vast indistinct shapes hanging in the snow, and they did not act.
That inaction... told Noah more about who Poona was than anything she had said. Shd had said they would offend a great deal of many where she came from so...where the hell did she come from?
She turned from them, and she came to him, drifting close through the falling snow, and her voice dropped.

"Little guy," she said."I really cannot afford to fail to bring another one of you back this time. So listen to me, and sense to the trueness of my existence as your newly formed Root should be very sensitive. I do not mean you any harm. Not the way these two fuckers did."
She glanced back at the titans, unbothered."Let us go, before either of them talks themselves into something stupid, okay?"
This unknown and terrifying being, who had made two Immense Ones stand still with a smile, was speaking to him as though she were coaxing a frightened animal down off a ledge.
And Noah, still gathered and ready to scatter himself to nothing, held that readiness, and reached out with his newborn sight into the boundless flowing information all around him, and read her.

He read the Trueness pouring off her, the deep weave of what she was, and in all of it, in every thread, there was no malice. None. Whatever else she was, whatever she wanted, she did not want to harm him, and his newborn existence could not find a single lie in her.
He did not lower his guard. But he did not scatter himself either.
"Just who are you," he said, "really?"
Poona’s smile turned almost fond.

"I am merely Poona. THE Dimensional Devourer."She drifted a little closer. "You do not understand yet what you are, so let me tell you, since it is the reason two Immense Ones just tried to snatch you out of the sky. A newly formed Root of Immensity is one of the rarest thing in existence, little guy. It is an entire path, an entire future of Immensity, sitting exposed at its very beginning. Untouched. Unspent. Full of everything it could ever become. To an Immense One greedy enough, a fresh Root is a Panacea. A cure, a fortune, a treasure beyond price, because to devour it is to swallow a whole path of potentail before it has walked a single step."
Noah went very still at that!

"So," Poona said brightly."I am going to tug on your existence now, and pull you somewhere safe. Do not kill yourself off, and do not run away, all right? It would waste a great deal of my effort, and I have had a very long day!"
Noah thought about it. He weighed the two watching titans and their held greed, the golden woman with no lie in her, the impossible situation he had walked into simply by becoming what he was!
And he trusted his intuition more than anything else!
He let his readiness to cease uncoil, just slightly.
Then he turned his cold gaze one last time upon THE SLEEPLESS FIEND and THE UNPAID COLLECTOR, the two vast indistinct greeds hanging in the frozen foam.
And in the next instant, he and Poona were gone as gold light flashed!

chapters.title: Chapter 5764: Legacy! I
paragraphs: Poona pulled him through existence, and Noah felt every layer of it pass!

He did not resist the tug. They sank down through layers of reality and up through tiers of Dimensionality, past depths he had never known were stacked beneath existence, with existence peeling open around them and folding shut behind, and he catologed every one of them as they went. It was a great deal to take in!
And then they arrived, and the place they arrived in was grand.

The Existential Conduits were here, the great pillars of flowing authority he had first seen threading the void above the sundered Train. But here they did not merely rise and stretch. Here they had been bent and shaped.

Woven into structure and form, the veins of existence itself coaxed into architecture, and out of them stood grand buildings and soaring towers, whole halls and towers raised from living rivers of Infinity and Source and Loom-light, coursing bright through walls that were somehow both solid and made of pure flowing authority.

And through those Conduit-buildings, moving freely, drifting between the towers and perching on the towers, went the Conduit Lifeforms, thousands of them, the incandescent critters of the deep, at home here in a way they had not been in the wild veins of the void.
It was an ancient place, and its Dimensionality was terrifying to stand within.
Above the towers, Dimensions and Observable Existences hung in the air like stars, whole domains turning gently in the dark as though they were nothing more than lanterns strung over a courtyard.

And beyond the towers rose mountains, vast ones, and they were not mountains at all, Noah saw, but Elsedimensions grown into the shape of mountains, great masses of sealed reality climbing into the heights with Existential Conduits running through them like rivers of light threading a range of peaks.
A civilization raised in the veins of existence, older than most things Noah had ever encountered, grand beyond the grandest empires!
And over all of it, heavy and constant, fell the snow.

The cold had reached even here. Even this ancient place of terrifying Dimensionality, this domain grown from the bones of existence, lay under the falling white, the Long Night’s chill permeating the Conduit-towers and the star-hung domains and the Elsedimension mountains all alike. It fell thick as beside him Noah saw Poona shiver.

She grimaced, and waved a small hand, and a coat wove itself around her out of nothing, thick and warm, and Noah’s new eyes saw that it was filled with boundless invisible authority, layer upon layer of it.
"Ugh," Poona said, pulling the coat close. "It reaches everywhere now. Even home."
Then she brightened, and turned to him, and there was real satisfaction in her face. "But look at this. Look at you, standing here safe! I did it. I actually did it this time!"
She said it with the pleasure of someone who had needed a win and finally gotten one.

"You should understand..." she went on, walking now, leading him in among the Conduit-towers under the snow. "Some Immense Ones, the greedy ones, the hungry ones, they would rather just eat the young. A fresh Root, swallowed whole, no thought given to it. That is what those two were. That is most of them, if I am honest."

She glanced at him. "But not all. Some of them care about legacy. About what comes after. About whether the path continues once they are gone. And you have arrived at a place built by one who cared about exactly that." A small, proud smile. "This place. This whole Domain. It was founded here by her."
She led him on, through the towers and beneath the hanging Domains, until they came to the foot of one of the great Elsedimension mountains, and there, at its entrance, stood a statue.

Noah looked up at it, and his new sight resolved what it was made of. Existential Conduits. The veins of existence themselves, bent and woven and set into the shape of a figure, rivers of flowing authority coursing through the carved form so that the whole statue glowed from within, blue and obsidian and white and a dozen colors he had no names for, an entire being sculpted from the living power of the deep.
And the figure it made was one he knew.

It was small, and rough, and hunched. A caveman shape of thick limbs and unadorned skin, calloused hands cupped as though pouring something out. And beautiful, terribly and anciently beautiful, even rendered in flowing Conduits a mile high.
It was Lucy!
Poona stopped before the statue, and she bowed her head, and when she spoke her voice had lost all its lightness and gone quiet and reverent.

"This is the one responsible for all of it," she said. "For this place. For me. For every one of us who ever awoke a Root and lived long enough to grow it. Before she left existence, she built this. An Immense Legacy, raised here in the deep, to give the young a place. Somewhere those who had awakened their Existential Roots of Immensity could thrive, and grow, and become what they were meant to become, without being hunted down and devoured for the treasure they carried before they ever had the chance to walk their path."Poona looked up at the glowing figure.
"This is her Legacy. She is THE Acharya of Immensity. Lucy!"
BOOM!
Noah’s eyes shone.

He thought of Lucy in the record, walking through her Primordial forest, telling him to go and experience existence for the first time now that his Root had emerged. She had not warned him how dangerous that would be. She had not told him that stepping out into the open with a fresh Root was to hang a jewel before every greedy Immense One nearby!
She had simply smiled and sent him out.
But now he stood before her Legacy, where someone belonging to it had found him at the exact moment two titans closed their hands around him, and pulled him free.

Had she expected that? Had she known, when she sent him out unwarned, that her Legacy would reach him before the hungry ones could? That a thing she had built at the beginning of existence would still be standing at the end of an Age?

He could not know. She was a record, and records did not answer follow-up questions. But standing here, looking up at her made of the veins of existence, he thought it was not impossible. It was not impossible at all!
Poona was already moving on.

"Come," she said, turning from the statue and leading him deeper toward the mountain’s entrance. "There is a great deal here, and you will need time to grasp all of it. In these Empyros Immense Legacy Mountains, you will find others like you, some who have awoken a Root of Immensity and not yet formed their Immensity, still growing, still becoming. And in some places, yes, you will see true Immense Ones, the ones who care about what comes after as they won’t try to eat you...for the most part."
She glanced back at him, and the lightness returned to her. "There is much for you to understand. But first things first. Let me take you to Sir Moriarty."

She said it with the pleasure of someone who had needed a win and finally gotten one.
"You should understand..." she went on, walking now, leading him in among the Conduit-towers under the snow.
"Some Immense Ones, the greedy ones, the hungry ones, they would rather just eat the young.
A fresh Root, swallowed whole, no thought given to it.
That is what those two were.
That is most of them, if I am honest."
She glanced at him.
"But not all.
Some of them care about legacy.
About what comes after.
About whether the path continues once they are gone.
And you have arrived at a place built by one who cared about exactly that." A small, proud smile.
"This place.
This whole Domain.
It was founded here by her."
She led him on, through the towers and beneath the hanging Domains, until they came to the foot of one of the great Elsedimension mountains, and there, at its entrance, stood a statue.
Noah looked up at it, and his new sight resolved what it was made of.
Existential Conduits.

The veins of existence themselves, bent and woven and set into the shape of a figure, rivers of flowing authority coursing through the carved form so that the whole statue glowed from within, blue and obsidian and white and a dozen colors he had no names for, an entire being sculpted from the living power of the deep.
And the figure it made was one he knew.
It was small, and rough, and hunched.
A caveman shape of thick limbs and unadorned skin, calloused hands cupped as though pouring something out.
And beautiful, terribly and anciently beautiful, even rendered in flowing Conduits a mile high.
It was Lucy!
Poona stopped before the statue, and she bowed her head, and when she spoke her voice had lost all its lightness and gone quiet and reverent.
"This is the one responsible for all of it," she said.
"For this place.
For me.
For every one of us who ever awoke a Root and lived long enough to grow it.
Before she left existence, she built this.
An Immense Legacy, raised here in the deep, to give the young a place.

Somewhere those who had awakened their Existential Roots of Immensity could thrive, and grow, and become what they were meant to become, without being hunted down and devoured for the treasure they carried before they ever had the chance to walk their path."Poona looked up at the glowing figure.
"This is her Legacy.
She is THE Acharya of Immensity.
Lucy!"
BOOM!
Noah’s eyes shone.
He thought of Lucy in the record, walking through her Primordial forest, telling him to go and experience existence for the first time now that his Root had emerged.
She had not warned him how dangerous that would be.
She had not told him that stepping out into the open with a fresh Root was to hang a jewel before every greedy Immense One nearby!
She had simply smiled and sent him out.
But now he stood before her Legacy, where someone belonging to it had found him at the exact moment two titans closed their hands around him, and pulled him free.
Had she expected that?
Had she known, when she sent him out unwarned, that her Legacy would reach him before the hungry ones could?
That a thing she had built at the beginning of existence would still be standing at the end of an Age?
He could not know.
She was a record, and records did not answer follow-up questions.
But standing here, looking up at her made of the veins of existence, he thought it was not impossible.
It was not impossible at all!
Poona was already moving on.
"Come," she said, turning from the statue and leading him deeper toward the mountain’s entrance.
"There is a great deal here, and you will need time to grasp all of it.
In these Empyros Immense Legacy Mountains, you will find others like you, some who have awoken a Root of Immensity and not yet formed their Immensity, still growing, still becoming.
And in some places, yes, you will see true Immense Ones, the ones who care about what comes after as they won’t try to eat you...for the most part."
She glanced back at him, and the lightness returned to her.
"There is much for you to understand.
But first things first.
Let me take you to Sir Moriarty."

chapters.title: Chapter 5765: Legacy! II
paragraphs: <Those Who Remain>
Seconds after Poona and the anomaly vanished, the sky changed.

An aura descended over the frozen forest and the sundered halves of the Train, and it was Immensity of a weight that even THE SLEEPLESS FIEND and THE UNPAID COLLECTOR, who were no small things, felt in their own existences.
The two hazy titans, who had loomed so terribly only moments ago, went somber beneath it.
Then it took a shape.

A figure formed in the churning snow, hazy and purple, humanoid in its outline but wrong in its crown, because from its head rose a pair of horns that did not stop. They twisted upward and outward endlessly, spiraling into the dark above without ever reaching an end, coiling on and on past where sight could follow.
The purple haze of it pressed down on the ruined region, and the two Immense Ones who had been the mightiest things present a breath ago now stood in the presence of something mightier still.
The horned figure spoke, and his voice boomed out across the frozen dark as it came edged with the flatness of a being who was used to being obeyed.
"Where is the Anomaly that was just here?"
It was almost a command. Almost. And THE SLEEPLESS FIEND, who did not care to be commanded by anyone, let a cold light pass behind his luminous eyes at the tone of it.
But he did not act imposingly. He weighed the horned figure’s Immensity against his own, and he simply answered!
"One of those from the Legacy of THE Acharya of Immensity came,"the Fiend said, "and took him."
Existence seethed!

The purple haze roiled, the snow whipping violently around the horned figure, and he looked at the Fiend and the Collector like a colleague looks at others who have broken something priceless through sheer stupidity.
"You did not think," the horned one said slowly, "that an emerging Root, forming in the very first hours after the Long Night began, might be a thing worth holding on to?"
Neither answered.

"One of the few things we were able to scry, across the whole of existence, through all the fog the winter has thrown over the future," he went on, and each word landed heavier than the last, "was this. That one of the three named in THE AUGURY OF THE LONG NIGHT, one of the three at the turning, would be the first to form a Root after the Night descended. The first. And you had that thing in your hands, both of you, hands closed around it, a piece of the single most important puzzle we face in this dreadful cold..."
The horns coiled endlessly above him. "And you let anothrr walk up and take it out of your grip? Really? Truly? You fucked it that badly?"
The Fiend’s threads buzzed, and the Collector’s mass seethed, their own Immensity flaring at the humiliation of the words! And the Fiend looked over, and his voice came cold and imperious.

"None of that information was shared with us,"he said. "We were told nothing of a scrying, nothing of an Augury. We caught a scent, we found a Root, we moved to take it. Perhaps if belonging to a Legacy actually granted us the benefits it is supposed to grant, rather than leaving us to guess in the dark like common hunters, we would have known to hold it more carefully."
The horned figure waved a dismissive hand, and the snow settled.

"The Long Night has only just begun," he said, the anger cooling into something colder and more organized. "There are things the ones who are not core to this still do not know. That is a failure of ours, not of yours, and it will be corrected. Let us go back, so that everything is made clear to everyone, and so that nothing like this ever happens again."

He turned his endless horns toward the deep. "We have known for a long time that one of the three is little Riven. He has been groomed and contained this whole time. If we could have gotten our hands on a second of the three as well, then surviving the Long Night would have been all but guaranteed."
"But we know where they took him now. So it may be that we simply do everything in our power to take him back. Come. There is a great deal to prepare."

He turned and dissolved into the deep of existence, his endless horns the last of him to fade, and a breath later the Fiend and the Collector followed, gone into the dark after him, and the frozen forest was left empty under the falling snow with no one to see it grow.
Far away, in a Domain lost in existence and time, Sir Moriarty worked at his corpse and watched a screen.

The illusory screen hung in the drifting snow of his hall, and upon it moved two small figures, Poona in her lovely borrowed shape and the anomaly at her side, walking the road of Conduit-light toward him.
Moriarty drew a thread of pale authority from the dead Immense One splayed before him, held it to his small neat spectacles, and set it aside, and did not look away from the screen as he worked.
Behind him, silent, a verdant eye opened in the air.
It was vast, and it was filled with an Immensity Moriarty did not turn to measure, and it wached the screen over his shoulder.
"The first Root formed after the Long Night," it said. "Isit confirmed that he is one of the three? We cannot build what we are building on guesswork."
Moriarty did not stop his work.

"We will know for certain in due time," he said, calm as still water. "EvenPoona does not know what he might be. None of the others do either. So I will take charge of it myself, and confirm it quietly, as we go. Do not worry."
The verdant eye did not answer at once. It gazed at the figure of Noah on the screen intently.

"I never much cared for the future," it said at last. "Why would I? I can always change my present. And I never much cared for this Augury of the Long Night, all its cryptic little verses about turnings and threes."

A pause, and the eye narrowed. "But THE Acharya of Immensity took it seriously. Lucy took it seriously and she told us that when the Night came, it would be our chance. Our one chance to stop being what we are. To no longer be Those Who Remain."

The verdant light deepened. "So we make sure. We gather every piece the Augury names, and we hold them, and we do not let a single one slip away because someone was careless. With the Long Night, the path is open again. The door that closed on us all those ages ago has cracked. And we cannot, we will not, merely Remain."
The eye held on Noah’s small figure a moment longer.
Then it closed, and was gone, and Moriarty was alone with his corpse and his screen and the falling snow.
He drew another thread of dead authority from the splayed Immense One, and he simply murmured to himself again!
"And at the turning, count three,"Moriarty said. "One shall look upon all that is, and grieve. One shall take up every weight, and not set it down. One shall no longer remain, and yet remain."
He set the thread aside, and reached into the corpse for another, and on the screen the two small figures drew closer to his hall.
"One shall no longer remain, and yet remain,"he said again, softer, and watched the anomaly come!

chapters.title: Chapter 5766: Legacy! III
paragraphs: <THE True Human Emperor>
Poona led him up through the mountain as they crossed many intricate Existential Conduits.

Now, even as they moved, he continued to collect information as he didn’t take Poona’s words as law. He knew very well how in existence, nobody did anything without reason. Everybody was selfish! Even Atlas had his aims.
So he simply had to grasp what the aims of Poona and this Legacy were, even if they didn’t mean him harm.
After going deeper into the Elsedimension Mountain filled with Existential Conduits leading the way...

Noah felt a whole sealed reality shaped into the form of a peak open up, Existential Conduits running through it like veins of light through stone, and at its heart, in a great open hall, waited the thing that ruled it.
It was...an octopus.
Noah stopped where he floated and simply looked.

A vast titan of dark coiling flesh sat at the center of the hall, tentacles moving through the drifting air with unhurried precision, and around it wound slow rivers of white and gold, currents of pure authority threading between islands of nothing.

Whole Dimensions floated in the space above it like lanterns. Snow drifted down through all of it, impossible and constant. And upon what passed for the creature’s face perched a pair of small, neat spectacles, absurd against its enormity, catching the gold of the rivers.
This would be the one Poona said was...Sir Moriarty?
Before it lay the corpse of an Immense One!
It was splayed and pinned in the drifting air, opened and parted and studied, and Moriarty’s tentacles worked through it calmly.
"Sir Moriarty," Poona said. "This time I reached in time and brought back another Root for the Legacy. This earns me some points, yes? The Fiend and another were ready to sniff him up..."
The octopus set down the thread of authority he was holding.
He turned, and the small spectacles turned with him as his eyes settled upon Noah with undisguised interest.
"So you did. Come in. Gaze upon everything as I am sure it must seem odd and interesting..."Moriarty said!

Noah stood in the drifting snow of the hall and looked at the octopus. There was power, first, an ancient and terrible depth of it that Noah could not find the bottom of. Question marks upon question marks!
"You are wary," Moriarty said, watching him. "
This is good. Wary is how the young survive long enough to become old."
He waved a tentacle, and a thread of the white-gold river coiled up and offered itself as a seat, which Noah declined.
"Let me guess. You do not trust where you are, you do not know what I or others want, and you are even suspicious we dragged you here to eat you as well. Am I close?"
"You are... close."Noah said.
"Hmm."

Moriarty adjusted his spectacles with a delicate curl of one tentacle. "So let me spare you the suspense. This is THE Acharya of Immensity, Lucy’s Legacy. These are the Empyros Immense Legacy Mountains. Yes, this is a real sanctuary. No, there is no catch you have not already guessed. Yes, some of the beings here are Immense Ones, and no, they will not eat you, because Lucy built this place with laws in its very structure and even the greediest thing here honors them, partly out of respect and partly because breaking them is a great deal more painful than they would like."
Noah listened intently!
"This is where the ones who care about legacy bring the young to grow. It has been here for a long time."
He turned one bright eye fully upon Noah then.
"So. Since we are getting to know one another. What kind of Root did you form?"
It was asked lightly, but it was heavy!
And Noah did not have an answer. His own weavings could not sort him into either box.
He deflected.
"I have only just formed it,"Noah said. "I am still learning what it is."
It was somewhat true.

"Fair enough," he said mildly. "A Root is a private thing when it is new, and you would be a fool to unwrap yours in front of a stranger. Poona, head back for now. I will finish the introductions with The Stranger."
"Okay!" Poona didn’t delay as she waved her hands and disappeared!
Sir Moriarty set his tools down and fully looked at Noah as with just the two of them here and a corpse of an Immense One behind, the air became heavy!
"There are two kinds of Root in all of existence,"Moriarty said. "Only two. Every awakened Lifeform you will ever meet is one or the other."

He drifted on. "The first is the Conceptual Root. A Root of idea. Of law, of narrative, of dream, of pure concept. It grows into what we call an Empyros Immense Lifeform, and an Empyros does not fight Existence as much as rewrite it. The Conceptual path is grand, subtle, and terrifying in the way a well-written sentence is terrifying, if you understand what a well-written sentence can do."

"The other." Moriarty’s spectacles caught the light. "The Physical Root. A Root of body, of flesh, of appetite, of raw dimensional mass and force. It grows into a Fiend Immense Lifeform. And a Fiend does not rewrite Existence A Fiend simply is larger than Existence’s ability to argue with it. THE SLEEPLESS FIEND you just came across is exactly what his name says he is. A Fiend of the Physical path, grown vast. He is a decently powerful one that is nigh unkillable..."
Noah’s eyes shone brightly!
"This is why the paths matter,"the octopus went on. "It is not a category. It is life and death."
Noah could not say for certain which he was!

Everything about him said Conceptual. He was a Dreamer. An author. A thing that had spent its existence imposing narratives, dreaming realities true, bending stories to his will, all of it concept, concept, concept.
But his Root had refused to say so!

He thought of his Infinity, the thing at the root of his Root. Dialetheic. A truth that is also its opposite. Finite and infinite at once, holding two contradictory things and being true in both without choosing.
What would a Root born of that principle be? Conceptual, or Physical?
Both. Neither?

chapters.title: Chapter 5767: Legacy! IV
paragraphs: He shook his head as he fished for more information.
"And an Immense One," Noah said. "In all of this...what is an Immense One, really?"
Moriarty looked at the drifting snow with luminous, terrifying eyes of power!

"A Root," he said,"is a seed. That is all any of you are, all of you young ones here. A seed cracked open, full of everything it could ever be, and nothing it is yet. And an Immense One is what happens when a seed is given enough time, and enough safety, and enough adversity in the right measure, to grow. From seed to sprout. From sprout to tree. From potential, all the way to bloom."

He turned his small spectacled eyes on Noah. "You are a seed. A strange one, an interesting one, a seed I cannot classify, but a seed. The tree is the goal. Immensity is only a Root that has finished growing. Out there across existence, many like you are devoured before you can bloom, unless you remain in your Existential Root Domain. But Immensity is hard to fully grasp by being idle as many try different things to survive."
The snow fell over the Domain relentlessly.
"And the winter," Moriarty added,"is very, very hard on seeds. This place...tries to make it a bit easier for seeds to grow. This place does not want your loyalty."
Noah looked at him.

"We are not some sect. We do not care whether you develop a fierce sense of belonging to us, or a deep sense of duty toward us, or whether you weep tears of gratitude every morning at the thought of our kindness."
Moriarty drifted along.
"You owe us nothing. Not belief, not service, not affection. Grow strong, leave when you like, forget my face entirely. It is genuinely all the same to us."
"That is a strange thing for a sanctuary to say,"Noah said.

"It is a strange sanctuary." Moriarty’s tone stayed dry. "We are not run for our own glory. Everything here, every law, every kindness, every seed we save from the winter, is done for one reason, and one reason only. Because she wished it."
He did not have to say who!

"Lucy did not build this place to gather followers. She had no interest in being worshipped. She built it because she wanted the young to have a chance she did not have. And so we honor her wishes, all of us, the greedy ones and the kind ones alike. Out of respect for her. She is the only thing any of us truly bow to here, and she is not even present to see it."
WAA!
Noah found that on this particular ideal... he believed it. Their reverence towards that being!

"So no," Moriarty went on, "you will not be asked to swear anything, or join anything, or become one of us. But you will be given something, because she wished that too. A gift she handed down before she left, for every budding Root that finds its way here."

He slowed. "And it is the reason most of the young survive long enough to bloom at all. A Root grows on its own, you have felt that already, I imagine. It secretes its own Dimensionality, raises its own weight, climbs a little every day whether you lift a finger or not. That is the nature of a Root. But growing on its own is slow. Achingly slow. It is a seed pushing up through hard groud one grain at a time, and a seed that grows only at that pace will not become a tree before the winter finds it. Not in an Age like this one."
He turned his small eyes on Noah.

"So Lucy left us a way to grow faster.A Narrative Immense Inscription Art. And it does one thing, one beautiful and terrible thing! It lets a budding Root reach out, across the whole of existence, across Time, Parallel Time, Apocryphal Existences, Multidimensions, Elsedimensions...everything really, and pull in what it needs to grow!"
"Pull in...what, exactly?"Noah asked.

"Immensity." Moriarty said the word with weight. "Existence is not empty, you have seen that now. It is full. Full of authority, full of flow, full of the whole churning chaos of everything that ever was and is and will be, all of it moving through the Conduits and the deep at once. And scattered through that chaos, rare and fine, are slivers. Molecular units, if you like, of pure chaotic Immensity. Loose fragments of the very thing your Root is trying to become. They drift through existence unclaimed, across every distance and every age, and the Art lets you reach out and gather them, and feed them to your Root, so that it grows toward the tree not one grain at a time but by the mouthful. It is how a seed becomes truly Immense before the winter can kill it. It is how any of us ever did."
Noah’s existence sharpened with the interest!

"It is the hardest thing you will ever attempt. When you reach out across existence, you do not reach into a tidy shelf of Immensity waiting to be taken. You reach into everything. All of it, at once, the entire boundless flow of chaos, every current and every stream, information beyond counting, most of it useless, most of it wrong, most of it nothing to do with what you need. And you must reject all of it. Every flow but the one. You must reach into the roar of the whole of existence and refuse every single thing pouring toward you except the rare, fine slivers of Immensity, and then, across a distance and a time you cannot even imagine, you must pull those slivers, and only those, toward yourself, without dragging in a single scrap of anything else."
He let that sink!

"It is a sieve,"Moriarty said."A sieve held up against an ocean, and you are trying to catch a specific grain of a specific sand while the whole sea pours through your hands. Most of the time you will fail. Most of the time you will reach for a sliver of Immensity and pull in a great slop of chaos you did not want, useless information, foreign flows, things that fight your Root instead of feeding it. That is the ordinary danger, and it is bad enough."
His voice dropped. "But it is no longer the ordinary danger, because The Long Night has come. And the winter has changed what is out there in the flow."
The snow fell heavier around them, as if the words had summoned it!
