chapters.title: Chapter 5768: Legacy! V
paragraphs: "There is cold in the chaos now,"Moriarty said.

"The descending cold has soaked into the flows of existence themselves, and some of the information drifting out there is no longer merely useless. It is frozen. It is destructive. Reach into the flow carelessly now, cast your sieve without the discipline, and you may pull in a sliver of The Long Night itself, a shard of that killing cold, and draw it straight into the heart of your budding Root. And a Root is a fragile thing. It is a seed, cracked open, soft and new. The cold that the mightiest Immense Ones can barely hold at bay would freeze a young Root solid in an instant, and there is no coming back from that. So the Art was always hard. Now it is hard, and it will kill you if your discipline slips."
He looked at Noah steadily."I would not blame you for waiting. Many do. They grow the slow way and hope to outlast the winter. Some of them even manage it."
"Show me the Art,"Noah said.
Moriarty regarded him a moment silently.
"Very well. Watch closely. And do not flinch."
The octopus rose.
And the Immensity came off him!
Noah’s existence pulsed as grand Immensity bloomed!
It was no lesser than THE SLEEPLESS FIEND! Well, likely greater as this mosntrous being was likely a fiend too.

The hall trembled with it! The rivers of authority bent! The floating Domains shuddered on their strings, and Noah understood, all at once and with perfect clarity, that the affable creature who had told him he owed nothing and offered him a seat of light was one of the most terrifying existences he had ever stood beside, and had simply chosen, out of respect, to be gentle about it!
From that unfurled Immensity, Moriarty conjured the Art.

It bloomed in the air between them, an Inscription, intricate beyond intricate, a vast and terrible methodology of interlocking weavings that turned slowly in the snow, and Noah looked at it and saw the whole shape of it at once, the reaching, the rejecting, the sieve held against the ocean, the discipline that pulled a single sliver of Immensity across all of existence and time and let nothng else through.
It was the hardest thing he had ever been shown. It was also, he saw in the same breath, beautiful. Why was it so beautiful?
Moriarty extended it toward him, and Noah reached out, and accepted it.
|You are viewing the weavings and understanding of THE NARRATIVE IMMENSE INSCRIPTION ART: IMMEGAGENESIS.|
Understanding the thing before him was not easy. But Noah was a dreamer, and dreaming was how he understood anything.

Profundity and reverie moved through his mind as he turned over everything the octopus had said, the idea of reaching out across every kind of existence to gather slivers of a thing he could not even have perceived an hour ago. He was a Provenance Lifeform. He generated everything he held, made it himself, and now his Osmontian Chorionic Gonadotropin generated his Provenance and his growth from within without asking anything of anyone!
But if a being wanted that growth faster, it seemed, it could reach outside itself and pull.
And when he came to the methodology of the Art, he found the shape of it familiar, and almost smiled.
It was an inscription.

It felt like the engineering Atlas had been drilling into him this whole time, and yes, it was intricate, layered with countless seams of Dimensionality turning inside it, a structure grander than anything Atlas had shown him. So what?!

He had carved inscriptions before. His body flickered, and infinite illusory pages flowed off him and into the floating Inscription of IMMEGAGENESIS, reading it, tracing it, learning it, and then his existence did what his existence did best.
It copied.

Beside the Art Moriarty had conjured, a second one began to form. Noah recreated its entire structure from nothing, layer by layer, every seam and layer and turning of Dimensionality, an identical Inscription blooming in the drifting snow beside the original. Then he waved his hand, and the new one flowed to him, and he closed his fingers around it, and his existence shone with resplendence as he took it.
He could feel Moriarty watching him.
The octopus looked at him intently, the small neat spectacles catching the light.

But Noah revealed nothing of himself. He simply sat down in the snow, and turned his attention inward, because his mind was full now, full of the way to spread himself across existence, which was all this Art really was.

IMMEGAGENESIS took the state he had reached in his transformation and sharpened it into a technique.He had learned, becoming what he now was, that existence was a set of boxes he could occupy at once, in different places, in different times, all together.

The Art took that raw ability and made it a craft. It let an existence stretch itself across those boxes on purpose, into layer after layer of reality, and perceive all the boundless information flowing through each one, the slivers of Immensity hidden in the roar of everything, and then reach out and pull them home.

It was, he thought, like a man learning to read a whole library at once. Not one book at a time, page by page, but every book in every room, open and legible in the same instant, and the trick of it was to find the single true sentence you needed in all those millions of pages and lift it out without carrying away the rest.
And to implement it, he was simply writing another inscription into his existence.But this one needed no Gu, no elements, none of the materials Atlas had taught.

This inscription asked only that its methodology be paired with a Root of Immensity, and then it would begin to cycle through the whole of an existence, reaching out for the boundless weavings of information across the deep.
So Noah reached out.
And.
HUUM!

His head rose, and from his eyes there erupted beams of golden-blue light, because the density of it nearly overwhelmed him. The information came flooding in the instant he opened, a booming roar of everything at once, more than any mind was built to hold, crashing into him from every layer and box of existence he had streched himself across!
His existence buzzed with the pressure of it, and he spoke to himself!

"My weavings are grand," he said. "No amount of information can overwhelm me. This is the first time I have met this Art. But I have always met this Art. I have always cast my weavings across the bounds of information and existence. I am proficient in this, because I have always been proficient in this. I am. I am. I AM!"
BOOM!
His existence stabilized.

And as it steadied, invisible threads erupted all around him and became visible, endless fine strings of light unspooling out of his seated figure and stretching away in every direction, across layer after layer of Dimensionality, out into box after box of existence.
Every thread was information. Every string a line cast into a different room of the boundless library, drinking what flowed there.
And at the very core of his existence, at his Root, he felt what all that information carried.
Cold.
It carried a tremendous, terrible cold. Frost crawled across his existence as the threads drew their harvest home, and beside him Moriarty stirred.

"Take it slow," the octopus said, and there was caution in it now. "Many have to be careful, and The Long Night has made this far worse than it ever was. You could do irreparable harm to your existence. You could freeze your very Root. Take it slow."
He was told to take it slow.
Noah did not take it slow.

As his senses spread through the boundless weavings, he cut apart and ignored the lifeforms that pressed on him like a storm, the churning weight of it filling this Domain and every Domain around it. It might have been information about others who had just formed their Roots in the Legacy. It might have been the weavings of full Immense Ones.
He did not care about any of it. He wanted the slivers of Immensity, the hidden ones, the fine loose fragments of the thing his Root was trying to become.
He was demanding with his own stretched existence, which felt now as though it spread out without end. Show yourself to me. Expose yourself.Open wide!
His existence buzzed as he screamed it inwardly, bellowed it into the roar of all that information.
And yet.
He could not sense a single thing that named itself Immensity.Not one sliver. Not one loose fragment of the thing he had reached across all of existence to find.
He frowned, and outwardly his seated figure fluttered with the endless light of illusory pages and the narratives of an infinite dream, and he said it aloud.
"I cannot sense any slivers of Immensity."
The words snapped Moriarty’s eyes wide, and a sudden somberness moved into them.

"Nothing?" the octopus said. "Some small ones should be drifting even through this Domain. Your existence should have stretched itself far already, farther than most ever manage on a first attempt. And you... sense nothing at all?"
Noah spread his senses out again, further, harder, into every box and layer he could reach.
And he felt only the endless blue-white wave of the cold.

Frost gathered thicker on his body as he reached, and he found The Long Night and nothing else. He visualized his endless strings of information, every one of them, all those fine lines cast across existence, and every single one carried the same thing back to him. Layers of snow. Layers of cold.
He looked down the length of all those countless threads, and where there should have been the whole churning wealth of existence, there was only winter, drifting down every line at once.
Nothing else.
"Was I...mistaken?"Moriarty said quietly beside him, in a deep and troubled voice.
Was he mistaken. Mistaken on what?
Noah did not ask. He did not care what the octopus meant. He reframed his focus and looked instead at the only thing he could sense at all.
The Long Night. The flakes of snow.
The cold.

It was so pervasive that it buried everything else, drowned out every other current of information, made it almost impossible to gaze at anything but itself. And Noah, sitting frozen in the falling snow with the whole of existence stretched out through him and nothing but winter coming back, turned the strangeness of that over, and asked himself the question underneath it.

What was this thing, that even Immense Ones felt it? That even Poona, who made two titans stand still with a smile, had to weave herself a coat of Immensity against it? What could reach past all of that?
And the thought came to him.
When it came to a thing that was truly immense, truly grand, then this cold, these endless particles of snow, were more immense than anything else in existence, right?
His existence went still.
What?
The cold that affected even Immense Ones was something more immense than them?

It was only a thought. He had only thought it. But the instant he thought it, he could not stop thinking it, could not unthink it, as he sensed the weavings of THE Long Night pouring down every thread and through every layer around him.
THUMP!
He felt the beat of his own heart, and a ridiculous, terrifying idea bloomed in him.
And a flicker of fear bloomed with it, because for all he had become, he was still human, and the idea was ridiculous!
But he felt possessed by his own intuition, the same intuiton that had never once led him wrong, and it did not care about the fear, and it opened his mouth for him.
"Come..." Noah said. "Come...COME!"
BOOM!
His existence opened itself.

His Osmontian Chorionic Gonadotropin opened wide, the infinite Root of him unfolding, and instead of reaching for the slivers of Immensity that would not show themselves, Noah reached for the only thing that would.
He pulled on the terrible cold. He pulled on the snow. He pulled on the Long Night itself, and dragged it toward his existence!
And Moriarty, beside him, saw a thing that stopped even his ancient mind.
The snow moved.

All of it, at once, across the whole of the Domain, every falling flake and every drift of the descending cold turned as though a tide had been called, and it surged toward Noah’s small seated figure like an endless sea rushing to a single point, countless waves of white pouring in from every direction toward the one being in all of existence mad enough, or lost enough, or grand enough, to open his arms and call the winter home!

He looked down the length of all those countless threads, and where there should have been the whole churning wealth of existence, there was only winter, drifting down every line at once.
Nothing else.
"Was I...mistaken?"Moriarty said quietly beside him, in a deep and troubled voice.
Was he mistaken.
Mistaken on what?
Noah did not ask.
He did not care what the octopus meant.
He reframed his focus and looked instead at the only thing he could sense at all.
The Long Night.
The flakes of snow.
The cold.
It was so pervasive that it buried everything else, drowned out every other current of information, made it almost impossible to gaze at anything but itself.

And Noah, sitting frozen in the falling snow with the whole of existence stretched out through him and nothing but winter coming back, turned the strangeness of that over, and asked himself the question underneath it.
What was this thing, that even Immense Ones felt it?
That even Poona, who made two titans stand still with a smile, had to weave herself a coat of Immensity against it?
What could reach past all of that?
And the thought came to him.
When it came to a thing that was truly immense, truly grand, then this cold, these endless particles of snow, were more immense than anything else in existence, right?
His existence went still.
What?
The cold that affected even Immense Ones was something more immense than them?
It was only a thought.
He had only thought it.
But the instant he thought it, he could not stop thinking it, could not unthink it, as he sensed the weavings of THE Long Night pouring down every thread and through every layer around him.
THUMP!
He felt the beat of his own heart, and a ridiculous, terrifying idea bloomed in him.
And a flicker of fear bloomed with it, because for all he had become, he was still human, and the idea was ridiculous!
But he felt possessed by his own intuition, the same intuiton that had never once led him wrong, and it did not care about the fear, and it opened his mouth for him.
"Come..." Noah said.
"Come...COME!"
BOOM!
His existence opened itself.

His Osmontian Chorionic Gonadotropin opened wide, the infinite Root of him unfolding, and instead of reaching for the slivers of Immensity that would not show themselves, Noah reached for the only thing that would.
He pulled on the terrible cold.
He pulled on the snow.
He pulled on the Long Night itself, and dragged it toward his existence!
And Moriarty, beside him, saw a thing that stopped even his ancient mind.
The snow moved.

All of it, at once, across the whole of the Domain, every falling flake and every drift of the descending cold turned as though a tide had been called, and it surged toward Noah’s small seated figure like an endless sea rushing to a single point, countless waves of white pouring in from every direction toward the one being in all of existence mad enough, or lost enough, or grand enough, to open his arms and call the winter home!

chapters.title: Chapter 5769: Pain! I
paragraphs: Pain was one of the most important things an existence could feel.

Most of the time, pain was a message. It was the plain, screaming report that something harmful to your existence was happening right now, and that you needed to act, to pull away, to run, to make it stop.
When a person put their hand over a fire and it burned, the pain was not nonsense. The pain was information. It was existence saying urgently, get your hand away from the fire, you dumb fuck.
And most of the time, people listened to their pain!
Most of the time, they should. A great deal of survival is nothng more than the wisdom to obey the thing that hurts.
But not always.
Noah was in a tremendous amount of pain.

The cold of THE Long Night was inside him now, and the freezing of it was not like heat’s burn. It was slow. It was a stilling. He felt every quark of his existence beginning to drag, to thicken, to lose the quick bright motion that made it alive, as though the whole churning engine of him were being packed in slower and slower ice!

His Provenance slowed. His Infinity slowed. The endless illusory pages that flickered off him came slower, and then slower, and his existence, the whole vast grand thing he had just become, was being brought grinding toward a halt.

Every existence, when The Long Night descended, had turned its authority and power to one task, which was to hold the cold OUT. To wall it off. To spend everything it had keeping the winter from reaching the core of it.
Noah had done the opposite. Noah had reached out and pulled the winter INTO the very Root of his Immensity!

And the pain of that was beyond bearing. He felt his Osmontian Chorionic Gonadotropin, the always-turning heart of what he was, go translucent, whitening, taking on the pale blue of deep ice. And from the Root the change spread outward, up through his weavings, out along his frozen threads, into his body, until Noah sat in the drifting snow of the Domain and became, in every visible way, a statue of ice.
Moriarty stared at him with utter incredulity.
And in the next moment a verdant eye bloomed into the air, its own Immensity roiling off it, and it looked at the rivers of snow still pouring endlessly into the frozen figure, and it blinked.
"Are you fucking serious?" it said. "This was our piece. This was one of the three, maybe, and you let him turn himself into a block of-"
"Wait." Moriarty’s deep voice rolled out across the hall.

"Wait? Wait for WHAT?" The verdant eye flared. "How did you let a potentially key figure turn himself into a popsicle in front of you? Why would such an idiotic chain of events be permitted to happen? I cannot fathom what possessed you to sit there and watch while he-"
"Wait," Moriarty said again, and he did not look away from Noah’s frozen figure, not for an instant!
His small neat spectacles were fixed on the statue of ice as though he could read something in it the eye could not. "Wait."
But wait for what?

The rivers of the Long Night went on pouring into the frozen thing, into a body that held no life now, no aura, no breath, no sense of anything living at all. By every measure the eye and the octopus both possessed, Noah Osmont had ceased. He had frozen solid at the core, and a Root frozen solid did not thaw!
They watched. And the winter poured in. And the ice held still.
Inside the pain, inside the profound stilling cold, Noah felt one thing that would not stop.

It pulsed. At the very Root of his existence, beneath the freezing and the slowing and the grinding halt of everything else, his Osmontian Chorionic Gonadotropin kept beating, and each beat carried a small terrible warmth. It was full of him!

Full of his boundless Infinity, his self-made Provenance, everything he had built himself into from nothing. And where the cold pressed in on his thoughts and his weavings and whispered to all of it to cease, to stop, to end, the pulse at his Root answered.
No.
The cold said cease. The pulse said no!
The cold said stop. The pulse said no!
Again, and again, and again, a heart that had generated itself from nothing refusing, with each beat, to be told it could not go on.
Until.
"AHH!"

Noah’s existence drew breath, as though it had a breath to draw, as though it had ever needed to breathe at all. Blue and white poured off him and through him, and slowly, gradually, his existence began to acclimate to the thing it had swallowed, and a prompt bloomed before his frozen eyes.
|By standard convention, your existence has ceased to function.|
|Your existence has arrived at ???|
His existence had ceased. Hah!

He would never agree to such words. Cease was a thing that happened to lesser existences. He had died and returned already, more than once, and he was not about to accept the verdict of a convention that had never met a being like him. His existence had not ceased.
But the other line was true. His existence had arrived somewhere. And exactly where, the prompt would not say.
The thought had barely formed when everything around him became clear, and what he saw was enough to make even Noah go still.
He was somewhere no living gaze had ever fallen!
It was....
Oh!
It was a place of cold beyond cold, a frozen domain stretching out further than sight, and everything in it was ice, or frost, or the deep blue stillness of things frozen forever.
The ground was rimed. The air itself hung heavy with drifting crystals.

And across the whole of that endless frozen expanse ran rivers and seas of white and blue, slow shining currents of pure cold winding away to horizons Noah could not find the end of, a whole existence built out of the substanse of the Long Night.
And seated upon those rivers were...the dead!

Not dead, quite. Worse than dead. Countless lifeforms, of every race and shape and size Noah had ever seen and a great many he had not, sat cross-legged upon the frozen currents, meditating, still as the ice around them.

Thousands of them. Tens of thousands, and more beyond that, seated in silent ranks across the frozen seas as far as he could perceive. And every one of them had eyes that were blank. No cognizance. No life. No spark of any awareness behind them at all, just open blank eyes staring at nothing while a swirling pillar of pure cold rose around each seated figure, wrapping them, feeding them, holding them in whatever frozen trance had taken them.
They sat. All of them sat.
Only Noah had risen!

He stood among the endless seated ranks, the one figure in all that frozen underworld who was upright, who had opened his eyes to cognizance instead of losing it, who looked around at the drifting crystals and the shining rivers of cold with alarm sharp in his gaze.
He turned, searching, taking in the impossible scale of the place.
And in the far distance, he saw a figure he knew.

It stood raised above the seated ranks, illusory and vast, and around it rose the single largest pillar of light in all that frozen expanse, a column of cold so immense it dwarfed every other. Its hands were lifted high. Its eyes, like all the rest, were blank, empty of any life or knowing. And from its raised palms poured endless rivers of the cold, feeding out into the frozen seas, feeding the whole terrible place.

Noah knew that figure. He had watched it die. It was The Overseeing One, the Immense One Vakochev had torn apart on the sundered Train, sitting here in this frozen underworld with blank eyes and lifted hands, pouring out the winter itself!
Noah felt the chill sink deeper and deeper into his existence, and alongside it, threaded all through the horror of it, came understanding, and wonder.

Because even now, even standing in this frozen place of blank-eyed meditators and a dead Immense One pouring out the cold, his existence had not stopped doing the thing it had begun. It went on drinking!
The winter kept flowing toward his Root, and around his own risen figure a pillar of cold swirled and rose, exactly like the thousands around the seated dead, and he absorbed it.
A pillar of cold for every seated thing.
Thousands of them, blank and lifeless and still.
And only Noah had risen.

chapters.title: Chapter 5770: Pain! II
paragraphs: The more his existence drank the particles he could not yet name, the more he understood.

He had no better word for them than the weavings of The Long Night, and so that was what he called them, and he drew them in, and with every one that sank into his Root a little more of the shape of the thing came clear to him!

He raised his hands, palms turned up, the same posture as the dead Immense One pouring the winter in the distance. But where light flowed out of that blank-eyed titan, something else flowed into Noah. Rivers of freezing white-blue brilliance ran down into his open palms, gathering there, pouring inward toward the Root that would not stop drinking.
Around him, the frozen underworld had become a storm.

He sat at the center of a swirling blue galaxy of snow, a slow turning vortex of white and blue drawn from every directon, pillars and rivers of the cold bending away from the seated dead and toward the one figure who had risen. It spiraled into him, all of it!
And Noah, half-frozen, his lips barely able to part, began to whisper, and as he whispered the storm answered, more and more of the freezing brilliance turning to feed him.
"When heat leaves a room," Noah said, "nothing has been added. You have only removed the agitation. The air slows. The dust settles."
A pillar of white-blue bent toward him and poured in.
"Many call this cold a catastrophe. An unprovoked curse. A sudden horror falling out of a broken sky. It is none of those things."His whisper carried, low and certain, through the frozen dark.
"It is... the withdrawal of an unearned indulgence. It is the arrival of pain."
More rivers turned. More of the winter came to him!

"Existence looked upon the work of entire ages, and it saw nothing worth preserving. It saw billions of lineages rotting inside the same borrowed frameworks. It saw the same scripted wars fought over and over, and not a single authentic new thing produced across ten thousand cycles. So it adjusted the temperature. It introduced a cold. A new...Cycle."
The storm tightened around him, and the brilliance poured down into his palms!
"The cold is not malice. It is a boundary condition. It is existence dropping its floor to zero and asking every lifeform one non-negotiable question."

His frozen lips shaped the words slowly. "Can you generate your own fire? Or were you only ever warming your hands over someone else’s funeral pyre? The high with no foundation turn to glass, because they were always made of glass. The weak endure, because they never had a blanket to lose in the first place."
He drew one long breath of the freezing air.
"This... is not the end of things. It is the beginning of an existence filled with Immensity."
BOOM!
His words landed heavy and clear in the frozen dark, and the instant he finished them, something moved!
Off to the side, among the endless seated ranks of blank-eyed things, one of them turned its head.
Its gaze came around to Noah, and it was hollow, empty of any life or knowing, and yet it had turned, and it had turned toward him!

It had the body of a great lion, heavy and powerful, muscle wrapped in pale frost-rimed hide. And where a lion’s head should have sat, there was another head entirely, a thing that was not quite a lion and not quite a man and not quite any beast Noah could name, wrong in a way the eye slid off of.

Terrible coldness wreathed the whole of it, pouring off its frame in visible waves, and it rose from its seat on the frozen river and fixed its hollow gaze upon the one figure in all that underworld who had dared to rise.
Then it moved!
Noah barely saw it. One instant it was seated across the frozen expanse, the next its paw was smashing down toward his head, and he threw up a hand on pure instinct.
BOOM!
The impact was terrible!

It caught him and flung him up and back, tearing him off the frozen river, hurling him across the underworld until he smashed into a massive floating meteorite of glacial stone, a stellar mountain of ice hanging in the frozen dark, and the crash of him against it cracked the ice for miles.
And his eyes cleared!
The pain and the impact tore him out of his reverie, out of the half-frozen trance of drinking the winter, and Noah’s whole existence buzzed suddenly with frost and Provenance both.
He pushed himself up off the shattered glacial stone and looked across the dark at the thing that had struck him.
It spoke. Its voice was heavy, and it carried no cognizance at all!

"What could you possibly know about beginnings?" it said. "About the cold? What do you know of pain? In existence, there is only pain. There has only ever been pain. You understand nothing of this cold, and nothing of that pain. Disappear."
The thing rose to its full height, and then it came at him, and it came terrifyingly fast!

It did not strike the way a beast strikes, or the way a human strikes. As it moved, the air in front of it changed. A figure took shape there, a solid three-dimensional thing hanging in the frozen dark, edges hard and bright, a simple pointed solid of only a few faces, and it glowed a deep yellow.
The instant it finished forming, everything inside its bounds pulled, wrenched toward its center with a violence that would have bent his whole existence like a crumpled piece of paper!
His Provenance surged as an endless sea of Dreams erupted around him!
He dodged, and frost sheeted off him with the motion, and another figure was already taking shape.

This one was larger and more complex, a many-faced solid glowing violet, and where the yellow one had pulled, this one shoved. The space inside it detonated outward in a wave of repelling force, and Noah felt like it could throw him countless Gigaparsecs away and even push his Quarks apart!

The push caught his shoulder and flung him spinning through the frozen dark, and he caught himself on nothing but the sheer weight of his own Provenance, immense frost pouring off his existence as he did.

The yellow and the violet shapes formed in front of this lifeform carried invisible waves of authority and frost as they came at him again, pull and push, one after another, faster now, and Noah set his own existence against them!

Rivers of dream poured off him, and rivers of Infinity, all of it laced through with the frost he had drunk into his Root, surging up around his figure in a churning storm of white-blue brilliance. And into that storm he spoke, dragging the words up out of his frozen chest, the oldest and truest thing he had, the Letters of his own Tongue.
"I AM."
WAA!
The pulling shape closed on him, and his Provenance met it, and the frost-laced rivers of his dream held the pull at bay.
"I AM!"

The pushing shape detonated against him, and he did not fly this time. He stood, existence buzzing, frost and dream and Infinity roaring around him, and he bellowed it again into the teeth of the thing that had come to unmake him.
"I AM! I AM! I AM!"

Each repetition landed like a hammer on an anvil, his own existence asserting itself against a reality that the beast was trying to reshape, refusing the pull, refusing the push, refusing to be moved or unmade or told what he was!
The frozen underworld shook with it. Glacial waves erupted where his rivers met the beast’s figures, whole sheets of ice thrown up from the frozen ground and detonating in the dark!

And all around them the seated ranks sat blank and undisturbed through the violence, thousands of hollow eyes staring at nothing while the one risen thing and the one that had come to put it down tore the frozen dark apart between them!

Rivers of dream poured off him, and rivers of Infinity, all of it laced through with the frost he had drunk into his Root, surging up around his figure in a churning storm of white-blue brilliance.
And into that storm he spoke, dragging the words up out of his frozen chest, the oldest and truest thing he had, the Letters of his own Tongue.
"I AM."
WAA!
The pulling shape closed on him, and his Provenance met it, and the frost-laced rivers of his dream held the pull at bay.
"I AM!"
The pushing shape detonated against him, and he did not fly this time.
He stood, existence buzzing, frost and dream and Infinity roaring around him, and he bellowed it again into the teeth of the thing that had come to unmake him.
"I AM!
I AM!
I AM!"

Each repetition landed like a hammer on an anvil, his own existence asserting itself against a reality that the beast was trying to reshape, refusing the pull, refusing the push, refusing to be moved or unmade or told what he was!
The frozen underworld shook with it.
Glacial waves erupted where his rivers met the beast’s figures, whole sheets of ice thrown up from the frozen ground and detonating in the dark!

And all around them the seated ranks sat blank and undisturbed through the violence, thousands of hollow eyes staring at nothing while the one risen thing and the one that had come to put it down tore the frozen dark apart between them!

chapters.title: Chapter 5771: Pain! III
paragraphs: Noah had let it go on long enough.
His eyes opened wide, and from them poured beams of incandescent light, cutting through the frozen dark as he spoke a single word!
"Enough!"
WAA!
And he imposed THE MORTAL COIL.

The Word settled over the two shapes the lifeform had just rendered, the yellow that pulled and the violet that pushed, and it did to them what it did to all borrowed things. It named their authority as a mortal, ending thing, and the authority answered. The shapes dimmed. Their edges softened!

The terrible force bound inside them dropped by half in an instant, the pull weakening, the push guttering, and Noah reached out and closed his hand and crushed both of them as they burst into nothing.
Then he brought his hand down!

It fell like a hammer! The whole weight of his Provenance came down with it, more than five hundred, an existence that had generated itself from nothing and refused to be told what it was, and it smashed into the frost-wreathed beast with a force the frozen thing could not hold.
BOOM!
The lifeform exploded!
It came apart all at once, its lion’s body and its wrong unnameable head and the terrible cold that had wreathed it shattering outward into countless drifting pieces. And then the pieces turned.

They did not scatter and fade. Every shard of the shattered beast, every wisp of its frost and every fragment of its weavings, turned in the frozen air and streamed toward Noah, drawn to him like the winter itself was drawn to him, pouring into his existence and his Root.
And with them came the pain!

Noah’s whole existence seized as the fragments sank into him. They came full of a suffering so vast and so old that it rolled through him in waves and nearly took him to his knees. It was not his pain!

It was the Yali’s, and it was worse than any wound, a deep and grinding agony threaded through with every dark thing an existence could feel, terror and despair and a bottomless, exhausted hopelessness, the emotional sediment of a thing that had been made to hurt for so long it had forgoten there was anything else.
It poured into him with the frost and the knowledge, and for a moment Noah, who did not show pain had to fight simply to keep standing under the weight of a stranger’s misery.
And prompts bloomed across his sight.
|You have collapsed the weavings of a YALI NIGHT LIFEFORM.|
|You have absorbed wisps of its knowledge of THE LONG NIGHT.|
|You have experienced the pain of a lifeform that was among thousands experimented upon for millions of years by an unknown existence, across a small region of existence.|
|What you feel is merely a sliver of that pain.|
A sliver.
Everything crashing through him now, the terror and the despair...all of it was a fraction, a single drop wrung from an ocean.
|You are perceiving a system of existence: THE RENDERING.|

|A wielder conjures a closed figure, a Shape, and everything inside its bounds is manipulated. The COLOR of the Shape decides what it does. The COMPLEXITY of the Shape decides how strong it is. A simple figure of few faces is weak. An intricate figure of many faces is devastating.|

|The YALI wields the Rendering through NEGATIVE PROVENANCE PSEUDO-IMMENSITY. It generates nothing of its own. It renders using the borrowed, hollowed authority of the Long Night that pours through it, an imitaton of true Immensity, a power that mimics the real thing without the living Root beneath it.|

|THE YELLOW SHAPE: a figure of Pull. Everything within its bounds is drawn toward its center. At the strength this Yali rendered it, it could crush an existence inward with a force a trillion collapsing Dimensions could only dream of.|

|THE VIOLET SHAPE: a figure of Push. Everything within its bounds is thrust outward. At the strength this Yali rendered it, it could push an existence apart until its very quarks split and disintegrated.|
Noah stood among the falling snow with the last of the Yali flowing into him, the pain slowly ebbing as his existence swallowed it.

He understood now what had nearly killed him. Not a beast as much as...a victim. A hollowed, tortured thing rendering shapes of pull and push out of borrowed cold, wielding a power that pulled hard enough to crush trillions of dimensions and pushed hard enough to scatter his atoms!
And then, above him at this time, the wasteland stirred.
Noah lifted his incandescent gaze, and from the endless ranks of blank-eyed seated things, ten of them rose at once!
Every one of them emanated waves of light grander than the thing he had just dissipated, deeper, stronger, further along whatever terrible road had made them.
Ten hollow figures, rising from the frozen rivers, ten pillars of cold swelling around them, and all ten turned their empty gazes up toward the one risen thing in all that frozen dark.
They spoke, at the same instant, in one flat cognizance-less voice that carried no anger and no life at all.
"You do not understand anything about pain."
Then they turned into streaks of light and surged toward him!
And Noah continued to drink the rivers of the Long Night as he watched on coldly!
The ten came at him as streaks of light, and Noah met them the way he had learned to meet everything.
He took what had tried to kill him and made it his!
He had watched the Yali render its shapes of pull and push, and then learned all about it when he devoured its weavings.
The methodology seemed...lethal!
So!

As the first streak resolved into a hollow-eyed thing lunging for his throat, Noah raised a hand and his Provenance answered, and a shape bloomed in the frozen air before him. His own. A figure of pull, yellow-bright, rendered not out of borrowed cold but out of his own boundless self-made authority.
He caught the lunging thing inside it!

The shape pulled, and it did not pull cleanly. Noah made it worse than that. He tightened the figure as it drew the hollow lifeform in, wrenching the body toward a center that kept shrinking, and the thing came apart inside the pull the way meat comes apart in a grinder, crushed and wrung and torn all at once!
Its existence shattered, and streamed toward him, and poured in!
And the pain came with it!

He saw it die. Not this death, the true one, the old one. He saw a creature of scaled hide and too many eyes, a thing that had once been proud, held down while an Immense One peeled the authorty out of it strip by strip, made it into a hollow engine for the cold, and left it seated in the dark for an age with just enough awareness to know what it had lost. The memory sank into Noah with the frost!
The second came, and the third.

He rendered a shape of push for them, violet and hard, and when they surged toward him he detonated it and smashed them away, hurling the hollow things back across the frozen underworld, buying the half-second he needed!

When a hollow lifeform came close, too close, thinking to grapple him, Noah conjured a shape of push directly against its body, an inch from its frame, and let it fire. The thing did not fly away. It could not!
The push had nowhere to send it but apart, and its whole existence was pulled in every direction at once, torn into streams of light that flowed, all of them, into him.
They fought him, and they wept as they fought.

Every one of the hollow things looked at him with the same accusatory gaze, empty of cognizance and full of something worse than cognizance, and from the blank eyes of several of them ran tears, bloody tears sliding down frost-rimed faces while they threw their borrowed shapes at him and died on his own.

They did not know why they hated him. There was not enough left in them to know anything. But something below knowing had turned its grief on him, and it said, over and over, in the flat chorus of the dying, the same thing.
You do not understand pain.

The fourth died, and the fifth, and Noah absorbed each one, and each one gave him a death. A city of them, frozen. A lineage, harvested. A mother-thing that had been made to watch. He took it all in, every unjust ending, every strip of authority torn from a living thing by an Immense One’s patient hands, and his existence buzzed and swelled and grieved with the inflow of it, and still he did not stop!
He was ruthless. He had to be. He rendered pull and crush, push and scatter, moving through the ten hollow things with cold efficency.

The sixth he crushed into a pulling shape until it was a point. The seventh he pushed apart at the seams. The eighth and the ninth came together, and he caught them both in a single yellow figure and drew them into each other until there was nothing left to draw!
And then there was one.
The tenth rose before him, and it was a woman.

She had white hair, long and drifting in the frozen air, and her existence was already crumpling, already coming apart under the weight of everything Noah had done to her kind and the weight of whatever had been done to her long before.

Bloody tears ran from her hollow eyes. She did not render a shape. She did not lunge. She only looked at him as her existence failed, and she spoke, and unlike the others, her voice was not entirely flat.
Something had surfaced in her at the very end, some last drowned ember of the self she had been before an Immense One hollowed her out.
"Do you,"she said, "understand our pain?"
Noah stood still.

"Why did you never do anything about our pain?"Her existence guttered, streaming apart into motes of white light that drifted toward him even as she spoke. "Will you do anything now, now that you take all that we have left?"
And then she was gone, dissolving into light, and her existence flowed into Noah like all the others, and her pain flowed with it.

Hers was clear. The others had been hollowed past memory, their agony a formless roar. But something in the woman had held onto herself to the very end, and so what poured into Noah was not just pain but a life.
He felt her taken. He felt the Immense One’s hands.
His existence buzzed and shook with the memory of it, and the prompts bloomed through the grief.
|You have collapsed the weavings of ten YALI NIGHT LIFEFORMS.|
|You have absorbed their pain, their memories, and the manner of their unjust deaths. Each was hollowed by an unknown Immense One and made an engine of THE LONG NIGHT eventually. |
|What you carry now is no longer a sliver.|
And with the last of the white-haired woman came understanding of a shape he had not seen before.
|THE RENDERING: a third Shape analyzed and absorbed.|

|THE GREEN SHAPE: a figure of Grow. Everything within its bounds is made to expand. At the strength these lifeforms render it, it can force an existence to grow beyond what it can hold, swelling its weavings past their own bounds until the existence bursts apart from the inside.|
|You now perceive three of multiple Shapes: Pull, Push, Grow.|

Noah stood alone in the frozen dark, ten deaths heavier, an entire chorus of stolen lives buzzing and grieving inside a Root that would not stop drinking the winter, and the woman’s last words would not leave him.
Will you do anything now, now that you take all that we have left?

chapters.title: Chapter 5772: Condition!
paragraphs: Noah breathed heavily, and his existence drank on!
More and more of the rivers poured into him, and he had a word for them now, or nearly one.Negative Immensity.

That was what these endless currents of snow carried, slivers of it, the power the hollow Night Lifeforms had wielded against him, the thing that let them render their shapes and bend reality so terribly inside their bounds.
It was Immensity turned inside out, hollowed and cold, and it was flowing into his Root without pause.
His existence buzzed with the possibilities of it. One had risen first. He had taken it, and ten had risen. He had taken them, and now the question remained. How many more were about to rise?

His Root did not feel finished drinking. Not yet. He could feel it, still reaching, still swallowing the winter, still not done becoming whatever it was becoming. He looked down, past his own feet, across the endless frozen underworld to the seated ranks below.
"Motherfucker..."
He could not help the curse.

Because down below, the largest pillar of all had begun to move. The hollow figure of the dead Immense One, the one who had sat with his palms raised and the rivers of the winter pouring endlessly out of them, was rising from his seat! His blank eyes, empty of all life, lifted from the frozen river and came around, up, across the whole vast dark, and settled directly on Noah.
Noah looked back at it. He had only wanted to keep drinking. That was all. But nothing was ever made simple, and it never would be!
He shook his head, and his voice boomed out across the frozen dark.
"Now this is just ridiculously unfair. I could face the other ones. But you, getting up right now? There is not even a need to fight."
Yes.

He could feel the pressure of the thing, and it was not a pressure he could stand against. This was the Immense One whose corpse, out in external existence, had given rise to a record of Lucy herself. Whatever stood here in the frozen dark was beyond him. There was no version of this fight that Noah won!
The massive figure of the Overseeing One rose into the air, blank-eyed and vast, and it spoke..
"Existence... is rarely fair," it said.

"Immense Ones have stood before lesser lifeforms who had no power, who could do nothing to defend themselves, and they have done to them whatever they wished. Others across existence have done whatever they wished and ended countless lives. That was unfair. It happened anyway. Across existence, countless unfair things occur every single minute." The hollow gaze held him. "So why can existence not be unfair to you?"
HUUM!
Why could existence not be unfair to him.
The words were heavy and suffocating!

The massive figure rose higher, and seas of coldness surged up around it and began to turn, rotating slowly around the risen titan like stellar galaxies of pure winter, vast wheels of white and blue circling a dead thing that could unmake him with a thought.
Noah looked on coldly, and he thought.

He turned over every possibility he had, every move, every art, every scrap of what he had become, and the honest answer was that there was not much. Not against this. But the dead thing had not struck him. It had risen, and it had spoken, and it had not struck, and that meant something.
A thing that meant to kill him would have killed him. This one wanted something else, and where there was a want, there was a door.
So Noah thought about everything he had learned, every sliver of knowledge he had drunk from the endless cold, and he found the shape of a question, and he asked it grandly.

"Existence can always be unfair to me," Noah said."I will take it as it comes. But this is not simply unfairness, is it? I have understood something, drinking all of this. This endless cold of the Long Night is a natural selection, laid across everything in existence. It is the arrival of pain and accountability."
His incandescent eyes did not waver. "So why. Why do you try to stop me from taking it?"
He had to ask, because he could feel his Root transforming, feel it nearly there, nearly done with whatever it was making of him. Nearly. But not quite!
The hollow Night Lifeform drifted until it came level with him, blank eyes to incandescent ones, and it answered.

"This power is intended to apply pressure across a slovenly and corpulent existence," it said, "and to rectify many wrongs. You cannot take it unless you agree to do what it intends. Kill the viruses plaguing existence, and allow existence to thrive. That is the condition of THE LONG NIGHT."
A condition.
To take this power, he had to agree to a condition!

To kill what plagued existence, and let existence thrive. Noah held that, and a piece of a much larger puzzle turned over in his mind, because now he understood, or thought he did, why Lucy had risen from the Overseeing One’s corpse out in external existence and planted a dense forest of frozen worlds across the ruin. The cold did not only kill. It cleared ground. It killed the rot and made room for new things to grow.
Noah thought about it for only a moment.
"Existence is vast, and it is full of terrors," he said. "I can accept a condition to cleanse existence."
WAA!
And the moment the words left him, the underworld answered.

All across the endless frozen expanse, every seated figure that stretched away past the limits of sight, countless blank-eyed hollow things, raised their heads at once. Every hollow gaze turned upward and found Noah, all of them, in the same instant, and every one of them spoke together, in a single flat voice that rolled across the frozen dark like a tide.
|So it shall be.|
HUUM!
The hollow Immense One clenched its fist.
And in the next moment, the frozen wasteland rose to answer the pact!

Existential Conduits erupted from all around, from the frozen rivers and the glacial stone and the drifting dark, great pillars of them filled with white-blue frost, and they came swirlng up around Noah’s figure, encircling him, wheeling slowly like the galaxies of cold that turned around the dead titan!

And from those Conduits, tendrils lashed out. Potent, pure, brilliant white-blue, they whipped through the frozen air and fastened onto him, one driving into his chest, others onto his arms, his legs, his limbs, fixing him in the center of the swirling pillars.
And through those tendrils, the purest slivers of Negative Immensity he had yet touched began to pour into his existence.
The pain was ten times worse!
It was beyond the Yali’s, beyond the ten, beyond anything he had swallowed so far, a flood of pure hollowed cold driven straight into the core of him, and Noah’s whole existence seized under it.
But his Root did not falter!

For the first time since he had reached out and pulled the winter into himself, his Root stopped feeling as though it might cease. It stabilized. In the middle of the worst pain he had ever known, the always-turning heart of him steadied, took hold, and began, once again, to pulse. And with each pulse it transformed his existence, the way it had transformed him once before in the dark.

Gradually, the excruciating agony began to plateau. And then, past the plateau, it changed. The burning of the cold cooled into something else, a deep and steady coolness that was not pain at all, spreading through him from the Root outward.
His Osmontian Chorionic Gonadotropin grew heavy, and vast, and grand!
And it accepted The Long Night, fully, wholeheartedly, drawing the endless winter into itself and making it, at last, a part of what he was!

"Now this is just ridiculously unfair.
I could face the other ones.
But you, getting up right now?
There is not even a need to fight."
Yes.
He could feel the pressure of the thing, and it was not a pressure he could stand against.
This was the Immense One whose corpse, out in external existence, had given rise to a record of Lucy herself.
Whatever stood here in the frozen dark was beyond him.
There was no version of this fight that Noah won!
The massive figure of the Overseeing One rose into the air, blank-eyed and vast, and it spoke..
"Existence... is rarely fair," it said.
"Immense Ones have stood before lesser lifeforms who had no power, who could do nothing to defend themselves, and they have done to them whatever they wished.
Others across existence have done whatever they wished and ended countless lives.
That was unfair.
It happened anyway.
Across existence, countless unfair things occur every single minute." The hollow gaze held him.
"So why can existence not be unfair to you?"
HUUM!
Why could existence not be unfair to him.
The words were heavy and suffocating!

The massive figure rose higher, and seas of coldness surged up around it and began to turn, rotating slowly around the risen titan like stellar galaxies of pure winter, vast wheels of white and blue circling a dead thing that could unmake him with a thought.
Noah looked on coldly, and he thought.
He turned over every possibility he had, every move, every art, every scrap of what he had become, and the honest answer was that there was not much.
Not against this.
But the dead thing had not struck him.
It had risen, and it had spoken, and it had not struck, and that meant something.
A thing that meant to kill him would have killed him.
This one wanted something else, and where there was a want, there was a door.
So Noah thought about everything he had learned, every sliver of knowledge he had drunk from the endless cold, and he found the shape of a question, and he asked it grandly.
"Existence can always be unfair to me," Noah said."I will take it as it comes.
But this is not simply unfairness, is it?
I have understood something, drinking all of this.
This endless cold of the Long Night is a natural selection, laid across everything in existence.
It is the arrival of pain and accountability."
His incandescent eyes did not waver.
"So why.
Why do you try to stop me from taking it?"
He had to ask, because he could feel his Root transforming, feel it nearly there, nearly done with whatever it was making of him.
Nearly.
But not quite!
The hollow Night Lifeform drifted until it came level with him, blank eyes to incandescent ones, and it answered.
"This power is intended to apply pressure across a slovenly and corpulent existence," it said, "and to rectify many wrongs.
You cannot take it unless you agree to do what it intends.
Kill the viruses plaguing existence, and allow existence to thrive.
That is the condition of THE LONG NIGHT."
A condition.
To take this power, he had to agree to a condition!
To kill what plagued existence, and let existence thrive.

Noah held that, and a piece of a much larger puzzle turned over in his mind, because now he understood, or thought he did, why Lucy had risen from the Overseeing One’s corpse out in external existence and planted a dense forest of frozen worlds across the ruin.
The cold did not only kill.
It cleared ground.
It killed the rot and made room for new things to grow.
Noah thought about it for only a moment.
"Existence is vast, and it is full of terrors," he said.
"I can accept a condition to cleanse existence."
WAA!
And the moment the words left him, the underworld answered.
All across the endless frozen expanse, every seated figure that stretched away past the limits of sight, countless blank-eyed hollow things, raised their heads at once.
Every hollow gaze turned upward and found Noah, all of them, in the same instant, and every one of them spoke together, in a single flat voice that rolled across the frozen dark like a tide.
|So it shall be.|
HUUM!
The hollow Immense One clenched its fist.
And in the next moment, the frozen wasteland rose to answer the pact!

Existential Conduits erupted from all around, from the frozen rivers and the glacial stone and the drifting dark, great pillars of them filled with white-blue frost, and they came swirlng up around Noah’s figure, encircling him, wheeling slowly like the galaxies of cold that turned around the dead titan!
And from those Conduits, tendrils lashed out.

Potent, pure, brilliant white-blue, they whipped through the frozen air and fastened onto him, one driving into his chest, others onto his arms, his legs, his limbs, fixing him in the center of the swirling pillars.
And through those tendrils, the purest slivers of Negative Immensity he had yet touched began to pour into his existence.
The pain was ten times worse!
It was beyond the Yali’s, beyond the ten, beyond anything he had swallowed so far, a flood of pure hollowed cold driven straight into the core of him, and Noah’s whole existence seized under it.
But his Root did not falter!
For the first time since he had reached out and pulled the winter into himself, his Root stopped feeling as though it might cease.
It stabilized.
In the middle of the worst pain he had ever known, the always-turning heart of him steadied, took hold, and began, once again, to pulse.
And with each pulse it transformed his existence, the way it had transformed him once before in the dark.
Gradually, the excruciating agony began to plateau.
And then, past the plateau, it changed.
The burning of the cold cooled into something else, a deep and steady coolness that was not pain at all, spreading through him from the Root outward.
His Osmontian Chorionic Gonadotropin grew heavy, and vast, and grand!
And it accepted The Long Night, fully, wholeheartedly, drawing the endless winter into itself and making it, at last, a part of what he was!

chapters.title: Chapter 5773: Target!
paragraphs: <Existential Interlude- Commitment>
In one of the earliest ages, when existence was still deciding what it would remember, there was an Immense One who made a promise.

She was called the Lamplighter, because in the dark of that age she had lit the first lights, and beings had gathered to them, and from those who gathered she had made a Provenance Lineage, a line of existences born of her own origin and carrying a spark of what she was. She loved them.

And when the first winter of that age came, and the hunting things came with it, she stood before her Lineage and she said: I will hold the dark back from you, all of it, for as long as one of you still breathes.
And existence heard her say it.

The winter was long. The Lamplighter held. She held for an age, and it cost a little of herself every night, spent against the dark so her Lineage could sleep. And then a night came when a greater thing than the winter stood before her and offered her a bargain: step aside for one night, only one, and be made whole, be given back everything the holding had taken.
One night. Her Lineage would never know.
The Lamplighter was tired past the reach of words. And she stepped aside.
For one night.

In the morning she stood again, whole and restored, and held the dark back as she always had, and she told herself no promise had been broken, because she had only rested, and the dark had only taken a little.
But existence had heard her say it. All of it, for as long as one of you still breathes.

And existence does not hear the words a being means. It hears the words a being says. She had said all of it. She had given one night. And a commitment, once made, is not a thing that bends to how tired you are.

Her Lineage began to fail. A spark went out here, a line of descent went dark there, and she could not find the cause, and she burned herself down to nothing searching for it, and never once understood that the cause was a night she had already forgotten. The last of her Lineage died with her name on its lips, and she died holding it, and existence, which had heard her promise, kept its own side to the very end.
A commitment is not a wish. It is a sentence you write into existence, and existence finishes the sentence whether or not you are still there to read it.
<THE True Human Emperor>
Noah did not know how long he had been gone.

He opened his eyes, and the light around him was dim, the Existential Conduits that had swirled up to bind him now hanging quiet and low, their white-blue frost dimmed to a soft glow. The tendrils had withdrawn. The pact was made. And his body, when he looked down at it, was glistening.
He was not the same shape!

A suit of Provenance wrapped him, a second skin of living light that clung to every line of his frame, pale white-blue and faintly luminous, fitted so close it moved as he moved, more a state of his existence than a garment.

Beneath it his body had changed. The muscle of him looked as though it had been cut from crystalline ice, clear and faceted and cold, and he understood without testing it that it was harder than any material he had come across in all of existence, a body that had drunk the winter and set!

His hair had gone white-blue, drifting in the still air. From his eyes rose a pillar of light, magisterial, cold, a column of radiance that lit the dim Conduits arond him. And on his chest, where his heart would have been, a mobius strip turned. It spun endlessly, a twisting band of light looping back into itself without beginning or end, turning like an engine, and Noah knew what it was! It was the reflection, worn on the outside now, of the Root that turned inside him without cease.
Prompts bloomed across his pillar-lit sight.
|Your Osmontian Chorionic Gonadotropin has devoured dense concentrations of Slivers of Negative Immensity.|
|It has transformed. It is now a DUAL CONCEPTUAL AND PHYSICAL EXISTENTIAL ROOT OF IMMENSITY.|
|It has grown. Its transformation is still ongoing.|
Dual!

Noah read the word twice. Every Root in existence chose a side, Conceptual or Physical, Empyros or Fiend, and Moriarty had walked him through the whole absolute divide of it, and his own Root had refused to answer. Now it had answered. Both!
It had drunk the winter and come out the other side as a thing the octopus had no box for, a Root born of an Infinity that was true in two directions at once, and now true in both!
|Elevated capabilities, current:|
|Your Root now adds 40 to 80 to all attributes daily, scaling as it grows.|
|You have grasped the initial weavings of the inherent Ruling of Existence of THE RENDERING, as it was preset within the Night Lifeforms.|
|You have developed immunity to the basal cold effect of THE LONG NIGHT. Only that effect, for now.|
|Your Provenance, and all weavings of your existence, now carry the undeniable chill of Negative Immensity. It can penetrate any form of authority.|

The chill that had nearly ended him was his now, threaded through everything he was, and it did not respect authority, any authority, the way the Long Night itself did not respect the mighty. Whatever he touched with his Provenance from this moment carried the winter in it!
He looked at himself!
|THE True Human Emperor / THE Human Dreamer|
|VERITAS: 611|
|PROVENANCE: 624|
|POTENTIA: INFINITE|
|PONDUS: 606|
|OSMONTIAN MOIRAI: 618|
|Provenances: THE Provenance of THE Human Dreamer (native, generated), THE Provenance of THE Immense Sovereign (claimed).|
|Infinity: DIALETHEIC INFINITY.|
|Existential Root: THE Osmontian Chorionic Gonadotropin. A Dual Conceptual and Physical Existential Root of Immensity. Transformation ongoing.|
Six hundred! He took all of it in calmly.
Then the snow came around him, drifting close, and he felt something he had not felt since the Long Night began.
A breeze!

The snow moved past his crystalline skin and it was only snow. Cool, soft, a breeze off a winter field. The cold that had crawled into his Root and frozen him solid touched him now and found nothing to freeze, and he stood in the falling white of the frozen underworld and felt, for the first time in a while...comfortable.
Then he blinked.
Because he sensed pages fluttering.
He looked ahead, and there was a woman.
She stood in the air before him where no one had stood a moment ago, and she wore a dress of frost, white and flowing, that moved around her as though it were made of falling snow that never landed.

She was tall, and she was still, and had dark hair drawn back from a pale sharp face, a mouth that had never needed to smile, eyes that held a coldness and an imperiousness beyond any measure Noah had for either.She looked like a thing that had been obeyed since before obedience had a name.
And her eyes held cognizance!

Every other thing in this underworld had stared at nothing out of blank hollow eyes. This one saw. She looked out over the frozen expanse with a mind behind her gaze, and down below her, all across the endless ranks, the hollow Night Lifeforms had gone back to sitting, settling onto the frozen rivers once more, storms of snow gathering and turning around each of them as the underworld resumed its long cold work.

She did not address him. She did not greet him, or name him, or acknowledge in any way that he had risen where thousands had not, or that he had made a pact with the Long Night that not one other thing in this place had ever made. She simply reached out, unhurried, and plucked one of the pages fluttering around her out of the air.
It looked like a sheet of ice. Thin, clear, faintly glowing.
She threw it toward him, and she spoke.
"Your first target to cleanse," she said. "You have twenty-four hours."
Noah caught the page.
It was cold in his hand, though the cold no longer meant anything to him, and on its surface an image had formed, an image set into the ice the way a face is set into a frozen pond.

A young man. He had the bearing of a young king, the poise of one born to a throne, handsome and compsed. But his eyes were wrong for his face. They were aged. Ancient. The eyes of a thing that had lived far longer than the young face that held them, looking out of that youth with a weight no youth should carry.
And Noah knew him!

He had met this being before. He had read and understood the unfortunate thing that had been done to him, a Vessel that had been targeted by THE Sealed One as what stood in that young king’s body was neither wholly itself nor wholly the thing that had tried to take it.
It was Adrastia!
The one who had the rather unfortunate case of being mixed with THE Sealed One!
