chapters.title: Chapter 5774: Nature Is Self Sustaining!
paragraphs: Noah turned the page of ice over in his hand, and the image of the young king turned with it, and beneath the face, script formed in the frost.

It gave him a place. It was nowhere near the Cluster where he had last seen the young king. Adrastia had gone far. He had crossed out of the split train entirely and sealed himself inside an Elsedimension, a pocket of reality set apart from the ordinary flow of existence.
The script named it only by its shape, a small sealed Elsedimension hung off the edge of a dying Dimension, quiet and hidden and hard to find. Adrastia was there!
Noah read it twice, and then he looked up at the woman in the frost dress.
"He did nothing wrong."

She did not answer. She stood in the air above the seated dead with her pages fluttering around her, and she waited like a person waits for a child to finish a sentence they have already decided is foolish.

"I have met him," Noah said. "I have read him. Something came to swallow him whole and he did the one thing none of the others managed. He fought. He swallowed half of it back. What is standing in that broken Dimension is not THE Sealed One wearing a body. It is a being who was attacked, and refused to go quietly, and got left holding half of his attacker inside his own skin for his trouble."
He held the page up. "That is not a virus. That is a wound."
"A wound does not stop bleeding," the woman said, "because it was unfairly given."
Her voice was calm!

"The condition does not ask whether a thing chose to become what it is," she went on."It asks only what the thing is. And what sits inside that Elsedimension is a piece of THE Sealed One, alive, connected, and growing. A half is still a half. Do you imagine the plague cares which of its carriers meant no harm?"
"I imagine the plague does not get to write its own justification," Noah said.
"No. Existence writes it. You agreed to that a while ago. You have always agreed."

She plucked another page from the air, looked at it, let it go. "You said the words. The dead below you heard them. Existence heard them. That was a commitment, and I would counsel you, as one who has kept a great many of them, to understand what you have promised before you begin arguing about which of the promised things you would prefer not to do."
Noah was quiet for a moment.
"Can you be...a bit clearer on this target?"
"The target is not his death,"she said.
Noah’s eyes narrowed.

"You were told to cleanse. You assumed cleansing meant killing. What plagues existence inside that Elsedimension is the Assimilation Factor. The connection. The living thread that runs from the being called Adrastia back to THE Sealed One, and through which THE Sealed One still reaches, still grows, still uses him whether he knows it or not. That thread is the virus. The man is only the host."
"So the goal," Noah said slowly, "is the thread."
"The goal is to eliminate the Assimilation Factor’s connection to THE Sealed One. Entirely. There are two ways to do that."
She raised one pale finger. "You may sever his life completely. A dead host carries no thread."
A second finger arose.
"Or you may split him from THE Sealed One completely. Cut the thread and leave the host standing, whole, and his own. The condition does not care which. Existence does not care which. Both cleanse."
Her eyes held his. "Only you care which. So choose, and be quick."
Noah looked down at the page, at the young king with the ancient eyes. There was always a door!
The door opening now...he felt like he could do it. After all, he held the Provenance for it!
He looked back up at her.
"Who...are you?"
She regarded him for a long moment, and when she answered, her voice had changed!
"I am a caretaker," she said."I am a remnant of the cold. That is all of what I am, and it is enough."
The pages turned slowly around her.

"When a Night comes, it gathers everything that sat down under it. Every existence that went hollow. Every pain that was inflicted and never answered for. Every wrong that was done in the warm ages and left to rot because no one was cold enough to correct it. The Night keeps all of it. It does not forget. And from all of that, from the boundless pain and the boundless retribution the ages leave behind, something is left over. A residue. A thing that stays when the winter passes, to tend what the winter made."

Her cold eyes did not blink. "That is me. I am what is left of every Night that came before this one. I am a collection of pain that was never answered, and a collection of retribution that was never paid. I am not a lifeform. I was, once, the way you are now. I have set that down. I am the cold’s caretaker, and I hand out its pages, and that is all."

"I am handing you this page. I have handed you the next page, and the one after. I am standing in the next Night, handing pages to whatever rises then. It is all the same act. Some experience it as a sequence because they are still young enough to stand inside time. I am not. I see the whole of the count at once, the way you see the whole of a page."
The faintest tilt of her head. "You will finish with this target. And when you do, you will have your reward, before the next page. That also is already so."
Noah held the sheet of ice, and the ancient eyes of the young king looked up at him out of it.

"Why not target THE Sealed One himself?"Noah’s voice was level. "If the thread runs back to him, cut the root. You hand me a page for the smallest vessel and leave the thing that made the vessel untouched."
For the first time, she looked at him the way a thing looks at something it finds faintly interesting.
"You do not have the capability to fully destroy THE Sealed One," she said.
"No one standing where you stand does. He is protected by many dredges of existence. He is protected by unsavory legacies and things."
The snow fell between them.

"So why would he be your target? Existence does not hand a Dreamer a page he cannot finish. It hands him the page he can. The smallest thread. That... is why the one with The Assimilation Factor is the target. Not because he matters most. Because he is where the knot has a loose end. Pull it. The rest unravels, in time, or it does not."
Noah floated calmly.
She drifted upward into the falling snow, and the pages went with her, and Noah stood alone above the seated dead with a face made of ice in his hand and a clock he could not see already running.
He looked at the young king’s ancient eyes one last time as before him, snow gathered while The Caretaker looked around serenely and said lastly...
"Nature inevitably restores balance. Nature is self-sustaining. What will be...will always be."
<Epigraph- The Legend of The One Who Shone>
In the age before the age, when existence was crowded with the mighty and no one had yet learned to be afraid of being seen, there was a young thing who shone.

He was not entirely the strongest. In that age there were True Infinite Lifeforms whose Infinity had crossed all thresholds, and there were True Source Lifeforms rooted so deep in THE Primordial Source that nothing could unravel them, and there were Primeval Ones who had been old when the frameworks were laid, and there were Descendants of Those Who Remain who carried a sentence in their blood that no lesser thing could speak. The young thing was none of these. He was only bright.
But he was very bright.

He burned so brilliantly that when he stood among the True Infinite and the True Source and the Primeval and the Descendants, all of them ancient, all of them terrible, every eye slid off of them and setled on him.
The very Provenance of Quiet came to him first.

The Provenance of Quiet was old, older than the mighty, and Quiet had watched a great many bright things come and go. Quiet said to him, You are shining. Do you know what shining does? It does not make you strong. It makes you found. Let me sit on you a while, the way I sit on the deep places, and you may live a very long time and no one will ever come to see why.

The young thing laughed at Quiet. He said, I did not join the two fires so that I could hide in the dark like a thing that never joined them. What is the use of being the only lamp if no one sees it lit?
And Quiet, who did not argue, went away.
The Provenance of Brilliance came to him next, and Brilliance did not have to say anything, because Brilliance was already blooming in him, and he loved it, and he let it out.
He shone across Dimensions. He shone across the whole of the age. He shone so brightly that the light of him reached places that were not meant to be reached by anything that small.
And in one of those places, something that had not slept in a very long time opened its eyes.

THE SLEEPLESS FIEND sat in a height that the mighty of that age could not perceive. It had watched True Infinite Lifeforms rise and fall without stirring. It had watched Primeval Ones graze whole Dimensions without stirring. Nothing in that crowded age had ever been strange enough to make it move.
The lamp made it move.

It came down. It came down out of its height and it stood before the young thing who shone, and everything went very still and very quiet, the way Quiet had wanted the young thing to be, and had been refused.
And the Fiend looked at him and wondered...what makes this one different?

What the Fiend found in the young thing who shone was an anomaly, a thing that had never been in existence before and should not have been there then, and that whatever it was, the Fiend did not leave once it had seen it. That had been the starting point for many, many things.
Everything that came after came from that.
Everything.

Every lineage that was burned for standing near his road, and every road that was bent so that it would lead to him. The countless lives that were changed, and the far more countless lives that were ended, across ages the young thing had not yet lived when the Fiend first looked down at him. All of it, they say, hung on one thing.
Someone had shone too brilliantly. And something had come to see why.
The Provenance of Quiet still sits on the deep places as it knows a critical, undeniable lesson.
Sometimes, it is more than all right to be low key.

sentences.text: Noah turned the page of ice over in his hand, and the image of the young king turned with it, and beneath the face, script formed in the frost.
It gave him a place.
It was nowhere near the Cluster where he had last seen the young king.
Adrastia had gone far.
He had crossed out of the split train entirely and sealed himself inside an Elsedimension, a pocket of reality set apart from the ordinary flow of existence.
The script named it only by its shape, a small sealed Elsedimension hung off the edge of a dying Dimension, quiet and hidden and hard to find.
Adrastia was there!
Noah read it twice, and then he looked up at the woman in the frost dress.
"He did nothing wrong."
She did not answer.
She stood in the air above the seated dead with her pages fluttering around her, and she waited like a person waits for a child to finish a sentence they have already decided is foolish.
"I have met him," Noah said.
"I have read him.
Something came to swallow him whole and he did the one thing none of the others managed.
He fought.
He swallowed half of it back.
What is standing in that broken Dimension is not THE Sealed One wearing a body.
It is a being who was attacked, and refused to go quietly, and got left holding half of his attacker inside his own skin for his trouble."
He held the page up.
"That is not a virus.
That is a wound."
"A wound does not stop bleeding," the woman said, "because it was unfairly given."
Her voice was calm!
"The condition does not ask whether a thing chose to become what it is," she went on."It asks only what the thing is.
And what sits inside that Elsedimension is a piece of THE Sealed One, alive, connected, and growing.
A half is still a half.
Do you imagine the plague cares which of its carriers meant no harm?"
"I imagine the plague does not get to write its own justification," Noah said.
"No.
Existence writes it.
You agreed to that a while ago.
You have always agreed."
She plucked another page from the air, looked at it, let it go.
"You said the words.
The dead below you heard them.
Existence heard them.

That was a commitment, and I would counsel you, as one who has kept a great many of them, to understand what you have promised before you begin arguing about which of the promised things you would prefer not to do."
Noah was quiet for a moment.
"Can you be...a bit clearer on this target?"
"The target is not his death,"she said.
Noah’s eyes narrowed.
"You were told to cleanse.
You assumed cleansing meant killing.
What plagues existence inside that Elsedimension is the Assimilation Factor.
The connection.
The living thread that runs from the being called Adrastia back to THE Sealed One, and through which THE Sealed One still reaches, still grows, still uses him whether he knows it or not.
That thread is the virus.
The man is only the host."
"So the goal," Noah said slowly, "is the thread."
"The goal is to eliminate the Assimilation Factor’s connection to THE Sealed One.
Entirely.
There are two ways to do that."
She raised one pale finger.
"You may sever his life completely.
A dead host carries no thread."
A second finger arose.
"Or you may split him from THE Sealed One completely.
Cut the thread and leave the host standing, whole, and his own.
The condition does not care which.
Existence does not care which.
Both cleanse."
Her eyes held his.
"Only you care which.
So choose, and be quick."
Noah looked down at the page, at the young king with the ancient eyes.
There was always a door!
The door opening now...he felt like he could do it.
After all, he held the Provenance for it!
He looked back up at her.
"Who...are you?"
She regarded him for a long moment, and when she answered, her voice had changed!
"I am a caretaker," she said."I am a remnant of the cold.
That is all of what I am, and it is enough."
The pages turned slowly around her.
"When a Night comes, it gathers everything that sat down under it.
Every existence that went hollow.
Every pain that was inflicted and never answered for.
Every wrong that was done in the warm ages and left to rot because no one was cold enough to correct it.
The Night keeps all of it.
It does not forget.
And from all of that, from the boundless pain and the boundless retribution the ages leave behind, something is left over.
A residue.
A thing that stays when the winter passes, to tend what the winter made."
Her cold eyes did not blink.
"That is me.
I am what is left of every Night that came before this one.
I am a collection of pain that was never answered, and a collection of retribution that was never paid.
I am not a lifeform.
I was, once, the way you are now.
I have set that down.
I am the cold’s caretaker, and I hand out its pages, and that is all."
"I am handing you this page.
I have handed you the next page, and the one after.
I am standing in the next Night, handing pages to whatever rises then.
It is all the same act.
Some experience it as a sequence because they are still young enough to stand inside time.
I am not.
I see the whole of the count at once, the way you see the whole of a page."
The faintest tilt of her head.
"You will finish with this target.
And when you do, you will have your reward, before the next page.
That also is already so."
Noah held the sheet of ice, and the ancient eyes of the young king looked up at him out of it.
"Why not target THE Sealed One himself?"Noah’s voice was level.
"If the thread runs back to him, cut the root.
You hand me a page for the smallest vessel and leave the thing that made the vessel untouched."
For the first time, she looked at him the way a thing looks at something it finds faintly interesting.
"You do not have the capability to fully destroy THE Sealed One," she said.
"No one standing where you stand does.
He is protected by many dredges of existence.
He is protected by unsavory legacies and things."
The snow fell between them.
"So why would he be your target?

It hands him the page he can.
The smallest thread.

Not because he matters most.

Pull it.
The rest unravels, in time, or it does not."
Noah floated calmly.

Nature is self-sustaining.
What will be...will always be."

chapters.title: Chapter 5775: Assimilation! I
paragraphs: <THE True Human Emperor>
Drifting back from the cold place was surprisingly easy.

Noah felt the visage of The Caretaker fade, her pages and her frost dress and her cognizant eyes dissolving out of his awareness the way a dream dissolves in the first breath of waking, and then there was only the pull of his own body, far away and frozen, calling him home.
CRACK!
He opened his eyes in the Domain where an Immense One in the shape of an octopus was looking at him.
BOOM!

The frost shattered around his figure. It burst outward in a ring, the ice that had sealed him shearing off in sheets and spining away into the drifting snow, and the rivers of cold that had been pouring into him without pause for however long he had been gone simply stopped.

They hung in the air, arrested, as though the winter had reached the end of what it had to give him and found the vessel already full. And yet he still looked like a block of ice. His body glistened crystalline and white-blue where the frost had fallen away, and when he lifted his hands, they were the hands of a thing carved out of dreaming ice, clear and cold and faintly luminous, and they moved.
Moriarty’s eyes went unfathomably bright behind the small neat spectacles.
"You," the octopus said, "are not dead."
He was not dead!

The words were ridiculous ones, and Noah felt exactly how ridiculous as he sat there in the falling snow and took stock of what had come back with him. His Provenance of THE Human Dreamer had passed six hundred, and it no longer sat quietly inside him the way it had at two hundred, or even at five.

Paired with its seat in his Unique Existential Root of Immensity, it felt like a blinding sun! The very idea of his Provenance swirled around him, a slow gravitational pull that he could feel affecting everything in reach, the snow, the light, the dim Conduits, the attention of the ancient thing watching him.
And he understood, sitting there, why.
Existence leaned toward what was self-made.
That was not a rule he had been taught. It was a thing he could feel now.

Everything borrowed in existence had to be held up by something else, propped and fueled and fed, and the moment the fuel ran out it fell. But a thing that had generated itself from nothing needed no prop, and so existence, which was tired of holding things up, leaned toward it the way water leans toward the lowest ground.
The grander he became, the harder existence leaned. He was no longer a thing that stood in existence. He was a thing existence had started to lean toward!

And now that he had harnessed The Long Night itself, all of it, his Provenance Essence and his Osmontian Tongue and every instrument he had ever used to reach his aims, had been sharpened with an extremely cold edge.
"No," Noah said, and his voice came out steady and a little strange, carrying frost in it."I am not dead. How could I be, when my Dream is only just getting started?"
He let that sit a moment, and then he asked the thing he actually wanted to know, before anything else.

"But I am curious about something. If I am to be outside, wandering across existence, not in here and not in my Existential Root Domain, just how long would it take before an Immense One could sense me and come for me?"

The question was clearly not the one the octopus had expected. Moriarty had the look of a being with a great many questions of his own stacked up and waiting, and this one had cut in ahead of all of them.
But he answered anyway as his shining eyes rested on Noah.

"A newly born Root is like a signal," Moriarty said. "It broadcasts. Some of the greedy ones search for that signal automatically, the way a predator’s ear turns toward a sound before the predator has decided to listen. Once a fresh Root is out in external existence, it might take only a few minutes before something senses it and locks it down. If one of them is already in proximity, seconds."
"You do not need to take that risk. So long as you remain here. And you really should remain here, because..."
His tentacles stilled.
"How is it that you survived taking in rivers of the cold of the Long Night?"
How?
Noah rose from where he had sat.

Ice fell from him as he stood, the last of the frost sloughing off his shoulders and his arms and scattering across the snow, and he clenched his hands, and the crystalline makeup of his body moved with it, slowly gaining more life, more warmth of motion.
"My Dream would not allow me to die. My Root...it simply decided to dream bigger than the death the cold offered."
He rolled his shoulders once, and ice cracked and fell.
"Ah. Anyway. Thank you for the Inscription. I need to acclimate to what has changed in me. Is there a mountain here, or an abode of some kind, that I can call my own while I do?"
He asked it casually. He knew the Immense One before him wanted to ask a great many more questions than that. He was not feeling especially sharing.
Because even this one had secrets.

Noah had not been entirely gone, in his state of freezing death. Some part of him had still been here, and it had caught a few words of a conversation, spoken over his frozen body between Sir Moriarty and something else, something with a voice like a verdant weight.

The conversation had been about him. About what he was. And a being that discussed a frozen guest with an unseen third party, in words the guest was not meant to hear, was a being that was not revealing everything, however warm its spectacles.
So Noah looked at him calmly, and gave him nothing, and Moriarty looked back.
And then the terrifying lifeform smiled, brilliantly and he clapped his tentacles together.
HUUM.
A figure stepped into being beside the octopus.

It was humanoid, tall and lean. Its skin held the deep blue-green of a sea seen from beneath, and faint ridges ran along its temples and down the sides of its throat, closed now, like the memory of gills.

Its eyes were large and dark and wet-bright, and a fine webbing showed between the fingers of its hands. It was dressed, incongruously, in a black butler’s suit, immaculate and severe, and over the suit, Noah noticed, it wore a heavy fur-lined cloak pulled close, and beneath the cloak it was shivering. It bowed to Sir Moriarty with the ease of long practise.
"This is a Legacy Keeper," Moriarty said. "Someone who may be considered a servant of this Legacy. There are many like him. Verys."The Keeper straightened.
"Take our young friend here to THE Glacial Elsedimension Mountain and get him settled. The cold does not seem to bother him. After you are settled, Poona or I may call for you soon enough."

Noah looked at the being called Verys, who turned and bowed to him as well, and then waved one webbed hand. A rift tore open in the air before them, a clean seam of light, and the Keeper stepped aside and gestured toward it, politely, the way a good servant gestures a guest through a door.
Noah looked at him, and his sight opened the Keeper up without asking.
|VERYS, LEGACY KEEPER|
|VERITAS: 250. POTENTIA: 250. PONDUS: 250. PROVENANCE: 0.|
Two hundred and fifty across the board, and not a single point of Provenance!
Two hundred and fifty of strength, and it could not keep him warm.
Noah felt no contempt for the Keeper, who had bowed to him correctly and would open a door for him without complaint.
It was only the ground sloping, the way it sloped for everything. Existence leaned toward what was made. It did not lean toward what was given, however much was given.
He nodded once to Sir Moriarty.
Then he stepped through the rift.
And at the same time, as his crystalline body passed into the seam of light, he did another thing.
He began extending his existence outward.

It was slightly dangerous. He knew exactly how dangerous, because the octopus had just told him, minutes, seconds if something was close. But his Provenance was a grand one, grand enough that it had very nearly hidden from the eyes of Immense Ones even before he formed his Root, and he sent it out now, carefully, quietly, out of the Legacy and across external existence, toward a small sealed Elsedimension hung off the edge of a dying Dimension.
Toward the place where Adrastia was!

He would dream his Infinite Dream again. He would never let himself be in any one place for more than a few minutes. He would move, and move again, so that even if some greedy thing out in the dark caught the signal of his Root, there would be nothing left where it looked for anything to lock onto.
The rift closed behind him, and the Glacial Mountain rose ahead, and he began to dream an endless dream!

chapters.title: Chapter 5776: Assimilation! II
paragraphs: <Achilles Adrastia>
Existence was a unique thing.

It held everything, and it held it strangely, and no two pieces of it were quite alike. But there was a thing more unique than existence itself, and Achilles had built his whole life on it. The capability to assimilate it. To take a piece of existence into yourself, whatever it was, whoever it had belonged to, and make it a part of what you were.

He had assimilated a great many things across his life. Powers, weavings, authorities, the cores of enemies and the gifts of friends, whole systems of existence swallowed and woven into his own. Most of it had settled. Some of it had fought. None of it had ever been as problematic as the monstrous weavings he had assimilated weeks ago, and none of it had ever kept him awake the way those did now.
The trees nearby did not care about any of that.

They grew out of meteorites, here, in this sealed pocket of existence that held no life but his and hers. Tens of thousands of them, stellar trees rooted in drifting stone, their trunks pale and their leaves a vivid pink, streching away through the dark in every direction like an orchard planted across a night sky.

And through all of them whipped the snow. A heavy storm of it, white and endless, driving between the pink-leaved boughs and across the meteorites and through the empty space where no wind should have been, because The Long Night did not need wind to fall.
Achilles leaned against the nearest tree and watched it come down.

He looked young. He always had, a young king’s face, handsome and composed. But his eyes had long since stopped matching it. They were old eyes, aged past the youth that held them, and lately they had gotten older still.

He wore a multicolored coat pulled close against the cold, layers of shifting hue woven from a dozen assimilated authorities, and he was not alone. Rose leaned against his shoulder with her arms wrapped around it, her green hair blowing in the storm, her own coat as many-colored as his, and the two of them watched the pink leaves and the falling snow together in a place where nothing else lived.
"What exactly will you do, Little Fatty?"
Rose asked quietly, without looking away from the storm.
"We have not come across any problem we could not overcome. Not one, in all this time. But this one..." She tightened her arms around his shoulder. "This one feels neverending."
Neverending!
That was the word for it, if there was a word. That was what it was to assimilate a portion of THE Sealed One.

Every time Achilles thought he was peeling back the layers of possibility, getting closer to autonomy, closer to a self that was fully and finally his own, he found only more layers underneath. HUUM!
His existence pulsed.

It tore like a page!

Achilles felt his existence churn. A profound oppression settled over the orchard, a pressure that was not aimed at him and did not need to be. His instinct, which measured everything as a thing to be taken, looked at this lifeform and found nothing it could take. That had never happened before. Not once!
Then he looked closer, and closer, and past the boundless Infinity and Immensity that seemed to fill the lifeform’s eyes, he recognized the face.
Was this not...THE Osmontian? Noah Osmont?!

He knew that face. He had crossed paths with this anomaly a few times and each time, Achilles had reached out with the sense that measured all things and found that he could not find the bottom of this one!
So why had he appeared here? Now?

"Hello," he said. "To what do we owe the pleasure of your appearance here today?"
The lifeform looked at him.
The pressure did not lift. If anything it settled deeper and when the lifeform spoke, its voice boomed out across the orchard.
"Adrastia," it said. "THE Ninth Adrastia Emperor King, is it?"
The hanging snow did not move!
"I have come for your Existence."
Achilles’s expression went heavy and defiant in the same instant, and beside him Rose flared.
Verdant flames spilled out of her, green and bright against the blue gold of the changed trees, and her body began to drink the authority around it, assimilating the surrounding weavings!

She did not step back and she did not flinch from the pressure that had stopped the snow. She looked at the monster across the orchard with the same defiance in her face that was in his, undaunted by his authority, and her flames climbed higher!

chapters.title: Chapter 5777: Assimilation! III
paragraphs: <Achilles Adrastia>
Achilles had spent a long life learning when not to move, and this was one of those times.

Of course, standing still was easier said than done. Rose’s flames were climbing beside him, and the pressure of the thing in the torn light had settled over the orchard and every instinct he owned was telling him that a man who did not act was a man who got acted upon!
But he held his ground.
"You and I have had no negative dealings," he said. "One of the last times I was near you, you came down with THE Creature to attack another Vessel of THE Sealed One. Not me."
He kept his voice level. "So before I do everything I can for my survival, can you at least tell me why?"
Why, indeed.

Why now, and why here, in a sealed pocket of existence that no one should have been able to find? Why him, of all the scattered pieces of THE Sealed One drifting through existence like seeds? Had he done something, some careless thing weeks ago, that had marked him as the first to be gathered? Or had he simply been the easiest to reach? Achilles did not know!

In fact, the lifeform did not answer him at all. Not the question he had asked, at any rate. It drifted closer across the changed orchard, the blue gold spreading through the trees ahead of it, and when it finally spoke it seemed to be picking up a different conversation entirely, one that had begun without him.
"Was that the time you assimilated the weavings of THE Sealed One?" Osmont said, almost idly. "Perhaps I should have been more thorough back then, and none of this would have happened. Oh well."
"When I say I am here for your Existence, I mean it. I am here to ensure your Assimilation Factor is never grasped by THE Sealed One. Consider me... your savior."
WAA!
Achilles had barely finished hearing the word when the anomaly’s hand rose and came down toward them.

He did not think about it! The light of dozens of assimilated Prime Causes and First Causes poured out of him at once, and assimilated Primordial Source surged up dark beneath it, and assimilated Infinity rose over all of it, and around himself and Rose he threw up a bubble of every color he had ever swallowed, seething and bright, a wall made of a lifetime of taking.
And yet nothing struck it!

The bubble held and seethed and waited, and no blow came against it. Instead, the orchard simply went away. The blue gold trees and the hanging snow washed out like paint under water, and in their place there were seas, golden and dreaming and slow, rolling out to every horizon under heavy golden clouds. Compared to the hand that had come down, it was almost gentle. Compared to anything Achilles had ever seen an enemy do, it was far more frightening.

Savior, the anomaly had said. Was that actually what this was? Had a being that stopped snow with its arrival truly come all this way to help a man it barely knew? Achilles wanted to believe it, but..
What he could not dismiss, though, was the authority.
It wrapped around everything now, this golden dreaming light, and it was unlike any weaving he had ever taken into himself or ever failed to. His existence seethed at the nearness of it!
The oldest instinct he owned, the one that had built him from a hungry man into a king, whispered the way it always whispered, that he should take it, assimilate it, now, before it was gone!
And in the very same breath he understood that he could not.
But even that was not the truly unsettling part.

The truly unsettling part was that, just by standing near this authority, he had begun to think about his goals. His dreams. He had not asked to. He had not wanted to, not here, not in the middle of a standoff with something that could end him.
And yet the thoughts came anyway. What kind of authority did that to a person? What kind of power made a being remember what it wanted, simply by being close?
Since he could not measure the thing itself, he did what he had always done. He measured the one who trusted it.
"Taylor of the Light always carried the highest belief and confidence in you," Achilles said. "I will use her character as the basis of trust, since I have nothing else to use."

He lowered the bubble by a fraction, and only a fraction. "So. If you truly came to help, what is it you think you will be able to do? I am irreversibly bonded to THE Sealed One. I assimilated a portion of his weavings of existence, and my Assimilation is absolute. It does not take a thing partway. I am that part of THE Sealed One now, and at the same time I am not him, and there is no line between those two facts that I have ever managed to find."

He held the anomaly’s gaze."It is not a matter of separating two existences. It is a matter of cutting apart a single one. If you can help with that, then by all means, go ahead. I am only unsure that it can be done."
In truth, he had turned the problem over ten thousand ways. Every angle of Assimilation he knew, every trick a lifetime of taking had taught him, and not one of them ended with him still standing.
So perhaps it was not so strange that he would take the help of a monstrous lifeform as readily as any other, if the help was real. He had a family to think about, after all. He had Rose.

And he had made himself a promise, in the long nights since the weavings settled into him, that on every morning still to come, however cold and however cruel, she would wake beside his face. His own face. Not the face of an ancient monster wearing whatever was left of him.
So he raised a hand and pushed her gently back.
"Stay behind me."
"Fatty..."She caught his sleeve befofe she let go, though her flames did not lower, and Achilles stepped forward out of the bubble to stand before the titanic figure alone.
Up close, he could feel what it emanated, and he found that he knew it. Provenance Essence. He knew the shape of that authority from the memories of THE Sealed One that lived inside him now.
Achilles had not thought Osmont had come this far. So maybe, he told himself. Maybe there was a chance.
The anomaly looked him over, up and down. Then he nodded, once.
"Are you human?" Osmont said. "Do you dream?"
Achilles blinked.
Of all the things he had braced himself to hear, that had not been among them. Was it a test? A riddle?
"I was very much born human,"he said slowly. "And of course I have dreams. Everyone has dreams."
The anomaly’s reply came grand and quiet.
"Then I will simply be making a dream come true," he said. "Open your existence to me. Let me see."
His dream.
Behind him, Rose’s expression had gone heavy. He thought about his Dream, since he had been asked to, and found that he did not have to look far.

His Dream was Rose. His Dream was his children. His Dream, if he was honest, had always been existence itself. He had wanted, from the very beginning, to assimilate every aspect of existence there was, to take all of it into himself until nothing anywhere could shake him, until he stood on a foundation made of everything. He had wanted to assimilate everything!

And was that not still true? Had the weavings of THE Sealed One changed what he wanted, or only what he feared? When he looked at it plainly, the wanting was exactly where he had left it. He could assimilate everything.

That was his Dream, and of course he wanted to reach it. And if this anomaly, this being that stopped snow and turned trees to gold and made him remember what he wanted simply by standing near him, could actually put him back on the road toward it, then perhaps the price of finding out was one he could afford.
Achilles was decisive, as he had always been.

He sat down where he stood, on the golden dreaming sea, in a meditative position, and as he settled his body changed. The young king’s flesh gave way to what lay beneath it, a crystalline figure shifting through every color at once, every authority he had ever swallowed visible now in the facets of him.A man made, quite literally, of everything he had taken.
He opened his eyes and looked up at the titan before him.
Neither of them said a word. The one standing reached out, and a frosty crystalline hand came down and rested, lightly, on the crown of his head.
|You have opened the weavings of your existence to THE HUMAN DREAMER.|
|A terrifying Provenance has begun to permeate across your existence.|
|Your existential genome is being studied.|
|Your Dream is being studied.|
A heavy Immensity spread through the whole of him, and Achilles steeled himself against it, and held!
Then the cold authority began to move. It moved through his existence and it found, in a matter of moments, the seam he had spent ten thousand attempts failing to find.

Achilles felt his existence stop. Had it truly been there all along, that close, that simple, and he had never once been able to see it? Or was it only there now, because a hand grander than his own had come looking?
He did not have time to decide. The authority had found what it was looking for, and it began, without any ceremony at all, to cleave!
It cleaved!

chapters.title: Chapter 5778: I Am Me!
paragraphs: <THE True Human Emperor>
Noah’s hand rested on the crown of the crystalline king’s head, and beneath it, he marveled.

He had expected the lifeform to be unique. The Caretaker had said as much. But expecting a thing and holding it under your palm were not the same, and what he held now was stranger than anything he had braced for.

Achilles Adrastia had not devoured the facets of existence he carried. This existence was a chameleon. It did not eat what it assimilated. It became it, seamlessly, so that the Prime Causes and the First Causes and the Primordial Source and the Infinity inside him were not swallowed things siting in a stomach. They were him. Every one of them, as native to his weavings as his own name!
And that, Noah understood, was exactly why he should have died weeks ago.

Because a chameleon that becomes what it touches has no defense against touching something too large to become. He had assimilated the weavings of THE Sealed One, and by every law of his own nature he should simply have become THE Sealed One, the way water poured into a larger vessel takes that vessel’s shape.
THE Sealed One was far too complex, far too vast, far too old for a single existence to become and remain itself. And yet Achilles had held on!

He had become a piece of the ancient monster and, by some stubbornness Noah could feel humming in the crystal under his hand, refused to finish becoming it. He had stopped halfway, and lived there, in a place no assimilator should have been able to survive.
So the task was not to pull two things apart. It was to find, inside a single existence, the line between what was the king and what was the monster, and cut along it without cutting the king.
Fortunately, Noah had been made for exactly this kind of work.

He had two Provenances, and they had never before been asked to do one thing together. THE Provenance of THE Human Dreamer had become terrifying in the manipulation of dreams since his Root formed, terrifying in a way he was still learning the edges of.

And THE Provenance of THE Immense Sovereign, could reach into the genome of existence itself and alter it, excise it, edit what a thing was at the level of its deepest weaving. One of them could see. The other could cut. So he set them to their tasks!

The Dreamer’s Provenance went in first, and it did not go looking for THE Sealed One. A being’s existential genome was a tangle beyond reading, and the monster’s weavings were threaded through every strand of it.

So Noah followed the Dream! He let his Provenance sink down along the shape of what Achilles wanted, and every strand of the genome that answered to that wanting, that pulled toward Rose and the children and the hunger to become everything, lit up gold in his sight. And every strand that did not, every thread that pulled instead toward sealing and collecting and finishing and owning, stayed dark.

There was the line! Not a seam Achilles had failed to find, but a seam that could only be seen by a thing that read Dreams, because the Dream was the one part of a man an ancient monster could not counterfeit!
Then the Immense Sovereign’s Provenance came down like a knife along the line.
It was cold work, and it was fine work, the cutting of a single existence into what it was and what it had been made to carry!

The dark strands parted. The gold ones held. The Assimilation Factor, the living thread that ran from this crystalline king back through the deep to THE Sealed One, came free under the edge of his Provenance and was severed, cleanly, completely!
The golden storm of Provenance Essence roared around the two of them, and Achilles Adrastia opened his eyes.
He did not move at first. He sat in his crystalline form in the middle of the storm and simply listened.
"It’s... quiet," Achilles said.
His voice was hoarse with astonishment.

"I don’t hear the buzzing. There was always a buzzing. An old horror, incessant, at the back of everything, every moment since I took him in."He turned his head slowly, as though the silence might be hiding somewhere. "It’s gone. I can’t hear it at all..."
Noah nodded, and reached to withdraw his hand, and was about to finish the work when something caught his sight.
Oh?

The excision had cut the thread. It had not cut the memories. Those had been assimilated, made native, become Achilles the way everything he took became Achilles, and so they had stayed on the king’s side of the line, and now they lay open under Noah’s palm like pages in a book he had not meant to read.

They were hazy. Rough. Half-ruined by the cutting, almost unrecoverable. But he could see enough of them to know what they were about, and what they were about made him look at the crystalline figure under his hand a second time.
Immense Ones. And a Legacy!

Memories THE Sealed One himself had carried, of dealings with Immense Ones, and of a Legacy, a structure of the kind Lucy had built, though whether it was hers or another’s the ruin of the memory would not say!

He let the hand on Achilles’s head rest a moment longer. "And I could always use an experimental subject."
Achilles’s crystalline eyes rose to his.

"As you elevate your Dimensionality, I learn. You will eventually need to reach the point of forming a Root of Immensity of your own. It is not easy. It does not begin where you might think. It begins with your own Chorionic Gonadotropin, the signal of your own becoming, and you have a unique Factor of Assimilation, which means you could very possibly form a unique kind of Assimilation Chorionic Gonadotropin, with my help."
He glanced, briefly, at nothing, at a clock only he could feel running. "But I am out of time here, and I will have to change scenery to experiment with you further. Do you want to try?"

He asked it calmly. But the man beneath his hand was smiling now, brilliantly, the smile of someone who has just been handed back his own existence and offered a road on top of it, and Achilles reached out with his senses.
"Thank you," Achilles said. "And yes. Just give me one second..."
The golden storm faded!

The dreaming seas rolled away, and the heavy clouds thinned, and the two of them stood once more in the sealed Elsedimension among the blue gold trees and the hanging snow, exactly where they had left it. And Achilles Adrastia stood up.

He was flesh again, the young king’s face and the ancient eyes, though the eyes seemed younger now by a great deal. He turned. He looked at the beautiful green-haired woman standing behind him with her flames burned down to embers and her face heavy, and he crossed the distance to her in three strides and pulled her against him and held her so tightly that Noah, watching, thought he might crack her.
Then he kissed her. Then he laughed, out loud, the laugh of a man who has been holding his breath for weeks.
"I am me," Achilles said into her hair. "All me!"
"Really?" Rose pulled back to look at his face, her hands on either side of it, searching. "Really?!"
"All me."

She made a sound that was half a laugh and half something else, and then she was kissing him, and he was kissing her, and the embrace between them went from relief to something a good deal warmer with a speed that suggested the two of them had forgotten, entirely, that they were not alone.
Noah, being human, allowed them a moment. He had a family too. He knew what it was to hold someone and find them still themselves.
Prompts bloomed across his sight while he waited.
|You have interfered in, and steered, a grand unfolding Dream.|
|Your Provenance increases by 25.|
|The gaze of an unfathomable existence is seeking to understand how one of its grandest tools was just separated from it.|
Noah looked at that last line, and raised his brows.
Then he looked at the two embracing lifeforms before him, who showed no sign at all of stopping.
"Time’s up,"he said. "Let’s go."
His Provenance blared!

It flooded out of him and took the orchard, the king, the woman, the whole of the small sealed space, and drew it into his Dream, and he took Achilles Adrastia and Rose out of the Elsedimension where they had hidden and carried them, in a single beat of his Root, toward another.

One with far heavier security. One where a part of him already stood among broken clocks and numbered meteorites, in a Dimension that had come apart from time itself. Atlas’s Elsedimension of shattered hours!
HUUM!
They were gone.

The orchard stood empty. And slowly, the way a held breath lets go, the blue gold drained back out of the trees, and the leaves returned to their vivid pink, and the snow that had hung motionless in the air remembered that it was falling, and fell.
For a few moments the Elsedimension was only an orchard on drifting stone again, with no one in it.
Then, moments later...
BOOM!
The sky tore open!

Not a page this time. Eyes! Multiple massive eyes forced their way open across the heights of the sealed Elsedimension, one after another, gazes the size of Dimensions blinking into being where no gaze should have been able to reach, and the pink trees bent under the weight of being looked at.
|THE SLEEPLESS FIEND casts his gaze across the orchard, and is displeased.|
|"A Root was just here. The scent of it is still on the trees."|
|THE UNPAID COLLECTOR’s gaze narrows.|
|"The same one. The one that slipped us in the frozen forest."|
|THE GLOATING JAILER is puzzled.|
|"How did it sense our coming so quickly? We had not even finished arriving."|
|THE SLEEPLESS FIEND does not answer the Jailer. His gaze turns downward, toward the orchard floor.|
|"And you. You were the one who alerted us to this place. You said a project of yours was taken away here."|
The words fell into the orchard from the sky, and below, existence opened.

Infinity spilled out of the air between the pink trees, and THE Primordial Source spilled with it, the two of them pouring open together the way no two authorities in existence were supposed to be able to pour, and out of the joined flood stepped a humanoid figure.
He was young, and he was ancient, and the two facts sat on him without quarreling. Tall, and lean, and pale as a thing that had never once needed the sun.
Long hair fell past his shoulders, pale gold shading toward white, and his face was cut fine and cold and aristocratic, every line of it composed.

His eyes were gold. Not warm gold. The gold of a thing found at the bottom of a very deep place. He wore a long dark coat that hung to his boots, severe and old-fashioned and immaculate, and he stood among the pink trees as though he had stood in a thousand such places and found them all equally beneath him.
It was THE Sealed One!
And it was not a vessel.
This was not a puppet. This was the genuine article, the hand behind every vessel! and his existence pulsed, slow and heavy and unfathomable, with a Root!

A Root of Immensity, seated in him, growing, and so dense that the snow could not get near him. It fell all around him and stopped, a hand’s breadth from his coat, and drifted away, as though the winter itself had decided he was not a thing it cared to touch!
He looked around the orchard coldly, at the pink trees, at the drifting stone.
"A Unique Existential Factor of Assimilation,"THE Sealed One said, "that would have made for a unique Aspect of my growing Root. Taken. It is a great shame."
He turned one pale hand over, as though weighing the loss in his palm. "Though I believe I may know who is responsible."
He raised both hands then, pale and long-fingered, into the air around him, and breathed in.
"I can smell his arrogance, tyranny, ans brilliance," he said. "And his Infinity. I know that Infinity. It is my greatest loss across the whole of existence, so far."
His gold eyes lifted to the massive gazes hanging in the sky. "The culprit should be a lifeform known as Noah Osmont."

chapters.title: Chapter 5779: Time! I
paragraphs: In the age before ages were counted, there was a Lineage that did not know what an hour was.
They were a Provenance Lineage. The First one among them had generated her own origin out of the dark.

They lived in a valley at the bottom of existence where nothing had yet been measured. They did not count their days, because no one had told them days could be counted. They only lived them, one after another.
And through that valley, though none of them could see it, there ran a river.

Time ran through the valley. It ran through everything, in that age as in every age, and it was the one thing in all of existence that every being received in exactly equal measure and no being ever kept.

The Lineage stood in it up to their necks and did not know it was there. They aged in it. They loved in it. They died in it, and were carried off downstream, and the ones left standing wept and did not know what had carried their dead away.
Of that Lineage there was a daughter who noticed the river.

She was not the strongest of them, nor the wisest. But she was the one who stood at the bank one evening and watched her mother be carried off, and asked the question none of the others had thought to ask.
What is this thing that takes us? And where does it go?
So she went looking for it!
She walked out of the valley, which no one of her Lineage had done, and she walked a very long way, and at the end of the walking she found The Provenance of Time.

The Provenance of Time was sitting on a stone. Time was not old, and Time was not young. Time had the face of everything that had ever happened and the eyes of everything that had not happened yet, and it was not doing anything at all, because Time does not do things. Time only...passes.
The daughter said to it, You take my people. I have watched you carry them off. I have come to ask you to stop.

The Provenance of Time said, I do not take. I do not give. I am the only thing in existence that every one of you receives equally and none of you keeps. Your people are not carried off by me. They are carried off in me.
The daughter did not accept this. She was of a Lineage that came from nothing, and such beings do not accept.

She said, My First mother generated her own origin. She owed nothing to any framework. Why then must I stand in your river like a fish? Why must I receive you as everyone receives you? I will make my own. I will generate a Time that is mine, the way she generated an origin that was hers, and then you will not carry me anywhere I do not choose to go.
And Time, who had heard this before, and would hear it again, said only, You may. It has been done. But understand what it costs, for I will not tell you twice.
The daughter did not ask what it cost. She did not ask!

She went back to her valley, and she sat down at the bank of the river she could now see, and she began to generate. It took her an age, though she did not count it, because she still did not count. She reached into the self-made fire her Lineage carried and she made, out of nothing, a Time that was hers.

Her own Provenance of Time. Not the common river that ran through everything, but a private current, originatng in her and answering to no one, which she could slow, and hasten, and stand outside of, and which would never carry her anywhere she did not choose to be carried.
And the day it was finished, she became Immense!

She stepped out of the river. That is all it took, in the end, once the current of her own was made. She stepped up onto the bank, out of the common Time that ran through everything, and stood in her own, and looked back down at the valley of her Lineage from a place where no hour could reach her.

She saw her people aging. She had not aged. She saw her sisters grow old and be carried off downstream, and she stood on the bank and could not reach them, because her hand was in one Time and theirs were in another, and a hand cannot cross that.

She saw her children, and her children’s children, live whole lives between one of her breaths and the next. She called to them, and her voice arrived in the valley a generation late, or a generation early, so that they heard a stranger shouting from a bank they could not see.
And in time, which was still running for them though it had stopped for her, her Lineage forgot her. Just like how a river forgets a stone it no longer touches.

They told stories about a daughter who had gone looking for the thing that took their dead and had never come back, and the stories were true, and she stood twenty paces from the storytellers and could not make them hear her.

That is the Provenance of Time. It is one of the grandest Provenances there is, because it is the only one that lets a being stand outside the river every other being drowns in. And it is the grimmest, because the river is where everyone you love is standing, and to leave it is to leave them, and a being with its own Time is the loneliest thing in all of existence!
Time had told her. It had said, understand what it costs. She had not asked.

Some say she still stands on the bank above a valley that no longer exists, watching a river with no one in it. Some say she learned to step back down into the common current for a moment at a time, to hold a hand that would slip from hers a heartbeat later, and that this was worse.

And some say that every Immense One who has ever stood outside an hour is that same daughter, learning the same lesson, in a different valley, and that Those Who Remain are only the ones who never once stepped back down!
Time was always a dangerous thing to play with.
<THE True Human Emperor>
Noah stood in three places at once, and none of them was safe.

The first was the Legacy of THE Acharya of Immensity, where his body sat under Verys’s care on the Glacial Mountain. The second was THE Chrysalis of THE First Sundering, where a part of him hunted Rare Gu and never stopped moving. The third was here, at the peak of a violet tree that stretched away for light years, in a Dimension that had come apart from time.
The gazes of the Immense Ones did not reach well into these last two. Their Ruling of Existence still let them watch a great many things. But it did not let them watch everything.
At this time.
The air tore beside him!
Achilles and Rose stepped out of it onto a branch.
The ring on Noah’s finger buzzed.
Atlas rose out of it, an old man made of light, and the billowing snow of the Long Night passed straight through his illusory chest without slowing. He looked at the two newcomers, and then at Noah.
"We were close," Atlas said. "We were this close to sniffing out where my old Workshop is. Why bring newcomers now?"
He nodded at them. "Who are they?"

"Somewhat unique lifeforms,"Noah said. "They were connected to THE Sealed One. I severed that connection seconds ago. And that old one, it turns out, is connected to a great many Immense Ones. Some of them are likely among those who killed you all those years ago."
Atlas blinked.
He looked Achilles up and down, slowly, like a craftsman looking at a tool he did not make and cannot yet place.
"Connected how?" he said.
"I don’t know yet. The memories are half-ruined. But there were Immense Ones in them. And a Legacy."
Achilles rose from where he had crouched. His eyes were shining!
"I am Adrastia," he said."I am thankful for what Osmont did to help me. And it seems he is not done doing so."
He looked at the old man of light as he asked Noah. "You mentioned... a Root of Immensity?"
Atlas glanced at Noah. Noah inclined his head as he nodded.
"I want to try inducing the formation of a Root of Immensity in others. I am doing it now. Here, with him, and at my home. Different subjects, the same work, at the same time."
Atlas tilted his illusory head.
"A Root is generated," he said. "It is not given. That is the whole meaning of the word. So how would you induce anything?"
Noah looked out over the light years of violet branches, and when he answered, his voice had the flat calm of a man describing something he could see from a great height.

"I am a space the house of existence was built in," he said. "When I stand near an existence, that existence begins to remember what it dreams. I do not hand anything my Root. I show their existence the shape of beginning, and whether it begins is their own weaving. Well, in theory. I could act to induce something made from his own signal of becoming. His own Chorionic Gonadotropin."
Atlas was silent for a while. The snow went through him. Noah turned to Achilles.

"Your Assimilation Factor. The thing THE Sealed One wanted from you. He wanted it because it is the only one of its kind. You do not devour what you take. You become it. Achilles’s crystalline eyes did not leave him as he grasped all these possibilities!
"That has no precedent, I believe." Atlas said.
"Nothing I have done these past days has precedent," Noah said.
He looked at the three of them, the old man of light and the chameleon of a king and the silent woman, and he spoke more of his existence.

"Existence is not static for me anymore. It is dynamic. I can see the equation of it turning, and I can see that most of the walls in it are only places no one has pushed. A great many things are possible now that were not possible a week ago. Just because a thing seems impossible does not mean it will remain so."

He looked at Atlas. "My Provenance is that of a Dreamer. I dream a thing, and existence adjusts to agree. So I will ask you the only question that matters. Why can I not dream impossibilities into existence?"
Atlas did not answer at once.
He looked at Noah for a long moment! He crossed his illusory arms.

The dozen turned around!
Twelve pairs of eyes found the four of them at once!
They were foreign Provenance Lifeforms, all twelve.
Rose’s flames lit green at her fingertips and stayed there, low. Achilles moved half a step in front of her without seeming to decide to.

sentences.text: In the age before ages were counted, there was a Lineage that did not know what an hour was.
They were a Provenance Lineage.
The First one among them had generated her own origin out of the dark.
They lived in a valley at the bottom of existence where nothing had yet been measured.
They did not count their days, because no one had told them days could be counted.
They only lived them, one after another.
And through that valley, though none of them could see it, there ran a river.
Time ran through the valley.
It ran through everything, in that age as in every age, and it was the one thing in all of existence that every being received in exactly equal measure and no being ever kept.
The Lineage stood in it up to their necks and did not know it was there.
They aged in it.
They loved in it.
They died in it, and were carried off downstream, and the ones left standing wept and did not know what had carried their dead away.
Of that Lineage there was a daughter who noticed the river.
She was not the strongest of them, nor the wisest.
But she was the one who stood at the bank one evening and watched her mother be carried off, and asked the question none of the others had thought to ask.
What is this thing that takes us?
And where does it go?
So she went looking for it!
She walked out of the valley, which no one of her Lineage had done, and she walked a very long way, and at the end of the walking she found The Provenance of Time.
The Provenance of Time was sitting on a stone.
Time was not old, and Time was not young.
Time had the face of everything that had ever happened and the eyes of everything that had not happened yet, and it was not doing anything at all, because Time does not do things.
Time only...passes.
The daughter said to it, You take my people.
I have watched you carry them off.
I have come to ask you to stop.
The Provenance of Time said, I do not take.
I do not give.
I am the only thing in existence that every one of you receives equally and none of you keeps.
Your people are not carried off by me.
They are carried off in me.
The daughter did not accept this.
She was of a Lineage that came from nothing, and such beings do not accept.
She said, My First mother generated her own origin.
She owed nothing to any framework.
Why then must I stand in your river like a fish?
Why must I receive you as everyone receives you?
I will make my own.
I will generate a Time that is mine, the way she generated an origin that was hers, and then you will not carry me anywhere I do not choose to go.
And Time, who had heard this before, and would hear it again, said only, You may.
It has been done.
But understand what it costs, for I will not tell you twice.
The daughter did not ask what it cost.
She did not ask!
She went back to her valley, and she sat down at the bank of the river she could now see, and she began to generate.
It took her an age, though she did not count it, because she still did not count.
She reached into the self-made fire her Lineage carried and she made, out of nothing, a Time that was hers.
Her own Provenance of Time.

Not the common river that ran through everything, but a private current, originatng in her and answering to no one, which she could slow, and hasten, and stand outside of, and which would never carry her anywhere she did not choose to be carried.
And the day it was finished, she became Immense!
She stepped out of the river.
That is all it took, in the end, once the current of her own was made.
She stepped up onto the bank, out of the common Time that ran through everything, and stood in her own, and looked back down at the valley of her Lineage from a place where no hour could reach her.
She saw her people aging.
She had not aged.

She saw her sisters grow old and be carried off downstream, and she stood on the bank and could not reach them, because her hand was in one Time and theirs were in another, and a hand cannot cross that.
She saw her children, and her children’s children, live whole lives between one of her breaths and the next.
She called to them, and her voice arrived in the valley a generation late, or a generation early, so that they heard a stranger shouting from a bank they could not see.
And in time, which was still running for them though it had stopped for her, her Lineage forgot her.
Just like how a river forgets a stone it no longer touches.

They told stories about a daughter who had gone looking for the thing that took their dead and had never come back, and the stories were true, and she stood twenty paces from the storytellers and could not make them hear her.
That is the Provenance of Time.
It is one of the grandest Provenances there is, because it is the only one that lets a being stand outside the river every other being drowns in.
And it is the grimmest, because the river is where everyone you love is standing, and to leave it is to leave them, and a being with its own Time is the loneliest thing in all of existence!
Time had told her.
It had said, understand what it costs.
She had not asked.
Some say she still stands on the bank above a valley that no longer exists, watching a river with no one in it.
Some say she learned to step back down into the common current for a moment at a time, to hold a hand that would slip from hers a heartbeat later, and that this was worse.

And some say that every Immense One who has ever stood outside an hour is that same daughter, learning the same lesson, in a different valley, and that Those Who Remain are only the ones who never once stepped back down!
Time was always a dangerous thing to play with.

Noah stood in three places at once, and none of them was safe.
The first was the Legacy of THE Acharya of Immensity, where his body sat under Verys’s care on the Glacial Mountain.
The second was THE Chrysalis of THE First Sundering, where a part of him hunted Rare Gu and never stopped moving.
The third was here, at the peak of a violet tree that stretched away for light years, in a Dimension that had come apart from time.
The gazes of the Immense Ones did not reach well into these last two.
Their Ruling of Existence still let them watch a great many things.

At this time.
The air tore beside him!
Achilles and Rose stepped out of it onto a branch.
The ring on Noah’s finger buzzed.

Some of them are likely among those who killed you all those years ago."

And a Legacy."
